More than 200 migrants crossed the Channel in a single dinghy for the first time on Monday morning – a clear demonstration of the trend by people-smugglers to cram growing numbers of people onto the flimsy vessels.

With French authorities better resourced than ever before, people-smugglers in northern France are turning to larger vessels to pick up migrants off shore, where immigration officers find it harder to intervene.

Launches are also taking place further afield, and some even in Belgium, as criminals seek to evade French authorities.

The trend to larger vessels has been happening over recent years, but the last few months have seen record-breaking numbers of people crammed onto the dinghies.

In mid-July, a new record was set with 128 individuals on one single boat, breaking the previous record of 125 in September 2025.

This was quickly overtaken on 24 July when 165 migrants reached the UK on a “mega-dinghy” - estimated to be the same size as a standard bus. And now 230 people have been crammed onto one boat arriving on Monday.

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham and minister for Border Security and Asylum Anna Turley stand by a recovered small boat, used by migrants crossing the English Channel ( AFP/Getty )

Downing Street criticised “ruthless” people-smuggling gangs “prepared to risk human lives for profit” on Monday, after news broke of 230 people crossing the Channel on one boat.

Recent reported prices paid to people-smugglers for facilitating the journeys range from £513 per person to £1,350 – meaning one mega-dinghy journey could net criminals more than £300,000.

Small boat arrivals in 2026 have been down compared to the same period in 2025, with some 14,000 people making the journey so far. Data from previous years shows that while the numbers of migrants arriving has been on the rise, this has not meant more boats.

In 2025, 41,472 people arrived on 672 boats, compared to 36,816 people in 695 boats in 2024.

The dangerous numbers of people being put on larger vessels comes with new risks, such as people being crushed under the weight of other passengers. The first known death to have occurred this way, was in 2023 when Wudanese, a 24-year-old Eritrean woman was killed inside a dinghy.

open image in gallery A small boat seized by the NCA in the UK. Dinghies are believed to be produced in China and then sent to Germany for storage and processing. ( NCA )

Greater surveillance on the French beaches and restrictions on purchasing inflatable kayaks has also meant that it is harder to launch independent journeys across the Channel, with the numbers of these crossings dropping in 2024, according to analysis by immigration experts.

This has led migrants, who previously would have attempted solo crossings because they can’t afford to pay smugglers, to rush the dinghies at the last minute in an attempt to squeeze onto the already overcrowded vessels.

open image in gallery Small boats from China seized at Felixstowe port by the National Crime Agency ( NCA )

Police pressure has also led to the emergence of “taxi boats”, which pick up migrants from water just off shore, and are more dangerous than launching dinghies from beaches.

The UK agreed earlier this year to provide £662m to France in a three-year deal to boost the numbers of border force officers patrolling beaches and to fund special riot-trained police.

Small boats are thought to be manufactured in China, along with their accompanying outboard engines. Some are then transported through Turkey to Europe, with recent boats discovered at the border with Bulgaria.

However others have been known to be shipping directly from China to the UK.

Bulgarian customs officers have been working with the UK’s National Crime Agency to track consignments of small boat equipment being shipped through the country.

open image in gallery A deflated dinghy is seen on the quayside in Dover, Kent on Monday 10 August. ( PA Wire )

Boats destined for the Channel have been stopped at the Lesovo border crossing, an entry point into Bulgaria from Turkey.

In June, 20 boats were found in a lorry at the crossing, with the dinghies being shipped to Germany. Germany is a well-known storage location and staging post for the equipment needed by people-smugglers facilitating the Channel crossings, the NCA have said.

In another recent seizure by UK officers, at least 25 inflatable boats and 25 outboard engines were found at the Port of Felixstowe, in a shipment from China.

The rubber boats, which were ten-metres long, were in a shipping container. Although they had been shipped from China to the UK, investigators believe the boats were on their way to Hamburg, Germany to be unloaded.

President Donald Trump spent the weekend insisting that vandals damaged his Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool renovations despite his own administration admitting there wasn’t sufficient evidence, ratcheting up pressure on U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro to reverse course after she dropped related criminal charges.

On Sunday, the president posted an image of court documents on Truth Social, writing that a “highly credible witness” saw David Hearn, a 67-year-old former Olympian, “violently” rip the pool’s newly redone coating.

“The National Park Service employee provided this witness testimony to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in early July,” wrote Trump, making a pointed reference to Pirro’s office, which has argued that park officials failed to turn over relevant information.

The president added that others had done “substantial” harm to the pool but there was “no video or proof” beyond the damage itself.

Hearn has pleaded not guilty and denied any wrongdoing.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has spent days ripping into his hand-picked DC federal prosecutor over her decision to drop criminal charges tied to his disastrous Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool makeover ( AFP/Getty )

One day earlier, the president posted photos showing peeling coating and apparent graffiti, each marked with the word “Vandalism.”

The move follows sharp criticism from the president on Friday, when he publicly urged Pirro to “re-visit her hastily made decision.”

Pirro’s office previously concluded that contractors working on renovation efforts caused the damage rather than criminal actors.

But Trump has repeatedly blamed maintenance issues and declining water quality on alleged sabotage following a controversial project in which he ordered the pool drained and painted with a “American flag blue” liner.

The rift escalated after Pirro moved to drop charges against Hearn, after court filings revealed the administration failed to produce evidence against him and admitted the damage resulted from a botched installation.

Trump publicly unloaded on the prosecutor from the Oval Office. “I was disappointed in Jeanine Pirro. Really disappointed with Jeanine Pirro. She folded like an umbrella,” he told reporters.

The president claimed she “choked” due to pressure from the judge overseeing the case. “Instead of going after the people who did it, he went after her, and went after her department, and I guess she choked. I don’t know what the hell happened,” he said.

Reporters questioned Trump on whether he planned to fire Pirro over the decision, as reported by CNN, prompting him to tell one journalist that “you’re fake news” and “don’t ever talk again.”

Pirro had initially claimed Hearn “woefully destroyed property” in a “deliberate act,” but her office later acknowledged in court documents that the Interior Department provided “less than fulsome information” and that the blue sealant began peeling “almost immediately” due to a rushed process.

open image in gallery Tensions between the White House and top federal prosecutor Jeanine Pirro spilled into public view after she dismissed a felony case against a 67-year-old former Olympian. Trump accused Pirro of having ‘choked’ under judicial pressure, insisting that photos and video prove the landmark was vandalized ( AFP/Getty )

“The Trump administration's case against Davey Hearn should have never been brought,” according to a statement to The Independent from Hearn’s attorneys. “The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology.”

The high-profile refurbishment project — which bypassed standard competitive bidding to award a $14.7 million contract to Atlantic Industrial Coatings LLC — was meant to be finished quickly for $1.5 million ahead of Fourth of July celebrations, according to the president. However, early rain, wind and missed testing deadlines led to rushed work that quickly deteriorated, with algae soon returning to the pool along with peeling paint.

In addition to the photos posted late Saturday, Trump shared a screenshot from X to support his claims of criminal activity.

open image in gallery Trump continues to insist that vandals were responsible for cutting the recently applied lining of the Reflecting Pool despite his own administration appearing to admit that there is no evidence to support his claims ( Getty )

“The material was cut right where the video tape showed, for 300 feet or more. People were on their knees with their hands in the water at the exact location of the ‘slashes,’” Trump wrote. “Additionally, there were witnesses to the VANDALISM, and the flexible areas of the material were cut with a knife.”

Trump had earlier asserted that vandals used a box cutter or knife to create a nearly 300-foot slit in the lining of the pool, while also claiming that fertilizer was poured into the water to trigger rapid algae growth.

“Jeanine Pirro made a mistake. It was vandalism,” Trump said Monday.

“We have photographs or tapes, like moving cameras, right? Where people are on the side cutting it with a box knife,” he added. “Now, I’m not saying I was 100 percent thrilled with the contractor, but the contractor was rushing. We wanted to get it open for July 4th, and we got it done. But, in addition, there was vandalism.”

Bath will play their final two home games of the 2026/27 Prem Rugby season away at an alternative venue as work begins on redeveloping the Rec.

The club secured planning permission in September 2025 for a long-sought expansion of the venue to a capacity of 18,000.

That uplift of 3,500 fans will see new East and West Stands built, with the target completion date for the project brought forward to the start of the 2028/29 season.

The phased development is set to begin during this campaign, with the club forced to play their Prem games against Harlequins and Saracens in round 16 and round 18 to an alternate venue – which would also be expected to host a home play-off match should Bath finish in the top two.

“We are in discussion with alternative host venues and we will update you once the location for these fixtures is confirmed,” said Tarquin McDonald, Bath’s chief executive.

“Our goal is to minimise disruption as far as possible, and we hope that you will all join us and help make these fixtures a proper home away from home.”

Bath have played on the Recreation Ground site since 1894. Johann van Graan’s side were beaten in the semi-finals of the Prem and Champions Cup last season.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Sports.title: Jurgen Klinsmann’s son almost paralysed by horror injury set to keep him out for well over a year
Sports.content:
JURGEN KLINSMANN’S son Jonathan Klinsmann suffered such a horrendous neck injury that he was almost paralysed.

Cesena star Jonathan, 29, suffered an awful clash with Palermo ace Filippo Ranocchia in a Serie B match back in April when his team suffered a 2-0 loss away.



The goalkeeper’s head connected to Ranoccia’s knee and although his scalp was cut and his ears were ringing he still felt this was just another knock.

But once the USA international got back up on his feet he quickly realised it was something far worse.



That didn’t stop him from completing the match, though, with four minutes remaining before full-time but he still had the hindsight to order his centre-backs not to pass him the ball as he stood still.

The Munich-born keeper didn’t know he had fractured his first cervical vertebra and sustained serious neck ligament damage and any movement could have resulted to a career-ending injury – even paralysis.



The ex-LA Galaxy ace quickly found out that his World Cup dreams were shattered and his season was over but doctors moved fast to make sure things wouldn’t get even worse.

Jonathan told The Athletic: “I went to the ground and sat there for a second thinking, ‘Ooof. That kind of hurt’. Then I rolled on my back and felt my neck just really tense up. It was like when you get in a car crash.

“So I figured, ‘Maybe I have concussion and whiplash’. My head was bleeding but I never lost consciousness or felt really dizzy. When I got up and the game restarted, my neck felt even tighter. The muscles were obviously going crazy trying to protect me from something.

“I told my centre-backs to just keep the ball. Then I tried to stand as still as I could. I could barely move my neck, couldn’t look down.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“If they had passed the ball back to me, I couldn’t have looked down to trap it, so the guys just kept the ball around the back until the whistle went. I’m genuinely not sure I would have walked away from that.

“At first, I didn’t fully understand the severity of it. The MRI scans weren’t too great and they said, ‘It’s a fracture in your spine. Your World Cup is probably not going to happen, your season is over’. So they were the first thoughts. I was thinking, ‘OK, let’s get through this’.

“But it was clearly a lot worse than just a fracture. Luckily, before the game ended my team kept the ball and Palermo were winning 2-0, so they didn’t press.

“It’s fortunate. I was really close to a much, much worse scenario if I had done something in those two minutes: like, never playing again, never walking again. So it was bad — but it could have been an unreal amount worse.

“I couldn’t use a pillow in the hospital in Palermo because they wanted to keep my spine as straight as possible. I had the neck brace on from the ambulance, which was a pretty generic brace with very little padding.



“So my pillow was a thick piece of plastic, and the pressure build-up in the back of my head was from the brace then going down into my neck and the injury.”

Jonathan was then set for a “very complicated surgery” that he decided to have in his native Germany.

But Jurgen‘s son, who is following in the Bayern Munich, Inter Milan and Tottenham legend’s footsteps, thankfully pulled through with a successful operation although his return date is not yet concrete.

Jonathan added: “They explained the multiple plans and back-up plans for the surgery, once they had got in there, with all the various contingencies.

“They also explained the risk of the surgery was very high. They have to tell you. The part of signing off on the paperwork and signing off on some major risks that weren’t even in your head before. It’s daunting.



‘Very complicated surgery’

“They were saying, ‘You have to understand, it’s an injury very close to the spinal cord and the C1 that connects everything. It’s almost solely responsible for all your rotation, and it’s a very complicated surgery’.

“Then hearing the numbers about when I might expect to be able to go home, or to walk, or to play again. They were tough.

“The moment of being rolled from my hospital room and passing my family on the way to the operating clinic was… it was just one we had to get through.

“It’s a highly-charged time, but luckily the anaesthetist was pretty funny. He made me laugh and by the time you realise he’s making jokes, you’re already asleep.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The second I opened my eyes, I was just asking how it went. The doctor was asking me how I felt but I just wanted to know if it was a success.



“Everything had been put back where it should be. Then, as I started coming off the heavy pain medication, I felt much better. I started to walk a bit a few days after the surgery.”

Sports.title: Man Utd icon, 41, reveals he needs hip replacement weeks after retiring from football
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester United star Ashley Young needs a hip replacement, just weeks after announcing his retirement from football.

The 41-year-old called time on his 23-year career this summer after a short spell at Ipswich Town, in which the Tractor Boys climbed back up to the Premier League.



Speaking on the High Performance Podcast, Young explained the problems he was having with his hip.

He said: “I went down on my hip in November and had an injection. I have always said to myself: ‘If my body is saying you need injections, there is a problem, you need to think about retiring’.



“Basically I need a hip replacement, in November I was told I would need it in about 10 years time.

“I got to January and was due to have another injection which would have got me through to the end of the season, as I was saying to the specialist ‘I know it is painful, but I want to make sure I do everything I can possibly do to help the team’.

“About a week before I am about to have the injection, I go down on it in training and I am like ‘this is worse, I know it is a lot worse’.”

Young then revealed that a specialist told him his hip had become “much worse”, giving him a two-year window to get it replaced.

He concluded that it came as a result of overuse following his 756-game senior career which spanned from 2003-2026.

The 41-year-old was physically unable to train for three months but was still determined to end his career on a high.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He said: “From January to the end of the season, I literally had two or three months where I couldn’t train it was that painful. I saw the specialist again and said ‘I’m not going out like this’. He said he didn’t want to give me another injection as it would weaken the area.

“I asked him ‘are you telling me I can’t play football again, you can say it if you want, trust me if I get an opportunity to be back on the pitch, I’ll be back on the pitch’.

“The last two months of the season I was training every day and he was like ‘it is not possible, you shouldn’t be training’.”

The ex-England man’s grit and determination saw him train all the way through the crucial end of season run-in, despite not actually getting on the pitch.

He added: “It would have been incredible to come onto the pitch for the last game of the season but for me to train like I did that week and for us to be promoted on the last day of the season, it was fitting.”



Ipswich finished second in the Championship, securing a return to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

It was the final feat of Young’s successful career, which included winning the Premier League, Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup at Man United.

Young also won a Serie A title in 2021 during his spell at Inter Milan.

Sports.title: Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos ‘closing in on stake in Liverpool and deal could be announced THIS WEEK’
Sports.content:
TECH BILLIONAIRE Jeff Bezos is reportedly closing in on a deal to buy a minority stake in Liverpool.

The Amazon founder is part of a consortium that is in talks with Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).



And according to Sky News, a deal could be announced as early as this week.

The investor group is headed up by Amit Bhatia, who was previously a long-term shareholder at Queens Park Rangers.



Bhatia’s father-in-law is Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, with a net worth put at around £23bn.

Eduardo Saverin – who co-founded Facebook alongside Mark Zuckerberg – is also said to be involved in the syndicate.



Saverin was memorably played by Andrew Garfield in the hit movie The Social Network based on the early days of Facebook.

The deal would see Liverpool given additional financial power from some of the wealthiest men on the planet.

Bezos has an estimated net worth of £213BILLION, making him the third-richest person on the planet.

So the news that Bezos, after joining forces with Amit Bhatia’s consortium, is nearing a deal to buy a minority stake in the Anfield side means they could become box-office once again. Sports.title: Arsenal’s pre-season woes are a sign of what’s to come if Declan Rice and Co aren’t back sooner rather than later
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S pre-season struggles are a warning sign for what might happen if their World Cup stars are not back sharpish.

And the Gunners will be desperate to get new £75m signing Bruno Guimaraes ready for action as soon as possible to make things right.



The reigning champions have leaked six goals in two consecutive pre-season defeats as Mikel Arteta battles to manage his bare-bones squad.

Sunday afternoon’s 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium marked the first time since April 2023 that Arsenal conceded three or more goals in consecutive games.



It followed their 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday and will have alarm bells ringing for Arteta with the Community Shield just SIX days away.

Arsenal kick off their campaign proper with a trip to Cardiff this Sunday, taking on Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City in the annual curtain raiser.

City have dispatched teams like Atletico Madrid in pre-season and are already playing with top returning players like Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush.

But Arteta finds himself without a host of top stars, which has made his champions look like a shadow of their usual selves in pre-season.

England quartet Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Ebere Eze, and world champions Mikel Merino, David Raya and Martin Zubimendi will only begin their pre-season preparations today.

Martin Odegaard played just 30 minutes against Dortmund after returning to training last week, and he will need more minutes in the tank before he can be trusted to play a full game.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Meanwhile Jurrien Timber and William Saliba both remain out with groin and back injuries, respectively, and are not expected to return for the start of the season.

The absence of those players has been felt throughout Arsenal’s pre-season.

Yesterday’s defeat to Dortmund showed Arsenal’s defensive frailties when Saliba and Timber are unavailable.

Cristhian Mosquera fell asleep, allowing Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind him and score the opener for Dortmund.



And Arsenal finished the game with 18-year-old prospect Theo Julienne at right-back after Ben White was substituted – showing their lack of depth in that position without Timber.

Arteta revealed after the game that both Timber and Saliba are still some way from returning to the fold.

The Arsenal boss said: “Jurrien is progressing really well. He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now. But he’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“And William is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, don’t aggravate the injury. It’s going to take some time to heal. We know that.”

In midfield, Myles Lewis-Skelly has been operating out-of-position as a lone No6.



Given his inexperience in that area, attacking players have run riot around him without an experienced head to help him through the game.

That was evidenced when Konstantino Karetsas stormed through Arsenal’s midfield as if it didn’t exist before firing a curling effort in for Dortmund’s second goal.

Guimaraes, who was paraded out on the pitch before kick-off, can be the man to help solve that problem when Arsenal take on City on Sunday – but only if he is ready in time.



Arteta will be desperately scrambling to integrate the Brazilian into training and get him up to scratch during their final pre-season friendly against Como on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham was watching from the stands too, at the Emirates to support his brother Jobe who started in midfield for Dortmund.

And what Arteta would give to have a superstar like him available to command the middle of the park in the absence of Rice and Zubimendi.

The Arsenal duo haven’t kicked a ball since the World Cup, and their return seems unlikely before Sunday’s Community Shield.

However, Arteta said that some of his World Cup returnees could be put on a fast track back to action if they were used sparingly during the summer tournament.



He added: “We have very different groups within the same time that they are coming back.

“Some of them, they’ve done more. Others, they’ve done less. Some of them, they almost didn’t participate in the World Cup in terms of minutes. So they are all very different stages.”

There are still some positives in the performance of new addition Christos Tzolis, who continued his pre-season form by getting an assist and winning a penalty.



But it feels paramount that Arteta gets some of his stars back as soon as possible, with Arsenal facing a monstrous start to the season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Gunners take on Man City, Coventry, Aston Villa and Chelsea in a tricky start to their title defence.

If they have to face those challenges without their best players back in action, they could hit a stumbling block or two – leaving them playing catch-up in the title race.

OPINION Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat by Ryan Taylor

Ezri Konsa

It wouldn't be a transfer window without Arsenal signing a defender who can play at centre-back and full-back. And there aren't many better when it comes to that profile than Ezri Konsa.

‌



The England international has already been the subject of a bid from Arsenal, who reportedly offered just over half of his £60m valuation. Aston Villa rejected it but it's been claimed that their dressing room are 'resigned' to Konsa leaving.

Arteta was asked directly if Arsenal wanted to sign a defender after Saliba broke down with a back injury during the World Cup. "We conceded some poor goals today in the way we competed, especially," the Gunners boss replied.

Who should Arsenal sign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 5 Images Ezri Konsa could join his England team-mates at Arsenal (Image: Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

‌



"But that's a very collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve, for sure, we want that."

Bradley Barcola

After missing out on Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers, could be third time lucky for Arsenal in their search for a big-money wide forward? Paris Saint-Germain winger Barcola fits the bill and is a top target for Liverpool.

Arsenal, however, are said to be considering a move themselves. PSG value the 23-year-old at an eye-watering £145m, although the impending arrival of Ferran Torres from Barcelona could pressure them into a sale at a lower price.

View 5 Images Paris Saint-Germain are demanding £145million for Bradley Barcola (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

‌



Kenan Yildiz

Sticking in the wide forward areas, Kenan Yildiz's name continues to be linked with Arsenal. The Juventus forward is versatile, a trait which Arteta loves, and is rumoured to be his dream target.

Yildiz, 21, is said to be valued at a cool €100m (£85m) making him a cheaper alternative to Barcola. The German-born Turkey international enjoyed his most productive season to date last term, scoring 14 goals and providing 10 assists, and is the kind of player than can give Arsenal the dynamism fans have craved in attack.

View 5 Images Kenan Yildiz is reportedly Mikel Arteta's dream target (Image: Janelle St Pierre/Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez

It's been nearly two months since Julian Alvarez revealed that he wanted to leave Atletico Madrid this summer, but he remains at the Wanda Metropolitano. Arsenal have a long-standing interest in the former Man City striker, who Atletico have already rejected bids for this summer.

‌



Barcelona and Real Madrid both tried their luck earlier this summer, but his employers insist that the only way Alvarez can be sold is if a club pays his €500m (£428m) release clause. However, if Atletico were to sell, they'd prefer to offload him abroad.

View 5 Images Arsenal would need to pay top dollar for Julian Alvarez (Image: LOF/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

That gives Arsenal an advantage and although this remains a long shot, the Gunners could try their luck. A swap deal involving Viktor Gyokeres has even been mooted.

Sports.title: Liverpool can get five transfers wrapped up this week as developments made for £150m spree
Sports.content:
Liverpool can get five transfers wrapped up this week as developments made for £150m spree

Liverpool could step up their transfer activity this week

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola is eyeing a major transfer raid (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

The clock is ticking at Anfield, with the Premier League season opener now less than a fortnight away. The urgency to get transfer business over the line is intensifying as Andoni Iraola prepares for his competitive debut at the helm against Newcastle United on August 23.

‌



A significant summer shake-up has already begun to take shape on Merseyside. The high-profile exit of Mohamed Salah to Turkish side Trabzonspor has headlined the outgoings, while the incoming recruitment drive has seen Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet put pen to paper, alongside the acquisition of promising young centre-back Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

‌



Pre-season preparations are in full swing, though Iraola's Anfield bow ended in a 3-2 defeat to Monaco on Sunday. With a pair of friendly games against Como looming next weekend, the new manager has had ample opportunity to assess his squad's deficiencies and has publicly hinted that reinforcements are needed.

‌



As the countdown to the opening day accelerates, the revolving door at the club is expected to see further traffic moving in both directions. With that in mind, here is a look at five potential deals that could be finalised in the coming days.

Ronald Araujo

One transfer which appears to be a question of when rather than if is Ronald Araujo's arrival from Barcelona. The Uruguayan will join on an initial loan deal, with Barca manager Hansi Flick already confirming the switch.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool show familiar concern as three players shine in Monaco defeat - 5 talking points READ MORE :

"We couldn't include him like I wanted and also I think he wants to make something new," Flick said. "You know it more than me because in the past, something has happened, so this affected him.

"I saw him this morning and I said goodbye and I think he was very happy and Liverpool is also a fantastic club. I wish him all the best because he deserves it. He's a fantastic guy and fantastic player and was a great captain."

Curtis Jones

Plenty of Liverpool supporters remain hopeful Jones will stay put. Yet, he could still depart should Inter Milan match the Reds' valuation.

‌



Jones has entered the final 12 months of his deal and this may explain why the Italian outfit have been hesitant to commit substantial funds. A fee of £35m might well prove sufficient, though.

View 5 Images Inter Milan are interested in signing Curtis Jones (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Whether that represents the correct decision is an entirely different question. The England international is a homegrown product who has delivered during crucial moments, but his departure could generate resources for recruitment elsewhere.

‌



Bradley Barcola

Among the high-value targets continuing to be associated with an Anfield switch is France international Barcola. The winger has become the primary wide option, following earlier target Yan Diomande's transfer to Real Madrid.

View 5 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top transfer target (Image: Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain's pursuit of Ferran Torres might ease the disappointment of parting with Barcola. As might a price tag of approximately £110m, which appears to be what the French giants would accept.

‌



Arsenal also remain connected with the former Lyon star. Barcola, who reaches 24 in September, netted 11 league goals for PSG last term and shone during France's journey to the World Cup semi-finals.

Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Ibrahim Mbaye

Barcola may not be the sole player to swap PSG for Liverpool. Ibrahim Mbaye is prepared to depart the Ligue 1 club and the Reds are amongst prospective destinations.

‌



Senegal star Mbaye has found his route to regular action in Paris obstructed. Several Premier League clubs have been mentioned, with Liverpool far from the only possible landing spot.

View 5 Images Ibrahim Mbaye played for Senegal at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The 18-year-old featured 30 times for PSG last term, although numerous outings came from the bench. His youth means he would represent both an immediate and long-term addition, while a potential price tag exceeding £40m reflects his considerable promise.

‌



Cody Gakpo

Should Liverpool manage to complete that £150m double-signing from PSG, it might enable them to part with Gakpo. Tottenham hold interest in the Dutch attacker but the Reds are understood to desire two fresh forwards before considering a departure.

View 5 Images Tottenham are interested in Cody Gakpo (Image: Liverpool FC, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Gakpo has found the net 50 times in 180 matches across all competitions since arriving from PSV Eindhoven. Yet, there are no signs of Iraola being keen to sanction a sale.

Article continues below

A substantial offer might alter that, however. Figures around £70m have surfaced in certain quarters online and that type of return could prove welcome to balance a major Barcola investment.

Sports.title: Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract
Sports.content:
Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract

The England captain has entered the final year of his contract with Bayern Munich.

View 2 Images Harry Kane looks set to extend his stay at Bayern Munich. (Image: Adam Pretty/Getty Images)

England captain Harry Kane will reportedly extend his Bayern Munich contract by a further two years, as the German side ward off interest from Barcelona. The striker has entered the final year of his current deal at the Allianz Arena.

‌



Reports suggested that Barcelona were interested in signing Kane this summer as the search for a replacement for Robert Lewandowski. However, it seems that a stay in Germany is on the cards.

‌



The Times reports that the 33-year-old is set to extend his contract until 2029, with no significant change to his current salary. Kane is one of the top earners at Bayern Munich, with a yearly wage of around £21.5million per year.

‌



Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers READ MORE :

Everton and Crystal Palace agree stunning swap deal as Lamine Camara bid rejected READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The striker is yet to return to pre-season, having had an extended break following this summer’s World Cup with England. He captained the Three Lions to a third-place finish in the tournament.

He is expected to meet up with his teammates later this week as the club prepares for their Bundesliga opener against Stuttgart on Friday, 28 August (7.30pm BST).

‌



Before that, they play Borussia Dortmund in the German Super Cup final on Saturday, 22 August (7.30pm BST).

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 games in all competitions for Bayern last season, helping them to lift the Bundesliga crown for the second season in a row. He will look to continue that impressive goalscoring record in the new campaign.

View 2 Images Harry Kane captained England in this summer's World Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



The report adds that there is an 'expectation' that Kane will eventually return to the Premier League as he bids to break Alan Shearer’s long-standing goalscoring record. He currently has 213 goals in the league, 47 away from Shearer’s record of 260.

There has been consistent talk of a possible return to Tottenham Hotspur, where he scored all of his Premier League goals after coming through the academy, but it seems that Spurs will have to wait a bit longer for a possible reunion.

Kane left the club in 2023, with Spurs receiving a fee of around £86million from Bayern Munich.

Article continues below

In his time in Germany so far, he has scored 146 goals in 147 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club
Sports.content:
Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club

The billionaire Amazon founder has been in talks over buying a stake in Liverpool FC, and a deal with the consortium led by Amit Bhatia could be announced this week.

View Image Jeff Bezos is closing in on a Liverpool stake

A consortium led by Amit Bhatia, with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, are closing in on a deal to buy a stake in Liverpool. The stake is said to be 'roughly one third.'

‌



The Reds' current owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), confirmed that a group has approached them to buy a stake in the club, managed by Bhatia. A statement read: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

‌



According to Sky News, the deal would see Mr Bezos join an investor group that also includes Eduardo Saverin, the Facebook co‑founder. The syndicate is headed by Bhatia, the son‑in‑law of steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal and, until recently, a shareholder in Championship side Queens Park Rangers.

‌



Darwin Nunez prematurely announces Liverpool transfer with social media message READ MORE :

The report states that FSG, the club's controlling shareholder since 2010, is preparing to announce a transaction 'as soon as this week.' While an update is expected in the coming days, it's also suggested the timeline could 'slip into next week.'

If completed, the deal would see a trio of the world's richest men become co‑owners of the Reds - one of English football's most successful clubs.

Mr Bezos' wealth is estimated by Forbes at over $280bn (£207bn), with Mr Saverin said to be worth more than $32bn (£23bn). With that, the trio's investment would reportedly value Liverpool at around $6bn (£4bn), making it one of the richest deals in the sport's history.

‌



There has been a surge in American involvement across the Premier League, with half of the 20 clubs now predominantly owned by US‑based investors.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mr Bezos has previously explored major sporting investments, most notably in the NFL with the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders, but ultimately chose not to pursue either bid.

‌



Meanwhile, Mr Saverin was part of a consortium that mounted an unsuccessful takeover attempt for Chelsea FC during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

As for FSG, who also own MLB giants the Boston Red Sox, they have been custodians of Liverpool since 2010, having rescued the club from the brink of administration under former American owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

On the pitch, Liverpool last won the Premier League title in 2024/25 but now face a season of transition following the sacking of head coach Arne Slot and the departure of Mohamed Salah. So far this summer, the Reds have signed Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo on loan.

Article continues below

Bradley Barcola has also been earmarked as a priority attacking target, with Paris Saint‑Germain open to selling the Frenchman. However, talks have yet to produce a breakthrough.

Sports.title: Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers
Sports.content:
Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers

Aston Villa are set to add some firepower to their forward line for Unai Emery as they begin to replace Morgan Rogers following his sale to Chelsea

View 2 Images Endrick is set to move (Image: David S. Bustamante/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Aston Villa have expressed an interest in Real Madrid ace Endrick and could land a bargain deal. The Brazilian forward is considering a loan departure from the Bernabeu, and the La Liga giants are willing to cover part of the striker's salary to facilitate a move.

‌



Endrick, 20, scored eight goals and provided eight assists in 21 appearances for Lyon during his spell with the club last season. The former Palmeiras wonderkid remains down the pecking order at Real Madrid, behind Kylian Mbappe and new signing Carlos Espi.

‌



The arrival of Espi has prompted Endrick to give serious consideration to another loan move, after Jose Mourinho left the decision over his future in his hands. The Portuguese coach sees Endrick as more of a centre forward, albeit not a pure No.9, and while the youngster played on the wing in France, he would remain behind the likes of Yan Diomande, Brahim Diaz, Bernardo Silva and Rodrygo.

‌



Villa can fulfil Endrick's conditions for a loan move, according to AS. The forward, who featured in four of Brazil's five World Cup matches, wants to play European football, preferably in the Champions League, and be guaranteed a starting striker role.

Unai Emery's side face competition from Roma, with Real Madrid reluctant to sell due to the risk of losing money on the player. Including the transfer fee, commissions, salary, and bonuses, the Spanish club are said to have spent close to €80million (£68.53m).

Jose Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd READ MORE :

Villa are continuing to look towards strengthening their squad ahead of their return to Champions League action. The Midlands side had the coffers boosted by the £130m sale of Morgan Rogers.

‌



The Europa League winners have spoken publicly about the club’s transfer interest in Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha. Damian Vidagany has confirmed talks with Bayern.

Vidagany told Bild: “We need a midfielder because Amadou Onana is out for the entire season – and João Palhinha is a very good player who would fit our plans.

View 2 Images Joao Palhinha was on loan at Tottenham from Bayern Munich last term (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement. If something were to happen, it would always be based on the great respect we have for Bayern.

“We are friendly clubs, and our relationship with Max Eberl, Christoph Freund, and all the other officials is excellent. Therefore, I cannot and do not wish to comment on any further details.”

Article continues below

“I believe Aston Villa would be a great club for the player. In the league, six or seven clubs have a bigger budget than us,” he added.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Viktor Gyokeres stopped in his tracks and bats away Man City question
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Viktor Gyokeres stopped in his tracks and bats away Man City question

Arsenal will kick off their season in the Community Shield against Manchester City, and Viktor Gyokeres isn't having any suggestion that the match is merely a friendly

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres gave a firm response (Image: Hayters TV)

Arsenal star Viktor Gyokeres has rejected the claim that Sunday's clash with Manchester City in the Community Shield should be considered a friendly. The Gunners will take on City at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Sunday for the chance to win the season's first piece of silverware.

‌



The two teams went head-to-head last season in the Premier League title race, with Arsenal coming out on top. City did, however, beat Mikel Arteta's side in the Carabao Cup final.

‌



Following Arsenal's 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in an actual friendly, Gyokeres was asked about the game against City. The striker dismissed a reporter who noted that a portion of fans and pundits view the Community Shield as just another stage of pre-season.

‌



"Against City? As a friendly? I don't know what other people think but we want to win that game of course, for sure," Gyokeres affirmed.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss READ MORE :

"When you win titles, you get confidence, you get a boost with everything that comes with it. So, yeah, it's only positive things with that. We want to make sure that we're not only on top of that but that we're ready for the new season."

‌



Arsenal have lost their last two friendlies and will face Como on Wednesday looking to end pre-season on a high. Arteta hasn't had his full squad available to him yet, but he was asked after the Dortmund match whether he expects some players who were involved in the latter stages of this summer's World Cup to be invovled on Sunday.

"Yes, because we have very different groups within the same time that they are coming back," the Arsenal manager explained. "Why? Because some of them they've done more, some others they've done less, some more than they did and almost participated in the World Cup in terms of minutes.

Who'll win the Community Shield - Arsenal or Manchester City? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres won't be treating the Community Shield like a friendly (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

"So they are all very different stages. I want to see as well the way they have looked after themselves, what they said they did and actually what they did and how they look. But I'm sure that will be all positive surprises."

Arsenal's title defence begins at home to newly promoted Coventry on Friday, August 21. The Gunners will then travel to Aston Villa for their second Premier League fixture.

Sports.title: Stella issues rivals warning over McLaren 'momentum' in title battles
Sports.content:
McLaren boss Andrea Stella has issued a warning to his team's rivals for the remainder of the 2026 season as he expressed confidence in the Woking squad's ability to maintain momentum once it has been gained.

The reigning constructors' champions claimed a long-awaited first victory of the season in the final race before the summer break as reigning drivers' champion Lando Norris dominated in Hungary.

The result brought Norris back to within 91 points of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, while McLaren closed the gap on the Italian's Mercedes team to 159 points. To retain his title, Norris would also need to leapfrog Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Charles Leclerc, while Ferrari are only 72 points back from Mercedes in the team standings.

While both margins are considerable, Norris' performance following a significant upgrade package in Budapest has provided Stella with belief that McLaren can continue to perform strongly over the remaining 12 rounds of the season, starting with the Dutch Grand Prix from August 21-23.

Asked whether his team can get back into the fight for world titles, Stella said: "That's a difficult question, but there's a very clear answer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Norris' victory last time out in Hungary, David Croft debates whether McLaren are now capable of winning further races or not

"If we can continue the season as we did in Budapest, we can still achieve a great deal. To do so, we must keep pushing with the development of the MCL40 and ensure we outpace our rivals - who certainly aren't standing still - in this race within the race, which is the competition over updates.

"The result will depend on how effective the solutions we bring to the track prove to be. In the first part of the season, we struggled more than we expected in this regard too, but I believe that in recent years, once we've gained some momentum, we've been able to maintain it."

McLaren were in a contrasting position this time last year, having reached the summer break with a 299-point lead in the constructors' standings, and Oscar Piastri leading team-mate Norris in what appeared to be a two-horse race for the drivers' title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

However, Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who trailed Piastri by 104 points with nine rounds remaining, staged a remarkable fightback to ultimately finish the season just two points behind Norris and 11 ahead of Piastri.

Stella added: "There are still 12 races left on the calendar, so there are plenty of opportunities given that 546 points are up for grabs.

"Of course, the gap in both championships is significant, but we remember last year's lesson well: after all, I always tell the team that if we've set up a new display cabinet to house the new, recent trophies at the McLaren Technology Centre, then we have a duty to do our utmost to keep filling it..."

Hungary upgrade represented 'change of direction'

McLaren had played down the upgrade package they brought to Hungary ahead of the event, but the results spoke for themselves as Norris took pole before showing searing pace to win the race.

The Brit ultimately beat Verstappen by 15 seconds but had he not been held up by Piastri for the first half of the race having been overtaken by his team-mate on the opening lap, the margin could have been far greater.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring

Reflecting on the process that led to the latest upgrades, Stella said: "There wasn't a single event that changed course; rather, it was a growing awareness of the scale of the challenge we're facing and the adjustments we needed to make.

"Paradoxically, the enforced break in April probably allowed us to focus entirely on analysing the MCL40's performance and to fully understand that we needed to redirect or strengthen its development in certain areas of the car.

"It is clear that the Budapest weekend, which brought the first half of the season to a close, was the highlight: not only because of the result, but above all because the aerodynamic package we introduced at the Hungaroring is the result of this change of direction in development and has enabled us to make significant progress in terms of competitiveness."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to his first win of 2026 saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

Stella also praised the work his team have done alongside engine supplier Mercedes to optimise the performance of their power unit.

"Over the past few months we've had the opportunity to deepen our understanding of the new power unit supplied by Mercedes HPP and to work with our technical partners to work out how best to utilise it," he added.

"It's been a long process, with its ups and downs, but one that's starting to bear fruit. That said, I expect that optimising the power unit will remain a complex issue throughout the 2026 season."

Sports.title: Amazon founder Bezos nears deal to buy stake in Liverpool
Sports.content:
Sky News understands a consortium including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is closing in on a deal to buy a roughly one-third stake in Liverpool.

Sky News has learnt that Fenway Sports Group (FSG), the Anfield club's controlling shareholder since 2010, is preparing to make an announcement about a transaction as soon as this week.

The deal will see Mr Bezos participate in an investor group alongside Eduardo Saverin, one of the co-founders of the social network Facebook.

The syndicate is led by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and until recently a shareholder in Championship club Queens Park Rangers.

One source indicated that an announcement was expected in the coming days, although they cautioned that it could slip into next week.

If completed, the deal would install a trio of the world's wealthiest individuals as co-owners of the Reds, one of the most successful teams in the history of English football.

Mr Bezos alone has a fortune estimated by Forbes at over £207bn ($280bn), while Mr Saverin is said to be worth over £23.7bn ($32bn).

Their investment in Liverpool will reportedly value the club at £4.4bn ($6bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Sky Sports News has contacted Liverpool and FSG for comment.

Image: Amazon founder Bezos has an estimated fortune of over £207bn

While Mr Bezos has not previously been linked to deals in football, his prospective involvement in the Liverpool FC consortium underlines the extent to which sport is now viewed by wealthy investors as an asset class in its own right.

Mr Saverin, who is 44 years old, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea FC during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

One insider said the deal was now expected to be slightly larger than previously thought, potentially involving a stake of over 30 per cent.

Nevertheless, if its valuation hits £4.4bn ($6bn), the deal will reinforce the huge financial success that FSG has enjoyed during its 16 years as the club's owner.

The Boston Red Sox owner acquired Liverpool for just £300m with the club in a troubled state financially.

The arrival of such a powerful consortium will fuel expectations that its members will ultimately seek outright control of the Reds.

A spokesperson for FSG said last month: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

FSG declined to comment further on the potential timing of a deal.

A spokesman for the consortium led by Mr Bhatia also declined to comment.

The last time a stake in Liverpool changed hands was in 2023, when Dynasty Equity bought a small interest valuing it at more than £3.3bn ($4.5bn).

Image: FSG have been in complete control of Liverpool since 2010

Sky Sports takes a look at some of the key questions surrounding the sale of a minority stake in Liverpool...

Who are Bhatia and Bezos?

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur who has an investment banking background.

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital, which invests in a range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail, and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

Sports.title: Super League's Final Charge: Play-off spots taking shape with five rounds left
Sports.content:
There are just five rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

Seven teams remain in contention for a play-off spot and most of those are still eyeing a top-two finish.

In Super League, the two teams who finish in first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

There are going to be so many twists and turns along the way and you can catch them all live on Sky Sports.

With that in mind, let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (36 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been sitting pretty at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their five remaining fixtures.

They stayed top in spectacular fashion with a win over Wakefield Trinity in their latest game, showing they mean business.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last five matches, they face Leigh Leopards (H), York Knights (A), St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

That means they have three teams in their run-in who are hunting play-off places. If they can remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (34 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he is pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Bradford Bulls (A), Wakefield Trinity (H), Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Wigan are likely to have their sights firmly set on ensuring they beat Wakefield and Leeds to pile on the pressure.

3) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caius Faatili produced an incredible run as he set up Caleb Hamlin-Uele's try for Wakefield against Leeds

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity. They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds.

Wakefield returned to Super League last year following their relegation in 2024 and have lit up the competition, their star-studded side becoming a formidable one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Sinfield scored for Wakefield against his father's former side Leeds as rugby league legend Kevin watched on proudly

They have games against St Helens (H), Wigan Warriors (A), York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left. That is four teams out of the seven still in the fight.

They will look at York as an absolute must-win and crucial two points. The Wigan and Warrington games will also be key as they are two other teams right in the chase for a top-two spot.

4) Warrington Wolves (30 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League clash between Bradford Bulls and Warrington Wolves as Matty Ashton scored twice in a dominant 42-4 victory for the visitors

Warrington Wolves, along with Hull KR, have six matches remaining thanks to their rescheduled round-two match.

This was moved due to the Robins playing in Las Vegas.

With that, it is a more jam-packed Final Charge for them but also one gives Sam Burgess' side a good opportunity to prosper.

In their remaining fixtures, they face York Knights (H), Hull KR (A), Huddersfield Giants (H), Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

If the Wolves are going to be contenders, they will have to pick up points against the four lowly sides they face.

5) Hull KR (28 points, one game in hand)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Castleford Tigers against Hull KR from the Super League

The other side with six games remaining, Hull KR, are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way and climb as high up the table as possible.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their remaining six matches are against Catalans Dragons (H), Warrington Wolves (H), Toulouse Olympique (H), Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

Four out of the six are at Craven Park, which will only boost their chances. Wins against Catalans, Toulouse and Huddersfield will also be a non-negotiable.

6) Leigh Leopards (28 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against York Knights from the Super League

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Leeds Rhinos (A), Bradford Bulls (H), Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

No one can deny that is a difficult Final Charge, but if Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to show their steel now.

7) St Helens (24 points)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of St Helens against Hull FC in the Betfred Super League

St Helens have five matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their most recent loss to Hull FC, it is fair to say St Helens look down and out.

However, they will now refocus and aim for five wins out of five to be in with a shout. If they win all five, they move to 34 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player St Helens chairman Eamonn McManus announced his side will take on Hull FC in a Super League clash in Dublin on April 25

Not only that, they face some of the other play-off chasing teams so some matches basically become worth four points.

They will take on Wakefield Trinity (A), Castleford Tigers (H), Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

Four out of their five remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do somehow find some form, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.
