Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Badri chases four-timer at Windsor
Sports.content:
Windsor takes centre stage on Monday with a six-race Flat meeting live on Sky Sports Racing.

7.15 Windsor - Badri seeks four-timer in Sprint Series Final

Badri seeks a four-timer in the feature race at Windsor, the Fitzdares Sprint Series Final Handicap over six furlongs.

This horse has been a credit to connections, winning 15 times in 75 starts with his last three runs resulting in success, all at Pontefract. That has taken him from 89-rated up to 99 which is his best mark since March 2024.

Another Abbot returns to Windsor looking to follow up his course-and-distance success two weeks ago after previously running a creditable race in behind Amazing Journey, who went on to to win the International Handicap on King George Day at Ascot. That form reads very well and he could be hard to beat.

Sudden Flight is a model of consistency, finishing second in his last three starts which included in behind Another Abbot two weeks ago. He does find winning hard to come by, though, having not won since July last year, but is now better off at the weights with William Haggas' charge and looks sure to run his race.

6.15 Windsor - Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On feature

Previous-winners Harry Knows and Keep Kicking On lock horns in the Fitzdares Nursery Handicap.

Harry Knows won in stylish fashion last time out at Windsor and received a three-pound rise for the success which might not be enough to stop him from continuing the winning sequence.

Keep Kicking On also arrives off the back of his first success over this track and trip when hitting the line readily three weeks ago and there could be more to come.

This Moment represents the connections of Bow Echo, dropping into a nursery for the first time and must be respected off 79 given the form of George Boughey and Billy Loughnane this season. He is interesting first time out after a gelding operation too.

5.45 Windsor - Mythological Star bids to defy penalty

Mythological Star headlines in the Find Us At fitzdares.com Apprentice Handicap where he carries a six-pound penalty for his success at Ffos Las.

Gelded before his first run, this half-brother to Astro King made it fourth-time lucky last time out when he won a shade cosily. Narrowly beaten on his penultimate start, that win came as no surprise as he was well supported and justified favouritism in good style for Daniel and Claire Kubler.

Hello Cotai disappointed at Epsom last month but this had followed a win here at Windsor and then a commendable third at Epsom before he finished last of four. He may prove best of the opposition.

Sports.title: Brennan secures FedEx Cup Playoffs spot with Wyndham Championship win
Sports.content:
Michael Brennan secured his place in the FedExCup Playoffs as he won the Wyndham Championship by three strokes from Beau Hossler.

Brennan had a run of five straight birdies between the fourth and eighth holes, and recovered from a bogey on the 11th by picking up further shots on the 13th and 18th holes, saving par on the 17th with an excellent second shot after running into the rough with his tee-shot.

Hossler, who shared the overnight lead with Brennan, had kept himself in touch with a birdie on the third and an eagle at the par-five fifth, but then bogeyed the ninth and 12th holes as Brennan surged forward.

"I did great for nine holes," Brennan said. "I felt really good on the front nine. Just playing my game, I was really staying within myself, hitting good shots.

Image: Brennan shot a final-round 64 at Sedgefield Country Club

"Felt like I was really in control. Got a little nervous around 10 and 11. I made a really nice par putt on 12 and that kind of steadied me a little bit going through and I'm just glad to make a few putts coming in.

"It's everything. I mean, I don't want to be done playing golf. I feel like I've played the best golf I have all year the last couple weeks.

"Unfortunately, a couple tough Sundays, but outside of that, I've been playing really solidly. This is my sixth week in a row and so seven's a lot, but I think I'm going to be perfectly happy running on fumes next week."

England's Harry Hall finished with a round of 65 to take a share of fifth place, one shot clear of compatriot Matt Wallace who had a share of seventh after he also closed with a 65.

Sports.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
Sports.content:
Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”.

In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

The three confederations are understood to have started preliminary discussions about the organisation of new competitions amid Uefa’s repeated threats to boycott Fifa events. As things stand, next month’s under-20 women’s World Cup could take place without the presence of European teams and alternative options are being sought.

The letter is signed by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, his AFC counterpart, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, and the Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani. Efforts to unite around a suitable candidate to replace Infantino have stepped up since his privately-backed plan was revealed and Montagliani is believed to be among the leading contenders.

“Leadership in football is not a possession,” part of the letter reads. “It is not about holding – or demanding – power to be held. It is a duty of service to the football family that entrusts it. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned.”

It strongly criticises Fifa’s response to the crisis, which saw a meeting between a small number of senior staff in Rabat followed by an apology from Infantino that appeared not to show remorse for the scheme itself.

View image in fullscreen The Canadian Victor Montagliani consoles Lionel Messi after the World Cup final. He is believed to be interested in running for the Fifa presidency. Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment,” the letter says. “It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the Fifa World Cup was a profound failure of judgment – not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions Fifa exists to serve.”

The three presidents also call for an independent review, conducted by a body outside of football, into the scandal. Fifa had previously committed to presenting a full report to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting. The letter also directly addresses concerns that countries may lose out on financial aid under a different leadership, saying it is “[not] about any member association losing the support it has earned, despite the fearmongering directed at our leadership to suggest otherwise.”

The letter concludes: “There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness … Football’s strength has always been its unity. We call for that unity to be honoured now, with leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Any candidates to run for the Fifa election must announce their bid by 18 November. The confederations are understood to consider all options on the table in their push for Infantino to be replaced, provided they fit within Fifa’s statutes and governance framework.

While the letter outlines the stances of the three confederations, and particularly their leaderships, the story is more complicated within individual member associations. Few outside Europe have been willing to come out publicly against Infantino and only a small minority have been tempted to recall the letters of support they had sent backing his re-election next March. Additionally the influential African and South American confederations, Caf and Conmebol, have both come out backing Infantino in recent days.

A number of larger member associations are understood to have written to Infantino asking for a meeting in which he would be required to explain his actions around the FFE scheme, with no response received so far. Nor has Infantino been in touch personally with federations to address his leading role in the ongoing turmoil.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 2: Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Ben Fisher’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

The image of John McGinn hoisting aloft the Europa League trophy in Istanbul as the confetti cannons fired is crystallised in the minds of Aston Villa supporters, but less than three months on, plenty has changed since one of the club’s greatest days. Three major players from the starting lineup – Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, two of whom scored – have exited, and another may follow if Arsenal make a serious play for the dependable Ezri Konsa.

A key trio of coaches have also left – the set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, assistant manager Pako Ayestarán and the influential individual coach, Antonio Rodríguez Saravia – but most importantly the common denominator and driver of Villa’s incredible rebirth remains in post. It is a good job Unai Emery enjoys a challenge. It has been a typically busy summer, with pre-season trips to Portugal, Indonesia and Hong Kong, plus the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on Wednesday and a friendly trip to Mönchengladbach to follow, but there is work to do if Emery is to repeat the feat of fourth place and break new ground, again, by securing Champions League qualification for successive campaigns.

After a terrible start, Villa edged over the line last season, but the landscape is unlikely to be so forgiving this time. Nobody played more minutes for Villa than Rogers and it was no surprise Villa’s alarming drop in form around spring coincided with Tielemans being injured. Villa need their replacements to work. João Gomes, a £38m buy from Wolves, looks a smart fit; the tigerish Brazil midfielder made the third-highest number of tackles in the division last season (107) and was fourth on the list for ball recoveries (194). Johan Manzambi is one of the game’s most exciting young talents, while Emery believes he can rehabilitate Alejandro Garnacho, who has joined on a season-long loan from Chelsea.

Only Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester City have amassed more Premier League points in the three-and-a-half years since Emery arrived, and while it would be foolish to write him off, every season his task seems to get that bit harder. He can still call on a core cast of reliable performers in Konsa, McGinn, Matty Cash, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins, while Boubacar Kamara’s return from injury this month is a timely boost. But it is hard not to wonder whether Villa have peaked.

Off-field picture

The response of a senior executive was telling when asked if qualifying for the Champions League makes life easier when it comes to meeting the financial rules. “Not easier but less difficult,” came the reply. Villa have since signed a lucrative shirt sponsorship deal with Visit Rwanda, worth about £20m per season, though Amnesty International warns Rwanda “is using sportswashing to deflect attention from its terrible human rights record”. Meanwhile, Villa Park’s makeover continues with the North Stand closed for the season, the stadium’s capacity falling to 37,000 during its redevelopment. The new-look stand will have a steel roof, modern facade and accommodate more than 50,000 supporters, and will be ready for 2027-28 and Euro 2028.

Owner-fan relationship

Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens will always be adored for putting Villa firmly back on the map, elevating them to become major Premier League players and, ultimately, as the people who gave Emery the keys to transform the club. Both joined the on-field celebrations in Istanbul in May, Sawiris with a claret-and-blue scarf around his neck. Michael Angelakis, chair of investment company Atairos and chief executive of Comcast, acquired a minority stake in 2023. The story goes that Sawiris, Egypt’s richest man, handed Emery a blank sheet of paper and asked him to design his vision when meeting the Basque for the first time in Madrid, at the home of the agent Jorge Mendes.

The manager

“He lives like a monk in a tracksuit,” was how Villa’s director of football operations and Emery’s right-hand man, Damian Vidagany, described the 54-year-old manager’s work ethic in the book Waking The Giant. During the season it is not unusual for Emery, who has an apartment in Birmingham city centre, to spend 12 hours a day at Villa’s Bodymoor Heath base, sometimes analysing footage on his laptop while on the exercise bike or treadmill, long after his players have gone. Emery’s squad have grown accustomed to long meetings, sometimes twice a day – one was held less than 12 hours after cementing their place in the Champions League after beating Liverpool in May, in preparation for Emery to clinch a record fifth Europa League title of his coaching career.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi looks pleased to be wearing the claret and blue. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

There were a few nerves at Villa as Manzambi illuminated Switzerland’s World Cup, concerns his price could balloon or that bigger fish may blow them out of the water. But Villa had done their homework and got a longstanding target over the line for a club-record £51m amid interest from rivals. Manzambi was on Villa’s radar long before he impressed against them for Freiburg in the Europa League final. Murat Yakin, the Switzerland head coach, described Manzambi as “a street footballer”, saying the 20-year-old’s humility and quality means he is capable of playing across the pitch. He played regularly as a No 8 in the Bundesliga and Emery is an admirer of his versatility.

Stat attack

Aston Villa scored 15 goals from outside the box last season. Seven teams had recorded more in one of the previous 17 Premier League campaigns, but no side in that period bettered their 8.4% shot conversion rate. As only 3.6% of attempts from this range are converted on average, Villa’s 2025-26 tally feels impossible to repeat.

Set for a breakthrough

It will be interesting to see if the 17-year-old Brian Madjo, son of former Plymouth and Shrewsbury forward Guy, can build on his encouraging pre-season form. Emery and his coaches are big fans of Madjo, a physical striker born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, so no wonder this month Villa welcomed the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) clearing Madjo to feature after Fifa rules prohibited him from playing after joining from Metz in a £10m deal in January. “English player allowed to play in England #freemadjo,” McGinn posted on social media. It has been a whirlwind 12 months for Madjo: he made his Ligue 1 debut last August aged 16, before scoring on debut for England Under-17s a few weeks later. Four goals in pre-season has led to a sense that his first competitive minutes for Villa are close.

World Cup impact

Amadou Onana, whose Villa career has been stop-start owing to injury, ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in Belgium’s last-16 win over the USA. Manzambi enjoyed a fine World Cup, even if his tournament also ended with a knee injury, ruling him out of Switzerland’s last 16 and quarter-final matches and delaying his Villa debut. Martínez made it to another final with Argentina. Konsa started every game for England before the semi-final against Argentina: his 72nd-minute introduction from the bench for Anthony Gordon widely pinpointed as a negative change that invited pressure.

Sports.title: Manchester City closing in on £85m Bouaddi to soften blow of Rodri’s expected exit
Sports.content:
Manchester City are closing in on signing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille, with the midfielder’s expected arrival clearing the path for Rodri to join Barcelona. The 18-year-old has agreed personal terms with City, but the club are still finalising the deal with Lille valueing Bouaddi at €100m (£85m).

City’s new manager, Enzo Maresca, wants to integrate the Morocco international into his first-team squad immediately. City meet Arsenal in the Community Shield on Sunday and open their Premier League campaign against Bournemouth on 23 August.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Barcelona are confident of landing Rodri from City, but will have to return with an improved offer after an initial €45m bid was rejected last week. The sale of Ferran Torres, who is of interest to Paris Saint-Germain, would finance Rodri’s purchase. City are all but resigned to the sale of the 30-year-old, who has a year left on his contract.

If the Bouaddi deal can be completed, he would join Elliot Anderson, who arrived last month from Nottingham Forest for £116m, in a new-look midfield, which has lost the experience of Bernardo Silva.

Manchester United, meanwhile, are interested in the Leicester teenager Louis Page. United, who face competition from Arsenal, are hopeful of a deal for the 18-year-midfielder, with Page believed to favour a transfer to Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton agree Brennan Johnson-Dwight McNeil swap deal
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace and Everton have agreed a straight swap for Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil – six months after McNeil’s partner accused Palace of “messing with the winger’s mental health” after pulling out of a deal.

McNeil and Johnson, who became Palace’s record signing when he joined in January from Tottenham for £35m, only to be surpassed by the arrival of Jørgen Strand Larsen from Wolves for an initial £43m a few weeks later, are understood to have both agreed four year contracts with the option of a further 12 months. Both are expected to have medicals on Monday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

McNeil, who has now entered the final year of his Everton contract, had looked set to move to Selhurst Park in February after Palace agreed a £20m fee on transfer deadline day. But the collapse of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s £30m move to Milan, after the France striker failed a medical, prompted Palace to change their offer to an initial loan with an obligation to buy at the end of the season. They submitted a deal sheet to the Premier League but then pulled out, with McNeil’s partner, Megan Sharpley, writing in an emotional post on Instagram that there had been “radio silence” from Palace and that the player’s mental health had been impacted.

“Tonight, and the last 48 hours, have broken my heart to see how the football world you love so much can be so cruel to you,” she wrote at the time. “We live in a world where everyone is aware of how big a problem mental health is. So, in football, why do we find it acceptable because these young men are on a lot of money and that’s okay to mess and toy with their mental health and that it’s just part of the job?”

Johnson has been disappointing since moving to south London, failing to score in 18 Premier League appearances. Given that he signed a lucrative four-and-a-half-year contract in January that is believed to be worth more than £100,000 a week, Palace will take a significant hit on the fee they paid but remove one of their highest earners from the wage bill.

Palace are also set to finalise a deal to sign Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise for £21m. The Israel right-back had his medical on Sunday and is expected to sign a five-year contract in south London. The 21-year-old’s move to Internazionale broke down last month after he failed a medical.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 1: Arsenal
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 1st (NB: this is not necessarily Ed Aarons’ prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st

Prospects

Even losing on penalties in the Champions League final could not take any of the gloss off last season as Arsenal ended their 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions. The celebrations have continued all summer after some wild scenes on the streets of north London on their return from Budapest, although concerns over the fitness of some key players after their exploits at the World Cup are mounting.

Arsenal have acted quickly to reinforce their midfield by signing Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle given Declan Rice’s workload must be managed very carefully after playing through neural pain in his hamstring and lower back since December. The arrival of Greece forward Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard also looks like a smart piece of business on the left-hand side of the attack. But with Vinícius Junior staying at Real Madrid, despite Arsenal’s best efforts, supporters will be hoping there is still a chance that the sporting director, Andrea Berta, could conjure up a heavyweight attacking signing before the window closes given Bukayo Saka’s fitness problems in recent seasons.

The back injury that will sideline William Saliba for an unknown period could prove even more central to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining their title. A defence that conceded 27 goals last year in the Premier League may struggle without the immense talents of the France defender, even if they can bring in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa as hoped. Whether Arsenal can maintain their dominance from set pieces over the past two campaigns will also be crucial, with more scrutiny expected from video assistant referees after the fallout from their controversial victory at West Ham in May.

Not since 1935, when Arsenal became the second team to win three successive league titles, have they retained their crown. Having strengthened the deepest squad in the division still further, they will take some stopping again.

Off-field picture

Money definitely isn’t an issue for Stan Kroenke. Arsenal’s co-owner became America’s largest private landowner this year and has spent more than £1.5bn on new players since becoming the majority shareholder in 2011 through his holding company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE). Next on the agenda is an upgrade to the Emirates Stadium that could increase the capacity of their home to more than 70,000. Talks have begun with the stadium’s original architects, Populous, over a project that could cost up to £500m. The much-criticised shirtsleeve deal with Visit Rwanda ended last season and has been replaced by the HR company Deel, itself controversial in some sections of the Arsenal fanbase, while Emirates have renewed their longstanding partnership until 2033.

Owner-fan relationship

Kroenke and his son Josh – who are co-chairs – clearly revelled in carrying out the Premier League trophy at Selhurst Park before it was presented to the captain, Martin Ødegaard, after Arsenal’s final game of the season in May. Having once been criticised for running the club “like an investment vehicle”, now they are praised for the enormous effect they have made. Kroenke Jr’s promise there would be “no standing still once this season ends” was an ominous sign to their rivals given KSE have a reputation as serial winners in a number of sports in America.

The manager

Mikel Arteta’s expected bumper new contract extension – that will make him one of the best-paid managers in the world – has yet to be confirmed, but there is no doubting his commitment to the cause. The Spaniard could not bear to watch as Manchester City’s challenge collapsed against Bournemouth last season and was in his back garden “building a fire” when Arsenal were confirmed as champions. With Pep Guardiola gone, Arteta has the opportunity to build a new winning dynasty of his own.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen The Gunners fans will be hoping to see Bruno Guimarães’ goal celebration on numerous occasions this season. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

The arrival of Guimarães was another big statement of intent from Arsenal. The former Newcastle captain wants to win more trophies after capturing hearts and minds on Tyneside and he will provide several options in the already well-stacked engine room. As well as relieving the load on Rice, the versatile 28-year-old Brazil midfielder is capable of fulfilling a number of roles, from deep-lying playmaker to box-to box destroyer. While it remains to be seen how Arteta chooses to use Guimarães when he also has Martín Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ødegaard and Mikel Merino at his disposal, his talents will only add to the quality in Arsenal’s squad.

Stat attack

Referees have been told to pay much more attention to grappling during set-pieces this season so it will be interesting to see if this has any effect on Arsenal. Only three teams in the Premier League had a better non-penalty expected goal difference than the Gunners had from set plays alone.

Set for a breakthrough

Max Dowman was a record-breaking revelation as he dipped his toes into senior football for the first time last season and the signs are that the 16-year-old could be handed more opportunities after impressing again during pre-season. A brilliant goal and an assist against Girona capped a man-of-the-match display from the right flank. With Saka and Noni Madueke to be eased back in after returning from World Cup duty, Dowman is ready to add to his solitary Premier League start, against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, and should appear more regularly in cup competitions.

World Cup impact

Rice and Saka arrived in the United States feeling the effects of a marathon season and it was to their immense credit that they played through the pain barrier and made it to England’s eighth match of the tournament. Only Thomas Tuchel knows why he left Saka on the bench in the semi-final against Argentina and his hat-trick in the third-place playoff a few days later showed how potent he can be even with an achilles problem. Both require an extended break before returning to the rigours of club football and Arsenal will give them as long as possible. But such is their importance that it will be sooner rather than later.

Sports.title: Arsenal step up push for defensive cover with Timber and Saliba sidelined
Sports.content:
Arsenal are stepping up their efforts to sign defensive cover for William Saliba after Mikel Arteta revealed Jurriën Timber is well away from returning to competitive action. Saliba will be sidelined for an extended period after breaking down during the World Cup with a back injury.

After Arsenal lost a second successive friendly when Borussia Dortmund won 3-2 on Sunday to lift the Emirates Cup in a performance that featured several defensive mistakes, Arteta would not be drawn on when the France defender is expected to return, but said it would take “some time to heal”.

There are also concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that led him to miss most of the run-in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.

“William Saliba is in rest mode at the moment for two weeks. He had to do almost nothing, an aggravated injury, so it’s going to take some time to heal.”

Pressed on how Arsenal will cope without Saliba, he said: “We have experienced that in the past, unfortunately. When he’s been available, he’s hit home and the stats are incredible. We know we lost a massive player, the same with Jurriën.”

Arsenal have had a bid for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected and are expected to return with a new offer for the England defender, who is also capable of playing at right-back. Villa value him at £60m, but with less than two years left on his contract Arsenal are unwilling to pay that much for the 28-year-old. The Premier League champions have also shown an interest in signing Cristian Romero from Tottenham, but any move for the Argentina defender is extremely unlikely given Spurs’ reluctance to sell to their north London rivals.

Arteta, who started with Cristhian Mosquera in central defence alongside Gabriel Magalhães against Dortmund, said Arsenal’s existing players must get up to speed before Sunday’s Community Shield against Manchester City, but did not rule out bringing in another defender.

“It has to be the right player in the market to make us much better,” he said. “We conceded some poor goals today, in the way we competed especially. But that’s a collective responsibility. So we need to improve with the players we have.”

Sports.title: Van Dijk looks forward to more quality arriving at Liverpool before new season
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk is ready to welcome Ronald Araújo as his new centre-back partner at Liverpool with the deal to sign the Barcelona defender almost complete.

Van Dijk played almost an hour, his first pre-season appearance, as Liverpool were beaten 3-2 by Monaco at Anfield, having led 2-0. The Dutchman fouled Aleksandr Golovin to concede a penalty just before the break, which Golovin scored.

Jérémy Jacquet remained absent, with Liverpool’s new £50m arrival being treated with kid gloves after an injury-hit spell at the end of last season with Rennes. Araújo has been signed to bolster Andoni Iraola’s defensive options, with Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni also sidelined.

“Any player that arrives at the club we will be welcoming,” Van Dijk said of Araújo. “I have no idea if it has been announced or not. I have not seen him so let’s see.”

Van Dijk was upbeat about Jacquet and the prospect of more transfer activity between now and the transfer deadline on 1 September. Liverpool are keen on adding to their forward line with Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola of interest.

“Let’s see what the next couple of weeks are going to bring. Any quality we can add to the team will definitely be welcome so let’s see.

“I’ve not seen any of him. I’ve spoken to him,” Van Dijk said of Jacquet. “I’ve seen him walking around and we have conversations. I can’t wait to see him back on the pitch and I hope that happens very soon. I’m not a doctor, so I don’t know exactly the situation, but I have a feeling this week he could be back on the pitch, hopefully as soon as possible.”

While Van Dijk accepted Liverpool are in a transition period after the sacking of Arne Slot, he revealed he has been in regular contact with Iraola and offered his full support to the new head coach.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Van Dijk said: “We had a great conversation in the first week when it got announced and the main thing for him to know is I am here for him regardless, anything he needs, wants to know, wants me to do for the team or whatever. Hopefully we will be successful this season.

“Nothing to take away from Arne and his staff, we had an amazing time together, but obviously last year [was] a disappointment. This year we have a new manager who has new ways of preparation, so we have to adapt to the new staff, different training methods. I liked working under Arne and I am sure I will like working under the new manager.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Endrick set for Villa loan? De Jong offered in Rodri deal?
Sports.content:
A sense of excitement is what Aston Villa need at the moment after selling off key players. What better way to create it than signing a prodigious talent from Real Madrid? The Villans have inquired about the Brazilian Endrick, who impressed on loan at Lyon last season, and may make a similar temporary move to the Premier League.

Manchester City are not particularly keen to sell Rodri but, with a year left on his contract money may well talk, especially if the midfielder wants to leave. Barcelona’s first bid was rejected but they are readying another. One idea is to offer Frenkie de Jong as part of the deal, so at least Enzo Maresca would have a shiny new midfielder to play with.

One player who could be leaving Camp Nou is the World Cup-winning goalscorer Ferran Torres, who has reportedly told Paris Saint-Germain he wants to pop across to the French capital. Not that a deal between the clubs has been agreed.

Another potential swap deal is on the cards between Everton and Crystal Palace. Calls have been made to discuss Dwight McNeil moving to Selhurst Park and Brennan Johnson swapping places with him at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The two wingers have struggled for game time perhaps a swap would reignite their careers. McNeil almost ended up at Selhurst Park in January before a late breakdown in talks left the player and his family furious.

Promoted Ipswich have been active in the market and could add the Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. A bid has been faxed over, leaving the Tractor Boys to play the waiting game, but they may face competition for his signature.

After what must have been a lot of wrangling, Chelsea have agreed to loan Filip Jörgensen to sister club Strasbourg. The Blues are well-stocked with players and need to bin a few who can’t be sent to Strasbourg, so they may allow Jamie Gittens to head on loan to Roma.

The departure of Bruno Guimarães will prompt a rethink at Newcastle, who rather desperately need a new central midfielder. Sandro Tonali was sold a while back, giving the club some cash to play with, but they still seem to be thinking about signing João Palhinha who is not wanted at Bayern Munich The former Tottenham man Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is another option. Palhinha is also of interest to Aston Villa, who have made contact with the Bundesliga champions.

Manchester United are planning for the future with a move for the Leicester teenager Louis Page. The 18-year-old came through the academy ranks with the Foxes, but is naturally more than happy to take the leap from League One.

And finally: Shea Charles is closing on a move from Southampton to Fulham for a roaring £30m.

Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Hammers knocked back in Parrott pursuit

West Ham have had their opening bid for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott rejected.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, the Hammers made their opening offer of around £15million over the weekend but it is likely to take a Championship record fee of £17.5m to get their man. They are now formulating a new offer.

RB Leipzig have also contacted Alkmaar in recent days but the Hammers are further advanced.

West Ham are exploring a move for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson and have made an approach for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Toon close on Hojbjerg

Newcastle and Marseille are working toward agreement on a £12million deal for midfielder Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on a Friday, talks had begun with the Denmark international to fill the void left by the departures of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal.

The 31-year-old is viewed as the experienced figure who can guide the new younger players Newcastle have added to their squad.

They had spoken to Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as a back-up option but Hojbjerg is keen to make the move and all is progressing.

Danish media Tipsbladet say the deal will be wrapped up this week.

The Israeli international saw a £21million move to Inter Milan collapse over a medical issue but has had a number of clubs enquiring since.

Shea Charles is undergoing his Fulham medical this morning ahead of his £30million transfer from Southampton.

Fulham have agreed to pay £27m with a further £3m in add-ons for the 22-year-old after Manchester City declined their option to activate matching rights.

Southampton retain a 20 per cent sell-on while Charles has agreed a five-year deal with an option for a further year.

Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson have been given permission to undergo medicals ahead of their respective swap deal to Everton and Crystal Palace.

Brennan Johnson are Dwight McNeil look set to swap their Premier League teams

Johnson has struggled to settle at Palace since joining from Tottenham for £35m in January. Everton have also held an interest in Johnson in previous windows.

Everton's move for Celtic right-back Alistair Johnston looks off as it stands.

Hammers approach Vardy

West Ham are among a number of clubs to have approached free agent Jamie Vardy.

The Hammers see the former England man as an option if they fail to prise Troy Parrott from AZ Alkmaar.

Vardy, 39, is determined to take his time over his next move as there was a feeling he rushed a family decision to join Cremonese last year despite the value of the experience.

West Ham are one of several clubs monitoring Jamie Vardy

New Fox Franco

The 27-year-old has signed a three-year contract at the King Power.

Blackpool are signing Middlesbrough defender Finley Munroe on loan.

City running rule over Rulli

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is undergoing a medical at Manchester City after the clubs agreed a £1.75million deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45million.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Araujo completes medical

Ronald Araujo has completed his Liverpool medical ahead of completing a loan move from Barcelona.

The 27-year-old's signing is expected to be announced this afternoon.

The Uruguay defender's loan also includes an option to buy for around £47.1m.

Villa keep tabs on Endrick

Aston Villa are among the growing list of clubs interested in taking Endrick on loan from Real Madrid. The 20-year-old joined Madrid from Palmeiras for £50m in 2024.

Masuaku closes on Turkey move

Sunderland defender Arthur Masuaku is finalising finalise his move to Konyaspor, in Turkey. A deal between the clubs was agreed over the weekend.

Masuaku joined Sunderland last summer and spent the second half of last season on loan at Lens.

Belgian club Mechelen have agreed a deal to sign Sunderland defender Leo Hjelde.

Sunderland are showing interest in Ipswich goalkeeper Alex Palmer.

Sunderland are interested in signing Alex Palmer from Ipswich

The 29-year-old has emerged as an option for Regis Le Bris' side with Anthony Patterson expected to undergo a medical at Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee around £8m.

Palmer is also on Wrexham's radar should a deal for Patterson fall down.

Sunderland face Ipswich on the opening day of the season.

Ipswich are among the clubs interested in Newcastle's Nick Pope.

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Jose Mourinho has made a big mistake with tale that he rejected chance to replace Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United - this is what he accidentally revealed about himself
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho is almost right when he says in a new documentary about his career that it hurts no one to reveal that he reneged on an agreement to join Manchester United in 2013 when he left Real Madrid and went back to Chelsea instead.

Mourinho likes to tell stories of self-aggrandisement that remind us that he was once, long ago, one of the great managers in the game, coveted by all. Back then, those who thought Cristiano Ronaldo was Lionel Messi’s equal also tended to think Mourinho was a match for Pep Guardiola.

Now that he is beginning a second stint in charge of Real Madrid, back in charge of A-list superstars like Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior, he may think it propitious to release details of the fact that he had been chosen to be Sir Alex Ferguson’s heir at Old Trafford.

The news reminds us he was a giant then, rather than the manager who has spent his most recent years as an also-ran at Spurs, Roma and Fenerbahce and was at Benfica last season, where he could only finish a distant third in the Portuguese league behind Porto and Sporting.

The main hope for Real Madrid is that Mourinho has been outmoded for so long that perhaps it is time for his negativity and his cynicism to come back into fashion, now that giants like Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp have left the club stage.

But even if we ignore the fact that Mourinho’s sudden fit of truth-telling casually lets everyone know that David Moyes was not the first choice to succeed Sir Alex at United, there is another person who does not quite escape clean from Mourinho’s revelations and that is him.

Jose Mourinho's revelation that he rejected the Man United job in 2013 reminds us of the man’s fickleness and how, sometimes, a job he takes can go wrong almost before it has started

It also reminds us that now he will have to convince Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Trent Alexander-Arnold and the rest at Madrid that he is not out of his time

Because it lets us know that Mourinho had an agreement to join one of the great clubs of the world and turned his back on it. Sure, it reminds us that he was once in demand but it also reminds us of the man’s fickleness and how, sometimes, a job he takes can go wrong almost before it has started.

It also reminds us that now that he, rather implausibly, has the reins at the Bernabeu, he will have to convince Bellingham, Mbappe, Vinicius, Trent Alexander-Arnold and the rest of the stellar cast at Madrid that he is not a man out of his time, a man who has been overtaken by football and who cannot keep up.

The new Mourinho documentary, which will air on Netflix this week, sheds new light on the conflicts that the manager endured with Ronaldo, Sergio Ramos and, particularly, Iker Casillas during his first spell in Madrid. Many believe those years at the Bernabeu curdled Mourinho’s attitude towards modern players.

It is already evident that he will have work to do to convince Vinicius to believe in him. The Brazilian forward has just signed a new six-year contract but it was only last season when, in the wake of allegations that Vinicius had been racially abused during a Champions League tie between Madrid and Mourinho’s Benfica, Mourinho accused Vinicius of inciting his players with his goal celebrations. Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was among those who criticised Mourinho’s stance.

If Mourinho retains any of the man-management smarts that were once such an integral part of his success, he will make it his mission to win over Bellingham and make the England midfielder his leader and his voice on the pitch.

Bellingham had an outstanding World Cup for England that went far beyond the tirelessness of his performances and his goal contributions. Bellingham already had little to prove to anybody but the tournament in North America was the time he answered every remaining question asked of him.

He proved, above all, that he was a leader, a player who can not only inspire by example but who can carry players with him. He proved that he is continuing to mature with frightening speed and that he is England’s captain in waiting.

Mourinho has made Federico Valverde his captain for the coming season and the Uruguay midfielder is a wonderful player who commands the respect of all. But Bellingham would have been an even better choice. He represents youth and promise and an insatiable hunger to succeed.

It is already evident that Mourinho will have work to do to convince Vinicius to believe in him

If Mourinho retains any of the man-management smarts that were once such an integral part of his success, he will make it his mission to make Bellingham his leader at Real

At a time when Madrid have lost the league twice in a row to Barcelona, Mourinho’s team is crying out for a fresh start. Bellingham symbolises everything they need to succeed and Mourinho’s relationship with him will be the key to whether Madrid can mount a successful challenge to dethrone their Catalan rivals.

If Mourinho retreats into suspicion and cynicism, then Madrid’s season will quickly become a familiar picture of the conflict and intrigue that have dogged so many of the manager’s club tenures. If he embraces the promise and the ambition and verve that Bellingham symbolises, then maybe there is a chance that even Mourinho can enjoy his very own Remontada in Madrid.

Tennis caught in a pickle

Back from nine weeks in the US, I have acquired a fondness for certain American pastimes. Chief among those is a new addiction to pickleball.

Our neighbours in New Hampshire traced out a pickleball court on their drive, bought a net from Walmart and we played every night after dinner. My son and I found a dedicated, thriving, two-storey pickleball club 20 miles away and spent a couple of evenings there, too.

My ambition for the next time I make it to the States is to play on the pickleball courts that spring up on the Wollman Ice Rink in Central Park, New York City in summer.

The surge of popularity of pickleball in the US is not dissimilar to the rise of padel in Europe. Both present a growing challenge to tennis at a time when the sport appears to be gravely lacking in leadership.

Enzo Maresca (right) will need to readjust his sights if he is to survive at Man City. There are a lot of tough jobs in English football but following Pep Guardiola (centre) is the toughest

Maresca's enormous shoes to fill

There is a man in charge at Manchester City now who helped throw more than £1billion against the wall at Chelsea and celebrated finishing fourth in the league by telling anyone who had doubted him to ‘F off’, as if what he had done was a great achievement.

Enzo Maresca will need to readjust his sights if he is to survive at the Etihad Stadium. There are a lot of tough jobs in the top flight of English football but following Pep Guardiola at City is the toughest of all of them.

Any attempt to celebrate finishing anywhere other than at the top of the table will not be viewed kindly by his new paymasters.

Sports.title: UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC presidents accuse Gianni Infantino of 'deception' in open letter demanding FIFA president is held accountable for failed plot to sell the World Cup
Sports.content:
UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC presidents accuse Gianni Infantino of 'deception' in open letter demanding FIFA president is held accountable for failed plot to sell the World Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA has accused under pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino of deception in a joint statement with the football federations of Asia and North and Central America.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs football in the Caribbean, North and Central America, teamed up with UEFA on Monday to attack Infantino over his conduct during the proposed sale of stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup.

The statement said that Infantino had broken trust 'through deception' with the now abandoned proposal, had 'placed himself above the collective' and the three confederations called for a fully independent review of what had happened.

'Football's strength has always been its unity,' the statement concluded. 'We call for that unity to be honored now, for leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it.'

FIFA released a statement on Saturday criticising a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to 'undermine' both the organisation and Infantino.

UEFA announced on Thursday that they will continue to boycott FIFA competitions if Infantino remains at the top of world football after his scandalous plans to sell £3.1billion in World Cup stakes to private investors collapsed. Meanwhile, Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) president Lise Klaveness called for him to resign on Friday.

UEFA (president Aleksander Ceferin, left) has accused under pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino (right) of deception in a joint statement with federations CONCACAF and AFC

Mexico's football federation broke ranks with CONCACAF to come out in support of Infantino, with Argentina, Qatar, Paraguay, Morocco and Egypt among those in favour of him remaining as FIFA president.

Infantino has also faced allegations this week that UEFA made a 'departure payment' to a female employee with whom he is alleged to have been in a relationship while general secretary of European football’s governing body.

UEFA have confirmed a payment was made, but FIFA labelled the allegation as ‘categorically untrue’.

The next FIFA presidential elections take place next March.

Sports.title: Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'
Sports.content:
Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death at the age of just 45.

The Canadian, who was described as 'a respected golfer, devoted son, hilarious brother, and friend,' turned professional in 2003 after playing college golf at Oklahoma State and Georgia.

He later secured his place among golf's elite and went on to compete in 32 PGA Tour events, securing three top-10 finishes as a rookie.

But according to an obituary, he passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada. No cause of death was listed.

'Whether on the course or in everyday life, he had a remarkable ability to bring people together, offering encouragement, laughter, and genuine friendship to everyone he met,' it read, per the Kingston Whig-Standard.

'His welcoming personality and unwavering kindness made him a beloved figure within Kingston's golfing community and beyond.'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death

He passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada

McQuillan's father, Mark, began teaching him how to swing a club at the age of 10 before he went on to reach the Canadian Tour and then the PGA Tour.

'Matt developed lifelong friendships while mentoring anyone who loved the game of golf,' his obituary continued.

'He will be deeply missed by many and his spirit, love and compassion will be remembered every day. Rest easy, Matty. We love you.'

Golf Canada added in a tribute that it 'joins the Canadian golf community in mourning the passing of Matt McQuillan... one of Canada's most promising young golfers in the late 1990s.'

According to the PGA Tour, the 45-year-old returned to his hometown of Kingston, Ontario, to teach golf, 'helping introduce and develop the next generation of Canadian golfers.'

McQuillan's best PGA Tour result came at the 2011 John Deere Classic when he shot a final-round 64 to finish in a tie for third behind winner Steve Stricker.

Sports.content:

Sports.title: T10 proposal is a cry for help from counties who know they're heading for a 'cliff edge' - here's what it reveals about the future for the haves and have nots of the county game, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
T10 proposal is a cry for help from counties who know they're heading for a 'cliff edge' - here's what it reveals about the future for the haves and have nots of the county game, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

The suggestion by the new chairman of Sussex that a T10 competition may be one way of easing the financial concerns of the non-Hundred counties isn't just a sign of the times. It's a cry for help.

The ECB have insisted all along that the funds raised at last year's auction, when the Hundred was valued at £975million, would bankroll domestic red-ball cricket for a generation – an apparently powerful retort to the traditionalists who fear the tournament will devour England's 18-team domestic setup.

But the ECB's narrative does not tell the whole story. Far from it. In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed details of a secret meeting at Northamptonshire's Wantage Road involving nine of the 11 non-Hundred-hosting counties.

The mood was gloomy, with the clubs – almost all of them loss-making – worried about the growing divide between them and the seven host counties, a divide they worry will only grow once the Hundred's private investors demand a greater slice of a new TV deal for 2029, and the best players migrate inevitably to the richest clubs.

And while the non-host counties can in theory access around £25million each following the Hundred windfall, that money has to be spent on projects approved by the ECB, such as paying off structured debt or improving infrastructure.

One source who attended the meeting, held without the knowledge of the ECB, said: 'The feeling was that all the clubs are heading to a cliff edge at various speeds. They will all fall over one after the other if something is not addressed in the short term.'

Sussex are proposing a T10 competition to supposedly help non-Hundred hosting counties

And that is where Ed Warner, the new Sussex chair, comes in. Sussex were one of two non-host counties (along with Durham) to miss the secret meeting, and for good reason: they have spent much of the year trying to unravel the financial mess that led to them being placed in special measures, and docked points in all three county competitions.

After telling The Guardian that the Hundred had 'not rescued us in any way, shape or form', Warner captured the mood that day at Wantage Road by considering ways a non-host county might stage more cricket, and make more money, during the Hundred's nearly month-long duration – a period, at the height of summer and during the school holidays, when clubs are staging only four home Metro Bank 50-over matches.

Warner wondered: 'Why couldn't you have a T10 triangular competition with Kent and Essex, for example? Make it very kid-friendly, make it a day at the seaside, then go and play at Canterbury, then go and play in Chelmsford.'

His suggestion, though not itself discussed at the meeting, deserves full marks for lateral thinking. But it should concern cricket lovers on a few counts.

The first is that it would further complicate an already insane schedule, in which the response to the introduction of a fourth format – the Hundred – has been to stage it at the same time as the 50-over competition, diminishing a format in which England are now international also-rans. Our calendar is already full to bursting, without a fifth format trying to elbow its way in.

The second is that T10 feels like part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom. Yes, Abu Dhabi has been hosting its own T10 tournament since 2017, but it has made headlines mainly for reasons of corruption, both proven and alleged. If the Hundred feels like a hurry, T10 is a sprint. What next: F5, or the toss of a coin?

The third concern, and the most significant, is that Warner felt the need to air the suggestion in the first place.

Forget for a moment the financial incompetence at Hove that last week led business management consultancy firm Campbell Tickell to suggest an overhaul of the Sussex board 'as soon as is practically possible'.

The format would complicate an already insane schedule and be part of cricket's headlong race to the bottom

What matters is that the smaller counties are having to countenance alternative means of paying the bills at a time when the ECB tell us the game is richer than ever.

As one chief executive put it at the Northampton meeting, the promise of Hundred money has generated more uncertainty, not less, because of the unknown impact on the next broadcast rights deal.

The ECB will blanch at the idea of counties coming up with their own fifth-format schemes, since it would entail an admission of failure by the board. But Sussex's T10 musings are the symptom of a wider malaise – no matter the repeated insistence that the Hundred will save English cricket.

Unless the ECB get to grips with the smaller clubs' concerns, there will be more desperate ideas where that one came from.

Sports.title: Tracking private jets, Andrea Berta holding his nerve and a last-ditch plea from Matthias Jaissle: This is how Bruno Guimaraes became an Arsenal player - and why Mikel Arteta was so desperate to get him
Sports.content:
The back-and-forth over whether Arsenal and Newcastle are actually in talks, the plane trackings and the staunch denials in the North East are finally at an end.

Bruno Guimaraes is an Arsenal player, theirs for £75million, and a transfer saga which has dragged on for weeks, much to the entertainment of rival fans, is over. Mikel Arteta has his man, a player he’s long admired and been desperate to sign.

This transfer has been an exhausting process, and far from straightforward. But Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has come out of it looking incredibly shrewd, having pulled off a relative ‘bargain’ in the current climate.

Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal started back in June. As Daily Mail Sport reported on June 24, the Brazilian had instructed agents to find him a new club and Newcastle were braced for an offer from the Gunners. Their interest had been registered.

Newcastle’s response was bullish. He wasn’t going anywhere, according to sources at the club. Given his status as captain and the player’s quality, Guimaraes’ value was enormous – particularly in light of the departures of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. They did not need to sell.

Money talks, however. Newcastle had briefed that they wanted closer to £100million, but internally there was acceptance that an offer of around £75million would see progress.

Bruno Guimaraes has joined Arsenal in a protracted £75million move from Newcastle

The transfer saga is finally over, with Guimaraes' long journey to Arsenal starting back in June

A force of nature.



Guimaraes is a Gunner ✍️ pic.twitter.com/E7k4mIHICg — Arsenal (@Arsenal) August 8, 2026

At Arsenal, they were willing to dig their heels in over the price, in the knowledge that Guimaraes really wanted the move. He had agreed personal terms with the Gunners last month and informed Newcastle of his desire to leave if a suitable offer came in.

There were also optics at play. Newcastle didn’t want to be seen as letting their talisman and a fan favourite leave without putting up a fight. Their fans would rightly have felt aggrieved.

So the negotiations dragged on, largely involving agent Kia Joorabchian. Newcastle would claim there had been no formal contact from Arsenal and felt bewildered by the process, relayed in reports of no direct contact between the clubs.

This conflict in media coverage added to the increasing frenzy attached to a potential move.

Weeks went by, before a real acceleration came last week. As Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday, July 31, a deal had been agreed in principle with a date reserved for the medical. Though a few sticking points remained.

Newly-appointed Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle also decided he wanted a final chance to try to convince the Brazilian to stay put.

Guimaraes travelled to Newcastle’s La Manga training base in Spain on Monday, before waiting for permission to leave and have his medical at Arsenal after telling Jaissle of his desire to move.

The initial reports that he failed to arrive on Sunday resulted in social media sleuths tracking flights to see if Guimaraes was in the air. It had all got a bit mad.

Even the Arsenal players were braced for the move. When Riccardo Calafiori was asked about Guimaraes’ impending transfer on Wednesday night after Arsenal’s 3-1 defeat by Real Betis in Dublin, he turned to the press officer and asked: ‘Is it official yet, no?’

Berta is a tough negotiator. He loathes to overpay, which in this market is extremely hard not to do.

Arsenal had wanted to pay a smaller fee for the Brazil midfielder, who turns 29 in November, while Newcastle demanded a minimum of £80million.

That Arsenal decided to play the long game and stick to their guns frustrated some of their supporters. But the club were never in doubt of the end result.

Newly-appointed manager Matthias Jaissle made a last ditch plea to persuade him to stay

Arsenal chief Andrea Berta held his nerve on the transfer fee throughout negotiations

It’s a smart deal in a market which has, as one agent claimed, ‘gone out of control’. As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, even kids as young as 16 are being paid £20,000 a week, as in the case of Man City’s Mishel Nduka.

In the senior ranks, Chelsea bought Morgan Rogers for £117million, while Spurs splashed out £100million on Tonali.

The strategy of Arsenal and Berta has paid off - after they walked away from Rogers because their valuation of the player had been far exceeded.

The deal for Guimaraes represents value for money - and it is one Berta deserves credit for.

An Arsenal midfield, which was already dominant, now looks even more menacing. Alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, Guimaraes completes a formidable trio.

Rice provides the ability to cover acres of space, while also being a threat going forward and strong defensively. Odegaard is in charge of creating chances in the final third.

Guimaraes, meanwhile, is an all-round No 8 who can affect games at both ends of the pitch, and brings an aggressive edge. His attempts at more ambitious passes will add some unpredictability the Gunners lack at times.

And so, after weeks of twists, denials and negotiations behind the scenes, the saga is finally over. Guimaraes is an Arsenal player – and Newcastle’s fight to keep their captain has achieved nothing more than a sizeable cheque.

Sports.title: Former Premier League bad boy Nile Ranger claims he got into a fight with Andros Townsend on England duty after the ex-Crystal Palace star 'spat in his pasta'
Sports.content:
Nile Ranger has claimed he and Andros Townsend were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty.

Despite never representing the Three Lions at senior level, Ranger scored six goals in 11 appearances for England's U19s after bursting on to the scene as a teenager.

The former Newcastle prodigy, 35, revealed on a podcast this week that he once clashed with fellow ex-England youth star Townsend while the pair were sharing a room in Ukraine on international duty.

'He wasn't playing and getting in the team at the time, but he's a man where he's stretching at night time and keeping himself ready,' Ranger told Undr the Cosh.

'I've played but I didn't play the best. And I'm like to Andros, "Look, just go to sleep man, just relax. You're stretching and doing all of this but your chance will come". I'm actually genuinely telling him that, I'm being real.

'He's like, "You what? Did you see how you played today? You had a stinker, I don't want to play like that. I've got to make sure I'm stretched out and ready".

Ex-Newcastle star Nile Ranger (left) has claimed he and Andros Townsend (right) were involved in a heated altercation while representing England as youngsters on international duty

The forward was once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest prospects as a teenager

'I don't know why he was coming at me. Take your anger out on someone else bro because I'm not the one. I'll just knock you out and then it's just long (not worth it).

'Anyway, we go down for food the next day and, you remember those old-school blue Lucozade bottles with the yellow top, he's drinking from it and he's spitting in my pasta. I'm looking around at players and being like - are you witnessing this as well? This is crazy antics right now.'

Continuing the anecdote, Ranger claims he and Townsend went upstairs and started brawling, surrounded by team-mates including former England international Kyle Walker.

'I can see Andros there, I'm on to Andros, and I've just crashed him,' Ranger added, making a punching gesture. 'His head hits the bin and man are trying to stop me, Kyle Walker trying to stop me, but the rage inside is just going mad, going berserk.

'We got split up, he's gone to his room. I don't know if the coaches found out about it but I've gone back later and he's like, "Look, let me stop you, I'm sorry. I think just being out here is getting to me and what not".

'I know how it feels. It's like when you get an injury or something and you're not playing. Or you feel like you can play and aren't getting the chance. It was just anger built up, that sort of thing.'

After off-field issues derailed his career, he ended up playing for a string of non league clubs

🚨 NEW SERIES OUT TOMORROW 🚨



Nile Ranger looks back on clashing with Andros Townsend while on England U19s duty 🥊 pic.twitter.com/LcqRCA5Q2n — UndrTheCosh (@UndrTheCosh) August 9, 2026

Once regarded as one of Newcastle's brightest young prospects, Ranger's off-field behaviour repeatedly overshadowed and ultimately derailed his career.

As a teenager, he spent time in a young offenders’ institution following an armed robbery, and his early professional years were subsequently punctuated by disciplinary problems and run-ins with the law.

After Newcastle opted not to renew his contract in 2013 after a string of off-pitch controversies, Ranger moved to Swindon Town before spells at Blackpool and Southend United.

He took a two-year break from football in 2018 following further run-ins with the law. Since returning in 2020, he has bounced between several non-league clubs, starting with Spalding United before brief spells at Southend, Boreham Wood, Kettering Town, Wellingborough Town and Chatham Town.

Once again a free agent this summer, the striker left Chatham Town at the end of last season after scoring six goals in 14 appearances for the club.

Ranger has also spoken openly in the past about his struggles with gambling addiction. In a 2023 interview, he claimed that, had he behaved better off the pitch and maintained a healthier lifestyle, he could have been as prolific as Manchester City's goal machine Erling Haaland.

Sports.title: Man Utd can finalise eight transfers this week including £89m of talent arriving
Sports.content:
Man Utd can finalise eight transfers this week including £89m of talent arriving

Manchester United are reportedly looking to strengthen their squad further in the summer transfer window, with nuerous high-profile stars linked with moves to Old Trafford

View 5 Images Marcus Rashford's Manchester United future remains up in the air on the cusp of the new season (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

It has been a busy summer at Old Trafford, with Manchester United making their mark on the summer transfer window and showing no signs of slowing down. Michael Carrick's men are preparing for life back in the Champions League next season and the manager knows a deeper squad will be essential if they are to compete on all fronts.

The arrivals of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos has set the tone for what looks like a significant midfield rebuild at the club. Karl Darlow has also come through the door to provide experienced cover for Senne Lammens between the sticks and a clutch of younger players have been brought in with one eye firmly on the future.

On the other side of the ledger, goalkeeper Radek Vitek has headed to Middlesbrough on a permanent basis and there is a sense further names could follow him before the window slams shut on September 1. With that in mind, Mirror Football takes a look at eight transfers United could realistically get over the line this week.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford

Marcus Rashford could be handed a fresh opportunity to secure a return to Barcelona as Ferran Torres edges closer to joining PSG. The United forward spent last season with the Catalan giants, who chose not to activate their £26million purchase option for the loanee.

Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future READ MORE :

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Barcelona's decision to offload Torres might open the door for the club to renew their pursuit of Rashford. Nevertheless, United manager Michael Carrick has discussed having the England international in his plans.

"I've played with him. I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history," said the United coach. "We have a full squad next week in Dublin.

"We fly straight there and meet Leeds on Wednesday. We have a few days in Dublin where we have the whole squad, including Marcus, Kobbie and Lisandro."

Jorge Salinas

View 5 Images Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas could be a budget-friendly option to improve United's left-back options (Image: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas could prove to be an astute acquisition for Carrick's side. The 19-year-old left-back is regarded as a highly promising talent and would provide United with a long-term plan to succeed Luke Shaw, though the club face competition from Barcelona.

Racing Santander sporting director Chema Aragon has made abundantly clear that the club will not entertain offers below his £13.7m release clause, adding: "There is nothing we can do if a big star appears."

Sky broadcasts more than 1,400 live matches across the Premier League, EFL and more with at least 215 live from the top flight alongside Formula 1, darts and golf.

Harry Amass, Dan Gore and Toby Collyer

United are believed to be receptive to bids for the academy trio as Carrick continues his overhaul. It emerged last month that the club would entertain either loan or permanent transfers for left-back Harry Amass and midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer.

Collyer, 22, enjoyed loan stints at West Bromwich Albion and Hull City last season, while Gore, 21, had a spell at Rotherham United. Amass, 19, was likewise sent out on loan to Sheffield Wednesday last summer before picking up an injury shortly after linking up with Norwich City in January.

Manu Kone

View 5 Images Reports earlier this summer suggested United have already agreed terms with Roma's Manu Kone (Image: Pablo Morano/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

Roma midfielder Manu Kone has been strongly linked with a switch to Old Trafford this summer. The Reds are said to be pursuing a third midfielder for their ranks and the France international, who impressed at the World Cup, has surfaced as a potential target.

Corriere dello Sport previously reported United had reached personal terms with the 25-year-old. Roma are understood to be demanding up to £51m (€60m) for the midfielder.

Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Brighton's Carlos Baleba are among the numerous other names to have been linked with reinforcing United's midfield. Nevertheless, the club could opt to conclude their engine-room makeover by sealing a deal for Kone.

Jhon Lucumi

View 5 Images Bologna defender Jhon Lucumi has a number of Premier League suitors linked with his signature (Image: LightRocket via Getty Images)

Bologna defender Jhon Lucumi could help shore up United's defensive line as speculation over his departure continues to mount. The Colombia international, who also featured at the World Cup, is reportedly keen on joining a "big club" this summer after attracting attention from a number of sides.

That's according to Quotidiano Sportivo, which claims Bologna are holding out for £21.4m (€25million) plus £2.6m (€3m) in add-ons. Juventus are said to have tabled two offers below that asking price.

Several other clubs, including Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest, are also understood to be keeping tabs on the defender. However, Lucumi's reported ambition to join a major club could hand United a significant edge in the pursuit of his signature.

Joshua Zirkzee

View 5 Images Joshua Zirkzee continues to be linked with a move back to Italy (Image: David Lidstrom/Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee has been the subject of exit speculation throughout the summer window. The Dutch forward has struggled to secure a regular place in the team since his arrival from Bologna in 2024.

Zirkzee has been touted for a potential loan to Juventus, with the attacker said to be receptive to the switch. Yet United's present shortage of centre-forward options beyond Benjamin Sesko could postpone any prospective departure.

Sports.title: Arsenal outline Gabriel Martinelli transfer stance as new club eyes Gabriel Jesus
Sports.content:
Arsenal outline Gabriel Martinelli transfer stance as new club eyes Gabriel Jesus

Arsenal's Brazilian forwards Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are both attracting transfer interest and could yet depart before the September 1 deadline

View 2 Images Clubs in Italy and Turkey are eyeing Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus

Roma have held initial talks with Gabriel Martinelli's representatives Roc Nation Sports.

‌



The Arsenal winger is facing an uncertain future with the Premier League champions, though it's still not considered a formality that he will depart the club this summer.

‌



Martinelli has one year remaining on his current deal with the Gunners, however, Arsenal also hold a one-year extension option they can trigger to protect his value.

‌



Had Mikel Arteta's side succeeded in their pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior, Martinelli would have been virtually certain to depart the Emirates Stadium before the transfer deadline.

Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss READ MORE :

OPINION Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat by Ryan Taylor

Now, the situation is complicated by the lack of top-quality replacement options and the Arsenal hierarchy will only make changes to Arteta's playing squad if there is scope to improve the Spaniard's ranks.

‌



Bradley Barcola was watched in-person at the World Cup with France but PSG's £145million price-tag is viewed as excessive. Liverpool are also believed to be his preferred destination of choice after contract talks with PSG stalled.

Additionally, Roma, who are determined to land a right-footed left-winger, would struggle to match Martinelli's current salary while also satisfying Arsenal's financial valuation.

Galatasaray are also keen as they view the 25-year-old as an alternative to AC Milan's Rafael Leao. Negotiations with Milan have proven problematic as their latest proposal, a loan-to-buy, worth a reported £30m was rebuffed by the Italian giants. Milan aren't interested in a loan.

‌



If they are unwilling to stretch much further for Leao, Gala would also find it tough to get close to what Arsenal would perceive to be a viable offer for Martinelli, who is keen to stay with the Premier League winners and is also liked by Fenerbahce.

New signing Christos Tzolis currently looks to be ahead of Martinelli in the Arsenal pecking order following the sale of Leandro Trossard to Besiktas after registering four goal involvements (three assists, one goal) in four pre-season appearances.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli would ideally like to remain at Arsenal (Image: Getty)

‌



Meanwhile, Napoli have emerged as frontrunners to sign Brazilian centre-forward Gabriel Jesus, who is available for transfer. His valuation was initially set at £20m earlier this summer but offers upwards of £15m would likely be considered.

The Serie A outfit are seeking to move Romelu Lukaku on and Jesus' agent Giovanni Branchini recently attended Napoli's training camp, though he has since clarified he was visiting Massimiliano Allegri. If Napoli can find a buyer for Lukaku, they will bid for Jesus.

Turkish side Besiktas also have Jesus among their list of targets if they fail to execute a deal for Dusan Vlahovic, who is a free agent after departing Juventus. Negotiations with the Serbian frontman are ongoing.

Article continues below

Jesus' Arsenal contract expires in 2027 and he is keen to stay inside Europe's top-five leagues despite being the subject of interest from numerous clubs back in his homeland of Brazil.
