World.title: ANALYSIS: Osun 2026: Rauf Aregbesola, ADC’s litmus test
World.content:
On Saturday, 2,339,233 eligible voters, according to the updated final voter register presented by INEC, will file out across 332 wards in the 30 local government areas of Osun State to elect a new governor.

The voters, spread across 3,763 polling units, have a choice to either re-elect incumbent governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party (AP) or choose another from the pool of candidates fielded by the All Progressives Congress (APC), the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP), and 10 others.

In all, 14 political parties are participating in the election.

Although on the surface, the governorship tussle seems to be a two-horse race between Mr Adeleke and Bola Oyebamiji of the APC, a third dark horse is lurking in the corner: the ADC’s flagbearer. The ADC is considered by many in the state as the third force, given the status and relevance of its major backer in the state, Rauf Aregbesola, who governed the state between 2010 and 2018, first on the platform of the defunct ACN, and then the APC, which he helped found in 2013.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Aregbesola was a pillar of the APC in Osun State until a bitter struggle for the control of the party in the state with his successor, Gboyega Oyetola, on one hand, and his estranged political godfather, President Bola Tinubu, on the other hand, made him part ways with the party in July 2025, before emerging as the national secretary of the ADC. By the way, Mr Aregbesola continues to claim that he and his supporters were forced out of the APC in the state.

According to some political observers in the state, the rift between Messrs Aregbesola and Oyetola was one of the significant factors that contributed to the latter’s loss in the 2022 gubernatorial election to Mr Adeleke of the PDP, now of the AP.

They contended that had they reconciled ahead of the election, it might have been difficult for the PDP to dislodge the APC from retaining the governorship seat of the state.

Be that as it may, the 2026 election will be a litmus test on Mr Aregbesola’s political influence in Osun State and more or less on the ADC ahead of the general elections in 2027. This is so because there will be no major election in the country again in 2026 to qualitatively assess the strength of the party before the general elections.

The performance of the ADC in the recent Ekiti governorship election was subpar, despite party leaders, including Mr Aregbesola, David Mark and Atiku Abubakar, visiting the state to campaign for its candidate, Dare Bejide. Mr Bejide polled 12,872 votes to come a distant third, behind the PDP’s Oluwole Oluyede and APC’s Abiodun Oyebanji, who emerged as the winner with 319,224 votes, according to the results released by INEC.

Before the Ekiti governorship election, the ADC did not win in any of the bye-elections conducted by INEC in August 2025. Four parties dominated the results: APC won 12 constituencies, APGA won 2, PDP won 1, and NNPP won 1.

The ADC did not win any constituency.

Some commentators attributed the party’s poor showing in the elections to its relative newness, having been adopted by some opposition elements only recently as the platform to confront the APC-led national government.

If the ADC was emerging from a prolonged hibernation in the August 2025 bye-elections, some observers felt it should have done better, having gained some mileage within the country’s political nautical miles in 2026, and hence must be able to amass some political fortune in the elections held so far in the year.

Contrary to these observers’ expectations, the results from the bye-elections again showed a party yet to gain the momentum it needs before 2027. The party failed to win any of the bye-elections held in June across six states, including the Dawakin Kudu/Warawa Federal Constituency bye-election in Kano State (2026), which the APC won.

In the February FCT Area Council election, the ADC also failed to make a good showing. The APC won five of the six area councils, namely AMAC, Bwari, Kuje, Abaji and Kwali, while the PDP got Gwagwalada, leaving ADC with none.

The party’s below-par performance in the 2025/2026 elections held so far is why the Osun election will be a major test of its strength. It has to demonstrate that it is capable of challenging for power to get the buy-in of the Nigerian electorate.

Ahead of the election, the dominant question on the lips of many people is: Does Mr Aregbesola have the mettle and reach to deliver Osun State to the ADC?

Yet another question closely related to the first: Does the ADC have the name recognition to win the coveted seat in the state?

The preponderant response to the first question is that it would be a tall order for Mr Aregbesola to deliver the state to the ADC because his political strength has waned considerably, against his recurring claim that he enjoys the goodwill of voters of the state and that they will deliver their votes to his new party – the ADC.

For the second question, the ADC in Osun is Mr Aregbesola; Mr Aregbesola is the ADC in the state. Whatever happens to one also happens to the other. For now, they are two identical and inseparable twins.

The perceived diminishing return in Mr Aregbesola’s political net worth in the state, some local commentators said, is significantly tied to his parting ways with the ‘progressive family’ and Mr Tinubu, with whom he was a political associate for over three decades. The APC claims to be the party of the progressive family in the state.

Mr Aregbesola’s perceived waning political capital in the state aside, the ADC does not have strong institutional support, organisational depth, mass appeal and the financial clout the likes of AP and the APC enjoy in the state, which are key determinants that drive election victory or loss, as the case may be.

The ADC’s choice of candidate – Najeem Salaam- also created a mess that the party has not been able to clean up completely. Moshood Adeoti, a grassroots politician with supporters across the state, was initially thought to be favoured by Mr Aregbesola to fly the ticket, until the pendulum swung in favour of Mr Salaam, a former speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly and ex-lawmaker representing Ede North/Ede South/Egbedore/Ejigbo Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives.

Mr Adeoti, popularly known as ‘Sheu’, has since distanced himself from the ADC and also broken ranks with Mr Aregbesola. The former Secretary to the State Government was the SDP candidate in the 2022 governorship election. He defected to the SDP after losing the APC ticket to then-incumbent Mr Oyetola. Mr Adeoti enjoyed Mr Aregbesola’s support in the election because of his fallout with Mr Oyetola.

Mr Salaam is from Ejigbo in the same senatorial district – Osun West- as Governor Adeleke, who is believed to be enjoying massive home support, plus the well-oiled Adeleke political dynasty domiciled in Ede, the governor’s hometown, but with tentacles across the state. It would be a Herculean task for the former speaker and, by extension, the ADC, to torpedo Mr Adeleke in the district in Saturday’s election. It is believed that voters in Osun East and Central would prefer to vote for Mr Adeleke, who has another four years to serve if re-elected, rather than Mr Salaam, who is constitutionally entitled to two terms of eight years, assuming he wins, so that gubernatorial power can shift to the other districts.

However, Mr Aregbesola’s diehard loyalists, who are spread across the state, believe it will be political hubris for the AP and the APC to deny his influence in the state where he was governor for eight years, with an extensive grassroots network of foot soldiers who are always ready to do his political bidding, come rain, come shine.

For Mr Aregbesola, Nigeria’s immediate past interior minister, the 15 August election is another chance to prove to his detractors, cynics and adversaries that he remains a political force in Osun State.

For his part, Mr Aregbesola is not shy to flaunt his political credentials and those of the ADC. “We are the main, principal and only political force in Osun and in Nigeria,” he said at a rally.

One way to prove this and silence his critics is to deliver Mr Salaam on Saturday as the next occupant of the Bola Ige House in Osogbo, the state capital. Otherwise, a poor showing at the election may well eclipse his political star in the state he once governed.

The challenge is clear for the ADC, too: win Osun and send a signal to the rest of the country that it is battle-ready against the APC at the national level in 2027. A loss in the election may altogether erase its seemingly marginal chances.

World.title: Kaduna 2027: Uba Sani, Ashiru, La’ah in new political battles
World.content:
The 2027 election season is entering a new phase, and in Kaduna State, the political battle is already taking shape.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has fixed 19 August for the commencement of campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while campaigns for governorship and State House of Assembly elections will begin on 9 September 2026. The governorship election will hold on 6 February 2027, with campaigns ending 24 hours earlier.

For Kaduna, the countdown has added urgency to an already fluid contest.

Governor Uba Sani of the All Progressives Congress (APC) is seeking a second term against a familiar challenger, Isah Ashiru of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), while former senator Danjuma La’ah has emerged on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The three men represent different political calculations.

Governor Sani enters the race with incumbency, government machinery, federal alignment and an increasingly dominant APC structure.

Mr Ashiru has statewide name recognition, two previous governorship campaigns and a substantial political network.

Mr La’ah brings two terms in the Senate, a strong Southern Kaduna identity and a powerful argument that the governorship should now go to Kaduna South.

But the biggest question may be whether the opposition can turn its combined strength into a single electoral force.

New phase in Kaduna politics

Kaduna has always been politically complex. Its three senatorial zones have distinctive political identities, while religion, ethnicity, geography, insecurity and longstanding regional grievances influence political behaviour.

But perhaps the most important feature of Kaduna politics is that alliances rarely remain permanent. The current contest illustrates that perfectly.

Mr Sani was once closely associated with former Governor Nasir El-Rufai. He succeeded activist politician Shehu Sani as senator for Kaduna Central and later became former governor El- Rufai’s preferred successor in 2023.

Today, the two are political opponents.

Mr El-Rufai has since left the APC for the ADC, while elements of his political network have increasingly aligned with Mr Ashiru.

That development has transformed the political calculations for the 2027 election.

Mr Sani and the advantage of incumbency

Governor Sani remains the candidate with the strongest institutional advantage.

He controls the government machinery and leads a ruling party that has expanded its influence considerably since 2023.

He also secured the APC governorship ticket unchallenged, receiving 459,393 affirmation votes at the party primary.

More importantly, the governor has succeeded in attracting politicians from outside the APC.

Former governor Ramalan Yero, former senators Shehu Sani and Suleiman Hunkuyi, among others, moved into the APC camp in 2025. Mr La’ah was also among those who joined the ruling party before eventually leaving it for the NDC.

Twelve opposition lawmakers subsequently defected to the APC, further strengthening the ruling party’s structure in the state.

The significance is not merely numerical.

Mr Sani is building a political machine that reaches beyond traditional APC supporters.

But the governor’s strength also presents a possible vulnerability.

A dominant ruling party can become complacent, particularly when politicians begin to assume that victory is inevitable. Opposition parties will attempt to turn that confidence into an argument for change.

Ashiru: The familiar challenger

For Mr Ashiru, 2027 represents another attempt to reach Sir Kashim Ibrahim House.

He contested the governorship in 2019 against El-Rufai and again in 2023 against Mr Sani.

His second-place finish in 2023 demonstrated that he has a substantial statewide following.

His move to the ADC has also placed him at the centre of the broader opposition realignment.

The emergence of Mr El-Rufai within the ADC has created an unusual political situation.

Mr Ashiru once campaigned against Mr El-Rufai.

Now, elements of the former governor’s political network are sympathetic to his candidacy.

Bashir El-Rufai’s public support for Mr Ashiru after the ADC primary reinforced speculation about the new alignment.

But Mr Ashiru also faces a difficult question: this is his third attempt.

The ADC must therefore convince voters that 2027 is different from 2019 and 2023.

The party must also resolve internal disagreements surrounding its governorship primary, which have already raised questions about cohesion.

The El-Rufai factor

No discussion of Kaduna 2027 can ignore Mr El-Rufai.

The former governor built one of the state’s most formidable political structures during his eight years in office.

His break with his successor, Mr Sani, has consequently become more than a personal disagreement.

It has become part of the larger political struggle over who controls Kaduna’s future.

The feud has involved disputes over governance, finances and insecurity.

Mr El-Rufai has criticised aspects of Mr Sani’s approach to banditry, while the governor has defended his combination of security operations, dialogue and socio-economic interventions in tackling the menace.

Mr Sani has argued that insecurity cannot be defeated through military force alone.

That disagreement could become a campaign issue.

For the opposition, Mr El-Rufai’s political influence is potentially valuable. But it is also a double-edged sword.

Too much association with the former governor could help mobilise his supporters while simultaneously reviving memories of controversies surrounding his administration.

MrbAshiru will therefore need to benefit from the El-Rufai network without allowing the election to become simply another referendum on Mr El-Rufai.

La’ah and the Southern Kaduna calculation

Danjuma La’ah has introduced a different dimension into the race.

A former two-term senator representing Kaduna South, he remains a significant political figure in Southern Kaduna.

His political journey has also been unusually fluid.

He once opposed Mr El-Rufai’s administration in the Senate, later joined the APC under Uba Sani and subsequently left after losing the APC senatorial primary.

He is now seeking the governorship under the NDC. His central argument is one of political rotation.

Mr La’ah says Kaduna North has produced governors including Namadi Sambo, Ramalan Yero and Mr El-Rufai, while Uba Sani comes from Kaduna Central.

Southern Kaduna, he argues, should now produce the governor.

That message could resonate strongly in the region. But winning Kaduna requires more than Southern Kaduna votes.

Mr La’ah must demonstrate that he can build support in Kaduna North and Central districts and become a statewide candidate rather than a regional one.

The third-force problem

Mr La’ah’s emergence could be decisive even if he does not win.

The question is whether he will divide the anti-APC vote.

Mr Ashiru has an established statewide base.

Mr La’ah has a potentially strong Southern Kaduna constituency. Both could attract voters dissatisfied with APC.

If they remain separate, Governor Sani could benefit from the fragmentation.

That is the central arithmetic of the election.

The opposition does not necessarily need to become more popular than APC. It needs to become more coordinated.

Insecurity remains the biggest issue

Security will almost certainly dominate the campaign.

Kaduna has suffered years of banditry, kidnapping and communal violence.

Mr Sani’s administration can point to security initiatives, negotiations that helped secure the release of abducted residents and efforts to reopen access to farms and communities.

But attacks have continued.

Recent killings and abductions in Birnin Gwari and other parts of the state demonstrate that insecurity remains a daily concern for many rural communities.

The political argument will therefore be straightforward.

The government will say the situation has improved and that its strategy is producing results. The opposition will argue that improvement is insufficient while farmers remain afraid to access their farms and travellers remain vulnerable.

For a farmer, the issue is unlikely to be theoretical:

Can I leave home, go to my farm and return safely?

That question could matter more than any campaign slogan.

The cost of living and everyday governance

Security is not the only issue.

Residents are also dealing with housing costs, unemployment, water shortages and the broader cost-of-living crisis.

These issues will test Governor Sani’s development narrative.

The administration can point to infrastructure, healthcare, water-sector investments and other programmes.

The opposition can ask whether those investments are translating into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Kaduna residents.

The priorities of a civil servant in Kaduna metropolis may differ significantly from those of a farmer in Birnin Gwari or a trader in Southern Kaduna. That makes a statewide campaign especially difficult.

What Kaduna voters are saying

Ordinary Kaduna residents who spoke to PREMIUM TIMES complained of also dealing with the consequences of inflation, unemployment, housing costs and access to basic services.

PREMIUM TIMES has reported rising rents in Kaduna metropolis, with residents complaining about sharp increases that have made housing increasingly difficult for low- and middle-income families.

Water supply remains another concern in the state

These issues could weaken the government’s development narrative if voters feel that large infrastructure investments have not sufficiently translated into improvements in household welfare.

There is currently no credible statewide opinion poll establishing a clear favourite.

Mr Sani himself has warned against confusing social-media popularity with electoral strength.

He argued that a candidate could lose on social media and still win at the polling units, stressing that the real test is grassroots mobilisation.

That is particularly important in Kaduna.

The election will ultimately be fought at ward and polling-unit level.

The ability to recruit agents, mobilise voters, reach rural communities and protect the vote may matter more than online popularity.

Mr Ashiru’s previous campaigns give him an advantage in this area.

The APC’s established structure gives Governor Sani an even larger one. Mr La’ ah of the ADC must now build one of his own.

APC’s power and its limits

The APC currently has the stronger political machinery.

It has incumbency, federal backing, lawmakers, local structures and a growing network of former opposition politicians.

But political dominance does not automatically guarantee voter loyalty.

Mr Ashiru’s evolution from Mr El-Rufai’s opponent into a politician who could benefit from sections of the former governor’s political network is perhaps the clearest example of Kaduna’s changing political geometry.

The campaign officially begins, but the real contest has started

INEC’s revised timetable gives the parties a clear electoral clock.

Presidential and National Assembly campaigns begin on 19 August, while Kaduna’s governorship campaign officially opens on 9 September.

Campaigns must end 24 hours before polling day, with the final day for governorship campaigning fixed for 4 February 2027. The governorship election follows on 6 February.

That compressed timetable means candidates cannot afford prolonged internal disputes.

For APC, the task is to maintain cohesion and convince voters that Governor Sani deserves another four years.

For ADC, the priority is to consolidate behind Mr Ashiru and resolve its internal questions.

For NDC, the immediate challenge is to settle the dispute surrounding its governorship ticket and give La’ah a stable platform.

World.title: Mass burial for 15 Benue attack victims as farmers face bandits’ levies
World.content:
Fifteen people killed in Efeyi-Utikpi, Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue State, have been given a .mass burial amid grief and renewed calls for stronger security in the state’s rural communities.

The victims, including women and children, were killed on 28 July when suspected armed herders attacked the farming community in the Ugboju District.

According to AIT, which reported the mass burial on Sunday, residents gathered in Efeyi-Utikpi to lay the victims to rest, weeks after a similar attack in the same local government area.

The report said the attack left homes destroyed and residents traumatised, with community leaders urging the federal and state governments to move beyond condemnations and provide effective protection for vulnerable farming communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A representative of Equipping the Persecuted, a United States-based non-governmental organisation, reportedly announced financial assistance for the bereaved families and local vigilante groups.

The burial came less than three weeks after another attack in Otukpo-Nobi, where eight victims were buried following an assault on the community on 12 July.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that police confirmed the attack, saying five adults and three children were killed.

The Commissioner of Police in Benue, Cletus Nwadiogbu, described the incident as a terrorist attack and said the attackers used guerrilla tactics before fleeing into nearby forests.

The attacks have continued to raise concerns over the safety of farmers in Benue, where insecurity has disrupted agricultural activities and displaced residents from their ancestral communities.

Farmers under siege

In a related development, a farmer in Mbagena Council Ward of Katsina-Ala Local Government Area has reportedly abandoned his farm after suspected local bandits demanded N500,000 before allowing him to harvest his crops.

The farmer’s son, John James, disclosed this at a capacity-building workshop on promoting safety, security, rights, accountability and access to justice organised by the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project in Makurdi.

Mr James said armed men invaded his father’s home about two weeks ago and demanded the money, threatening him after he pleaded for more time.

According to him, the bandits later abducted his mother after his father failed to meet the initial deadline.

“They charged him to pay a ransom of N500,000. My father pleaded with them because there was nothing at the moment. He had to plead with them for our lives because contacting the security will only worsen the situation,” Mr James said.

ALSO READ: Suspected herders kill 14 in another Benue attack

He said his father eventually paid N200,000 and was allowed to harvest part of his groundnut, beniseed and soybean crops, but the attackers demanded another N300,000 before he could harvest the remaining produce.

Mr James said his father subsequently fled the community, leaving his farm produce behind.

“These people are moving freely in our vicinity, and they are local bandits. In fact, some of them are known to the villagers because they are from the same community,” he said.

He added that other farmers had suffered similar attacks and that residents were reluctant to report the incidents to the police for fear of reprisals.

The development highlights the growing security challenges confronting farmers in Benue, where attacks have repeatedly disrupted farming and forced residents to abandon their communities.

On 17 July, troops of Operation Whirl Stroke reported rescuing three kidnapped victims during an operation in Katsina-Ala Local Government Area.

The troops said they neutralised two suspected terrorists and recovered firearms and ammunition from a hideout.

The renewed attacks also followed the killing of the Benue chairman of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, Risku Mohammed, on 26 June, which residents have linked to subsequent reprisal attacks in parts of Benue South.

The Benue State Government has repeatedly directed security agencies to intensify operations in affected communities, while Governor Hyacinth Alia has called for the safe return of displaced residents to their ancestral homes.

The latest mass burial and reported farm levies underscore the continuing difficulty faced by rural communities trying to farm amid persistent insecurity.

World.title: “I’ve never slept with another woman since I married my wife,” — Aregbesola (VIDEO)
World.content:
The National Secretary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rauf Aregbesola, has disclosed that he has never had sexual relations with another woman since marrying his wife, Sherifat, in 1983.

The former Osun governor made the disclosure while campaigning for the ADC governorship candidate, Najeem Salaam, in Ejigbo Local Government Area ahead of the state’s 15 August governorship election.

Speaking in Yoruba, the 69-year-old invoked his marital fidelity as an act motivated by his fear of God and prayed that, on that basis, the ADC would occupy the Osun Government House after the election.

“Since I got married to my wife, because of the fear of Allah, I have never had intimacy with another. I told God, if I did this because of you, next June, we must do it at the Government House,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Aregbesola married Sherifat in 1983, two years after meeting her on Ibrahim Taiwo Road in Tudun-Wada, Kaduna. The couple have been married for about 43 years.

The declaration comes as Mr Aregbesola campaigns to return to the Osun Government House politically under a different platform. He governed the state from 2010 to 2018 and later served as Minister of Interior under the APC-led federal government before emerging as National Secretary of the ADC.

‘Angel’

Mr Aregbesola added that not every man could make such a commitment. “Allah, if it is truly I am serving you and I did not add anything else to it, what I am about to say, only a few men can say.”

While celebrating his wife’s 60th birthday in 2020, Mr Aregbesola described her as a resourceful mother to their children and a worthy matriarch of the family.

He added that, over the years, his wife had been an angel who came into his life in 1981, whom he married in 1983, and whose love had remained total and unquenchable.

According to him, Sherifat was tailor-made for him, noting that the feeling was mutual and that she had been a worthy companion and source of support throughout his journey through life.

Mr Aregbesola said she had filled him with laughter and joy, adding that she was worth more to him than the entire world.

, , – @raufaregbesola

Some people may find it very difficult to believe this pic.twitter.com/m1AV7E6DMh — (@AdabanijaQomaru) August 9, 2026

“Protect your votes”

Mr Aregbesola further urged citizens to protect their votes at the rally, which coincided with the 61st birthday of the ADC governorship candidate, Najeem Salaam.

He added that Mr Salaam’s candidacy represents both the continuity the state needs and the renewal it deserves.

“Yesterday, we were in Ejigbo to celebrate the 61st birthday anniversary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, Dr Najeem Folasayo Salaam, alongside the people of Ejigbo, who came out en masse to receive us.

“I joined the Deputy Governorship Candidate, Mrs Temitope Agiri, and other leaders of our great party in encouraging our supporters and the good people of Ejigbo to come out in their numbers to exercise their democratic rights, vote for our candidate and, importantly, protect their votes”, he wrote on his X page.

Mr Aregbesola said the party’s candidate represents the true heirs of late Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive tradition, which promotes quality education, accessible healthcare, social welfare and opportunities for the masses.

The state governorship election is scheduled for 15 August, with Mr Salaam set to face Ademola Adeleke of the Accord Party, who is seeking re-election, as well as Bola Oyebamiji of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other candidates.

World.title: Akwa Ibom budgets N26.91bn for hotel renovation, temporarily shuts down facility
World.content:
The Akwa Ibom State Government has budgeted a total of N26.91 billion for refurbishing, furnishing, and renovating the electrical and mechanical facilities at the Ibom Hotel and Golf Resort in Uyo between 2025 and 2026.

This insight into the budgetary provisions for the project follows the state government’s announcement of the hotel’s temporary closure from 22 August to allow for the completion of ongoing renovation works and the repositioning of the facility under a new management company.

The government announced the closure on Saturday in a public notice signed by the Commissioner for Information, Aniekan Umanah, and the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Anieti Udofia.

The hotel, one of the state’s major tourism assets built about 19 years ago by the administration of former governor Victor Attah, has been undergoing rehabilitation since March 2025.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Despite the billions of naira allocated to the project, the state government has not publicly disclosed the total cost of the rehabilitation, the amount already spent, the contractor handling the works or when the renovation is expected to be completed.

Budget breakdown

A check of Akwa Ibom State’s 2026 approved budget and 2025 revised budget shows that the state government allocated N10 billion in its 2025 budget for the “Refurbishing and Furnishing of Ibom Hotels and Golf Resort”.

It also provided N6 billion in the same year for the “Renovation of Electrical and Mechanical Facilities of Ibom Hotel and Golf Resort”.

The two provisions brought the 2025 budget allocation for the hotel’s renovation to N16 billion.

In the 2026 budget, the state reduced the allocation for refurbishing and furnishing the hotel to N7.32 billion. Another N3.59 billion was allocated for the renovation of its electrical and mechanical facilities.

The two provisions amount to N10.91 billion in 2026.

When the 2025 and 2026 allocations are combined, the state has budgeted N26.91 billion for the two components of the hotel’s rehabilitation.

It remains unclear how much of the N16 billion allocated in 2025 was released and spent before the additional N10.91 billion provision in the 2026 budget. Since the first quarter of 2025, the Akwa Ibom State Government has failed to publish detailed budget performance reports including its capital expenses.

PREMIUM TIMES has reported that under Governor Umo Eno’s administration, Akwa Ibom has slipped deeper into fiscal secrecy.

Full closure

The government initially adopted a phased approach to the renovation, allowing the hotel to continue operating while parts of the facility were being rehabilitated.

The state had said 40 of the hotel’s 163 rooms and the seven chalets were initially shut to enable renovation works.

But in its latest announcement, the government said the entire hotel would temporarily suspend operations from 22 August.

“This is part of the ongoing comprehensive rehabilitation and renewal of Ibom Hotels and Golf Resort,” the government said, adding that the closure would allow for the “speedy completion of renovation works and the implementation of a new operational framework.”

The golf course, however, will remain open.

The government said the course had been maintained and remained in good condition for players and visitors.

Who is supervising the project?

Although the rehabilitation projects are budgeted under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Charles Udoh, a former commissioner for information, environment and culture/tourism, is supervising the renovation.

Mr Udoh currently serves as Mr Eno’s delivery advisor on hospitality infrastructure.

The rehabilitation commenced in March 2025.

The state government has, however, not publicly provided a comprehensive project document stating the approved total cost, implementation period, contractor, milestones or expected completion date.

The lack of publicly available details makes it difficult to determine how the N26.91 billion budget provision relates to the actual cost of the ongoing rehabilitation and how much of the money has so far been expended.

Government changes hotel management

The closure will also coincide with a change in the management of the state-owned hospitality business.

The government said management of Ibom Hospitality Limited would be handed over to ALEPH Hospitality, an international hospitality management company, from 22 August.

According to the government, the decision is intended to introduce “global best practices”, improve service standards and operational efficiency, and enhance the commercial performance of the state’s hospitality assets.

It said the decision followed more than 18 years of continuous operation of the hotel without a major transformation.

The government also said no existing employee would be laid off solely because of the management transition.

It, however, acknowledged that some employees might choose not to continue under the new operational arrangement, while others might not possess the skills required by the new management.

Such workers, the government said, could be considered for opportunities elsewhere within the state’s hospitality chain, including the ARISE Palm Resort when it becomes operational.

During the closure, a team of employees will remain at the hotel to support the rehabilitation works, protect the property and ensure its maintenance, the government said.

The government described the rehabilitation and management transition as part of its plan to reposition Akwa Ibom’s hospitality sector and make the state a major tourism and business destination.

But the scale of the budgetary commitment — N26.91 billion in two years — raises questions about the actual expenditure on the project, the status of the works and the timeline for reopening the hotel.

The government did not provide those details in Saturday’s announcement.

World.title: Tonto Dikeh establishes prophetic ministry, holds weekly fellowship in Abuja
World.content:
Nigerian actress and evangelist Tonto Dikeh has announced the establishment of her prophetic ministry, New Wine Prophetic Tabernacle (NWPT).

She announced the ministry on her Instagram page on Sunday, describing it as a ministry grounded in the foundational truths of scripture.

The actress has recently made headlines for openly expressing her devotion to God’s work.

Her activities have included conducting deliverance sessions and warning men against using spirituality as a substitute for genuine effort when seeking women for marriage, among others.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She wrote: “New Wine Prophetic Tabernacle (NWPT) is an interdenominational altar, spiritual home, and global movement of consecrated believers called to experience the raw power, purity, and presence of God. Grounded in the foundational truth of Scripture, ‘And no one puts new wine into old wineskins…’ (Mark 2:22).

“NWPT exists as a dwelling place of His presence for those who refuse to settle for lukewarm Christianity and are hungry for genuine revival, fire, and transformation.”

Vision

Furthermore, she stated that the ministry’s vision was to witness a global awakening of consecrated believers who operate in the power, purity, and presence of God.

She said the ministry would seek to empower these believers to transform nations and establish Christ’s Kingdom on Earth.

“To build an interdenominational altar of prayer, revival, and apostolic training that equips watchmen, activates spiritual gifts, drives relentless soul winning, and delivers total freedom to the captive through the power of the Holy Spirit”, she revealed the mission statement.

She said NWPT is not a church but an intense gathering of people consecrated and equipped to fulfil God’s purposes.

“A people set apart, refined by his presence, and commissioned to advance his Kingdom. Gathering & Location Details. Venue: Omini Grand Hotel (formerly Alexis Hotel), upstairs, by Masalachi Junction, Jabi, FCT-Abuja. Fellowship Day: Every Friday. Time: 6:00 PM.”

World.title: Army, Air Force, police engage over 100 bandits at Zamfara-Kebbi border
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

ABUJA — A combined force of the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Air Force and Police is currently engaged in a fierce gun battle with more than 100 suspected bandits operating around the Zamfara-Kebbi border.

Security sources said the operation involves troops of the Chief of Army Staff Intervention Battalion 3, under 8 Division of the Nigerian Army; the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma; and personnel of the Mobile Police Force.

The sources said the bandits emerged in large numbers from the Sangeko Gap in Zamfara State and were advancing towards Makuku in Kebbi State when intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance assets detected their movement.

According to the sources, the armed group was moving in three separate formations, with the suspected bandits reportedly travelling on motorcycles.

The development has heightened security concerns in communities around the affected areas, with some residents reportedly moving to safer locations as security forces intensify efforts to contain the advance.

The engagement involves coordinated ground operations by troops and police personnel, supported by air operations by the Air Component of Operation Fansan Yamma.

The deployment is aimed at preventing the suspected bandits from gaining access to surrounding communities, disrupting their movement and stopping them from expanding their operations in the area.

Residents have been advised to remain vigilant and comply with directives from security authorities while the operation continues.

The ongoing engagement highlights the security challenges posed by armed groups operating across parts of the North-West, where security agencies have sustained operations aimed at disrupting criminal networks, rescuing kidnapped victims and restoring normalcy to affected communities.

As of the time of filing this report, the security agencies had not released an official casualty figure or confirmed the outcome of the ongoing operation. Further details are expected as the military and other security agencies provide updates.

World.title: Wike denies lobbying for APC campaign council DG
World.content:
Wike

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked reports in some sections of the media suggesting that he was lobbying to be made Director General of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council PCC.

Reacting through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the monister described the report as false, saying he did not at any time discuss the leadership or even membership of the Presidential Campaign Council with anyone.

A national newspaper (not Vanguard) had on Monday listed the FCT minister among top party chieftains and government officials lobbying or being mentioned for the position of APC Presidential Campaign Council DG.

Wike, who reiterated his unflinching support for the reelection of President Bola Tinubu, said he does not need to be the DG or even a member of the President’s Campaign Council to ensure that the President wins massively in Rivers State and the FCT.

“I am outside Nigeria, resting and relaxing after spending over 30 days, commissioning projects, flagging off new ones and inspecting ongoing ones, especially those scheduled for commissioning in December and January, next year.

“When I return, our focus will be the continuous delivery of our mandate in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda and to further enhance his electoral fortune in Rivers State and the FCT.

“Therefore, I do not need to be the DG or even member of the Presidential Campaign Council of Mr President’s political party to contribute my quota by ensuring that he wins handsomely in Rivers State and the FCT,” Wike who is now the leader of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party PDP said.

World.title: Army, police rescue kidnapped victim in Edo, recover ransom
World.content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – PERSONNEL of 4 Brigade Nigerian Army in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, have rescued a kidnapped victim identified as Lucky Egbiki during a coordinated operation in Ubiaja, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State.

The 50 years old Egbiki was kidnapped at his farm in Ubiaja, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State.

A statement on Sunday by the Brigade’s Assistant Director Army Public Relations, Captain Kennedy Anyanwu rescue operation was conducted “at about 1800 hours on 6 August 2026 by troops, in conjunction with personnel of the Nigeria Police. The security forces exploited ransom negotiations to lure the kidnappers to a predetermined location at Onogholo, within Esan South East Local Government Area, where they engaged the criminal elements.”

He said during the encounter, one of the kidnappers who arrived at the location to collect the ransom was neutralized by the troops, forcing the other members of the gang to abandon the victim and flee into the surrounding forest, with some believed to have sustained gunshot wounds.

He said the troops subsequently rescued the victim unhurt and recovered the sum of ₦1.5 million intended as ransom payment. “The rescued victim was handed over to his family after preliminary debriefing and medical assessment, and was confirmed to be in stable condition.”

Anyanwu said the successful operation further demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s operational readiness, intelligence-driven approach and unwavering commitment to combating kidnapping and other forms of violent crime in Edo State and “It also underscores the importance of inter-agency collaboration in enhancing the effectiveness of security operations.

“The people of Edo State are therefore encouraged to continue providing timely, credible and actionable information to security agencies, as such support remains vital to sustaining operational successes and enhancing security across the state.”

The Commander, 4 Brigade Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ahmed Balogun, commended the troops for their proactiveness, courage and professionalism displayed during the operation and reassured the people of Edo State that the Brigade would continue to apply sustained pressure on kidnappers and other criminal elements operating within its area of responsibility.

“The Commander further affirmed that troops would sustain aggressive and intelligence-led operations aimed at denying criminal elements safe havens, protecting lives and property, and creating a secure environment for farming and other legitimate economic activities across Edo State.”

World.title: Video: ‘My daughter needs treatment’ – Nigerian US army woman begs Trump over visa denial
World.content:
A Nigerian woman serving in the United States Army has appealed to President Donald Trump to intervene in a visa dispute preventing her 10-year-old daughter from joining her in the US.

The woman said her daughter is critically ill and requires urgent medical attention that she believes is difficult to access in Nigeria.

She made the appeal in a video posted on TikTok, saying she had been separated from her daughter for about 10 years and feared she could lose her before they have the opportunity to reunite.

She said she had taken an oath to serve the United States and remained compliant with the country’s laws, but was now seeking Trump’s intervention as a mother desperate to save her child.

“Please do not scroll. I’m at the verge of losing my daughter. They said social media is powerful, and this is my last resort.”

According to the woman, her daughter had completed the necessary immigration process but remained unable to travel to the US because of current visa restrictions.

She said the child became critically ill while the family waited for the immigration process to be completed, increasing her concern over the girl’s access to adequate medical care.

“I’m not just speaking as a soldier; I’m speaking as a mother whose heart is gradually breaking. I have been separated from my daughter for the past 10 years, and she remains in Nigeria,” she said.

“Every day that passes by increases my fear that I might lose her before having the chance to hold her again and reunite with her.”

The US Army member acknowledged the importance of immigration laws and national security but urged the government to consider her circumstances on humanitarian grounds.

“My plea now is not about politics but a humanitarian one, a compassionate one that you should review carefully and consider. I’m simply asking that there should be an exception for me and for people that fall into this category,” she said.

She also questioned why she should remain in the US, where she said her daughter could have access to better healthcare, while the child remains critically ill in Nigeria.

“How can I be in a country that has quality healthcare and let my daughter die?” she asked.

She disclosed that she had contacted her commander and US Senator Amy Klobuchar for help, saying the senator attempted to intervene but was informed that the immigration process was proceeding as expected.

“I’ve reached out to my commander and Senator Amy Klobuchar. She tried her best, and they told her everything is going as planned. But your visa process and policies are keeping my children from reuniting with me,” she said.

She further said she could not return to Nigeria because of security concerns, arguing that her children should not be viewed as a threat to the United States.

“My kids are barely minors that can’t pose a threat and are not coming here to be criminals,” she said.

She subsequently appealed to social media users to share the video and tag Trump, saying she had turned to social media after exhausting other options.

“I never thought a day would come that I would be facing the camera and pleading. Dear Mr President, please help me reunite with my daughter,” she said.
