World.title: Onoh tackles SA envoy over xenophobia denial, demands protection for Nigerians
World.content:
By Dennis Agbo

ABUJA — Former member of the Enugu State House of Assembly and former Southeast spokesman for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Chief Okey Onoh, has criticised the South African Consul-General to Nigeria, Prof. Bobby Moroe, over his denial of xenophobia in South Africa.

Moroe, in a recent interview, had assured Nigerians that South Africa remained safe for tourists, business travellers and other visitors, insisting that “there’s no xenophobia in South Africa” when asked about reported attacks on foreigners.

Reacting in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja, Onoh disagreed with the envoy, arguing that the denial did not reflect the experiences of African migrants in South Africa.

He alleged that xenophobic and anti-immigrant sentiments remained a serious concern in parts of the country, citing reported attacks on foreign nationals and activities of groups he identified as Operation Dudula and other anti-immigrant organisations.

According to Onoh, the activities of such groups had created fear among African migrants and affected their businesses and livelihoods.

He also cited reports by human rights organisations and research bodies which, he said, had documented anti-immigrant sentiments and incidents involving attacks or discrimination against migrants.

Onoh argued that South Africa’s domestic economic and security challenges should not be blamed on African migrants, alleging that foreigners had sometimes been used as scapegoats for wider social and economic problems.

He called on the South African government to do more to protect foreign nationals and prosecute those responsible for attacks and discrimination against migrants.

Onoh also criticised what he described as the silence of some South African officials over reported attacks against African migrants, saying the country should uphold the principles of African solidarity that characterised the struggle against apartheid.

He recalled the support provided by African countries, including Nigeria, during the anti-apartheid struggle, arguing that the continent’s solidarity should be reciprocated through the protection of African nationals living and doing business in South Africa.

The former lawmaker further called for what he described as a coordinated continental response to attacks against African migrants in South Africa.

He argued that African countries should reconsider the economic and diplomatic benefits extended to South Africa if the safety and rights of their citizens could not be guaranteed.

Onoh said Nigeria should prioritise the safety and dignity of its citizens, while urging the South African authorities to address concerns surrounding xenophobic violence and discrimination.

Concluding his statement, Onoh said: “Keep your South Africa, while we keep our Nigeria.”

He maintained that Nigerians should feel safe and protected in their own country and urged the South African government to take concrete measures to protect African migrants and strengthen peaceful relations among African nations.

World.title: Abia new CP, Afolabi assumes duty, vows zero tolerance for misconduct
World.content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State has a new Commissioner of Police, Mr Wilfred Afolabi, who assumed duty on Monday with a pledge to strengthen intelligence-led policing, deepen community partnership and enforce discipline within the rank and file.

CP Afolabi, who becomes the 35th Commissioner of Police in Abia, succeeds AIG Danladi Isa, who has been promoted and redeployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Kaduna.

The new CP, who spoke to journalists shortly after assuming office, said his administration would focus on strengthening existing security structures and re-engineering the state’s intelligence network to enhance crime prevention.

“Because of my intelligence background, intelligence is really going to be given much priority. We are going to make sure that intelligence structures are re-engineered and the intelligence network enhanced,” he said.

The new CP said his administration would replicate the agenda of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, in Abia, particularly the objective of building a police force that discharges its responsibilities with professionalism and dignity.

He disclosed that his first major engagement after assuming duty would be with the intelligence department, underscoring the importance he attaches to intelligence gathering.

The new CP also promised to take community policing to a new level through regular engagement with stakeholders, including traditional rulers, youth and religious leaders, hoteliers, pharmacists and school proprietors.

According to him, such engagement would create a “two-way traffic” through which residents could communicate their security concerns to the police while also providing useful information for crime prevention.

“When there is mutual trust, there will be free flow of information. They will feel free to share information with us,” he said.

Vows to prepare Abia police for 2027 polls

As the 2027 general elections draw closer, Afolabi said his administration would embark on extensive capacity building for officers, including training on electoral laws, human rights, emotional intelligence, crime mapping and investigation.

He said officers would also undergo physical and operational preparedness exercises ahead of the elections.

“We need to make our officers undertake what I call combat courses,” he said.

The CP further promised to review existing crime prevention strategies and introduce new approaches where necessary, while ensuring greater professionalism and uniformity in the handling of police case files.

‘We won’t spare deviant officers’

Afolabi also came down hard on police personnel who deliberately abuse their powers, warning that officers who commit serious offences would face the full weight of disciplinary procedures.

He said his administration would combine mentoring and capacity building with firm disciplinary measures.

“If, after investing millions in training you, you still decide to become a deviant, be rest assured that we are not going to treat your matter with kid gloves,” he warned.

He gave an instance of any officer who unjustifiably shoots a motorist, saying such conduct would not be excused through intervention by traditional rulers or religious leaders.

“You cannot go and shoot a motorist along the highway now for no justifiable reason and expect that you will bring your king or your religious leader to come and beg me. I will not forgive you,” he said.

However, Afolabi said not every breach of duty would automatically attract dismissal, stressing that officers whose shortcomings arose from inadequate professional training would be mentored and retrained.

To prioritize welfare of officers

The new CP also listed police welfare among his priorities, arguing that officers who are properly catered for would be more motivated to perform their duties effectively.

“When our officers are taken care of and catered for, you get the best out of them,” he said.

He also pledged to maintain discipline within the command, declaring that his personal discipline would be reflected in the standards expected of officers under him.

Promises media-friendly administration

Afolabi also assured journalists of a cordial working relationship, describing the media as critical partners in crime prevention, public enlightenment and confidence-building between the police and the public.

He promised regular interaction with the media in Abia, stressing that journalists should report both the successes and shortcomings of the police.

“I’m not saying if I’m not doing well, you should keep quiet,” he said.

Afolabi said he respected journalists and regarded them as partners in the war against crime.

Meanwhile , a statement issued later by the Police Public Relations Officer PPRO, Maureen Chinaka, described CP Afolabi as a seasoned police officer with over three decades of service, who was enlisted as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police in 1992 and holds degrees in Botany and Peace and Security Studies.

It said Afolabi had served in several strategic command positions, including Commissioner of Police in Ondo State, CP Admin, Training and Development at Force Headquarters, and senior operational and investigative roles in Delta, Katsina, Bayelsa, Anambra, Imo and Abuja.

“Afolabi also has extensive international policing experience, having served with the African Union Mission in Sudan and the United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he was involved in police reforms, training and peacekeeping operations.

“His professional training includes strategic and tactical leadership, internal security, low-intensity conflict and peacekeeping negotiation”, the statement said.

World.title: NERC sacks Kaduna DisCo’s board over N456bn debt, appoints interim administrator
World.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has dissolved the board of Kaduna Electricity Distribution Company (KAEDC) and appointed its Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Abubakar Umar Hashidu, as administrator for an initial six-month period, citing severe financial, operational and regulatory failures.

The regulatory intervention, contained in Order No. NERC/2026/086, issued on Monday, took effect from August 10, 2026, and followed an inquiry and consultations with key industry stakeholders, including the Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE).

According to NERC, KAEDC was in a “grave situation” characterised by prolonged regulatory and market default, inadequate investment, weak operational and commercial performance, insufficient assets relative to its liabilities and an inability to present a credible pathway to sustainable recovery.

The Commission said the DisCo’s cumulative market obligations since privatisation stood at approximately N456.5 billion as of May 2026, comprising N415.5 billion owed to the Nigerian Bulk Electricity Trading Plc (NBET) and N41 billion owed to the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO).

It added that KAEDC had accumulated another N14.26 billion in non-market statutory and third-party obligations.

NERC further said that since ASI Engineering Limited (ASI) took over operations of KAEDC in June 2024, the DisCo had incurred an additional N118.6 billion in market debt as of May 2026.

The Commission said ASI and KAEDC had “persistently failed” to furnish NBET and NISO with acceptable payment bank guarantees as required under their Vesting Contract and the Market Rules of the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI).

The core investor also failed to provide a credible payment plan for the outstanding liabilities, NERC said.

The Commission cited KAEDC’s poor remittance performance as another reason for the intervention. It said the DisCo paid only 41.93 per cent of adjusted market invoices in 2025, leaving a market shortfall of approximately N46.71 billion.

The poor remittance performance was linked to KAEDC’s high Aggregate Technical, Commercial and Collection (ATC&C) losses, which stood at 71.88 per cent during the 2025 review period.

“This means that in the 2025 review period, KAEDC was only able to account for only 28.2 per cent of the energy received and delivered to end-use customers,” the Commission said.

NERC also faulted the investor’s capital expenditure performance, saying ASI failed to meet its capital injection commitments towards the recapitalisation of the utility.

According to the order, KAEDC’s actual capital expenditure in 2025 was approximately N2.48 billion, against a minimum capital expenditure provision of N24.51 billion, representing only 10 per cent CAPEX performance.

The Commission noted that the actual expenditure followed derogations and forbearances granted by NERC.

The DisCo’s metering performance was also described as “abysmally low”, with meter coverage of its end-use customer population remaining between 33.26 per cent and 35.54 per cent since ASI took over the company, despite interventions aimed at supporting metering deployment.

NERC said its earlier conditional no-objection of January 18, 2024 had approved the proposed acquisition of a 60 per cent equity stake in KAEDC by ASI, working with its nominated technical partner, Akanksha Power and Infrastructure Limited (APIL), subject to several conditions.

These included evidence of APIL’s capacity to perform in Nigeria, a substantive technical-support proposal for KAEDC’s turnaround, a compliance plan for meeting NERC’s key performance indicators, a credible management team, a credible ATC&C loss-reduction trajectory and plans for bank guarantees in favour of NBET and the relevant market operator.

However, NERC said ASI continued to fail to demonstrate full compliance with the requirements, while outstanding regulatory conditions remained unresolved.

Against this background, the Commission dissolved the existing board and removed all its directors from office.

It appointed an interim board chaired by Dr. Abdullahi Garba, with Engr. Francis U. Agoha, Mr. Aliyu E. Aliyu, Major General Henry E. Ayamasaowei (rtd), Dr. Haliru Dikko and Mr. Ayodeji A. Gbeleji, representing the BPE, as special directors.

Hashidu was also appointed a special director for an initial six-month term and designated administrator of the DisCo.

As administrator, he will oversee day-to-day operations, implement interim board resolutions and NERC directives, safeguard KAEDC’s assets and records, and handle matters reserved for approval by the Commission or interim board.

NERC also withdrew the Key Yardstick Licence (KYL) approvals issued to members of KAEDC’s management team and directed affected staff to present themselves for revalidation.

The Commission imposed restrictions on major financial and corporate decisions by KAEDC during the transition period, including borrowing, disposal or transfer of material assets, related-party transactions, changes to senior management remuneration, appointment or removal of senior officers and alteration of the company’s capital structure.

The administrator was further directed to submit a costed 12-month stabilisation plan within 60 days, covering cash-flow controls, market remittances, collections, metering, energy accounting, loss reduction, service reliability, safety, customer complaints, capital expenditure, procurement, staff obligations and legacy liabilities.

NERC said the special transition period would continue until the earlier of the completion of the transfer to a replacement core investor approved by the Commission, or termination, extension or variation of the intervention by a further order.

World.title: Full list of African countries qualified for 2027 Women’s World Cup
World.content:
The 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco is doubling as Africa’s qualifying tournament for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, with the four teams that reach the semi-finals earning automatic tickets to the global competition.

Four countries have already secured their places at next year’s tournament in Brazil after advancing to the last four of WAFCON.

They are Algeria, Morocco, Cameroon and Malawi, with each nation booking its place at the World Cup through its quarter-final victory.

Meanwhile, Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa still have an opportunity to qualify through the play-off route.

Here are the four African countries that have qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

1. Algeria

Algeria made history by securing their first-ever qualification for the FIFA Women’s World Cup after producing a remarkable comeback against Côte d’Ivoire.

The Fennecs fell behind early but responded strongly to defeat the Ivorians 2-1 in their WAFCON quarter-final.

Ines Khiri and Amira Ould Braham scored the goals that completed Algeria’s comeback and secured their place in the semi-finals.

The victory means Algeria will make their debut at the FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2027.

2. Morocco

Hosts Morocco also booked their place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup after overcoming South Africa 2-1 in the quarter-finals.

Sakina Ouzraoui Diki and Hanane Ait El Haj were on target for the Atlas Lionesses as they progressed to the WAFCON semi-finals.

The result keeps Morocco’s hopes of winning the continental title on home soil alive while also guaranteeing them a third successive appearance at the Women’s World Cup.

3. Cameroon

Cameroon secured their World Cup ticket after stunning defending champions Nigeria in one of the biggest results of the WAFCON quarter-finals.

The Indomitable Lionesses defeated the Super Falcons 1-0, with 19-year-old Myriam Nyadjou scoring the only goal of the encounter.

Nyadjou’s long-range effort proved decisive as Cameroon advanced to the semi-finals and ended Nigeria’s hopes of retaining their African title.

The result also guarantees Cameroon a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

4. Malawi

Malawi produced one of the biggest surprises of the tournament by defeating Ghana 2-1 to reach the WAFCON semi-finals and qualify for the World Cup for the first time.

The Scorchers fell behind when Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah put Ghana ahead early in the match.

Malawi responded through Temwa Chawinga, who restored parity before Rose Kadzere scored the winning goal.

The historic victory secured Malawi’s first-ever qualification for the FIFA Women’s World Cup.

WAFCON 2026 semi-final fixtures

The four qualified teams will now battle for the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title.

The semi-final matches are:

Morocco vs Cameroon

Algeria vs Malawi

The winners will advance to the WAFCON final and compete for the continental championship.

Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa still have a chance

Although Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa were eliminated in the quarter-finals, their hopes of reaching the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup remain alive.

The four teams will enter an additional African play-off, with the winners moving on to the intercontinental play-offs.

Côte d’Ivoire will face Ghana on Thursday, while Nigeria will battle South Africa.

The two winners will join the six other teams in the 10-team intercontinental play-offs, where three teams will ultimately qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

The tournament is scheduled to run from June 24 to July 25, 2027, in Brazil.

African countries qualified for 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup

The four African nations that have already secured their places are:

Algeria Morocco Cameroon Malawi

These four countries will represent Africa at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, while Ghana, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa continue their campaigns through the play-off route.

Vanguard News

World.title: Coalition to Tinubu: Don’t Assent to National Tobacco Control Act Amendment Bill
World.content:
* Says it compromises public health

Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The Nigeria Tobacco Control Community has called on President Bola Tinubu to withhold assent to the National Tobacco Control Act (Amendment) Bill 2025, saying it compromised the public health of Nigerians.

It also called on the National Assembly to immediately recall the consolidated Bill and subject it to a transparent, public health-led review.

It further called on the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to publicly clarify its position and demand the recall of the Bill if it was not properly consulted.

The group made the call on Monday in Abuja during a press conference with the theme ‘Why Nigeria must reject harmful amendments to the National Tobacco Control Act.’

Speaking at the event, the Executive Director of Corporate Accountability & Public Participation Africa (CAPPA), Oluwafemi Akinbode, maintained that Nigeria needs one strong and product-neutral framework for every tobacco and nicotine product.

He said having carefully reviewed the proposed legislation, the Bill does not protect Nigerians, instead it weakens existing safeguards and creates a wide-open market for tobacco and nicotine companies to thrive at the expense of public health.

To this end, Akinbode demanded its immediate recall for a comprehensive and transparent review.

He stated: “We agree that our primary law, the National Tobacco Control Act of 2015, alongside its 2019 Regulations, requires updating to address evolving markets.

“However, modernising our legal framework must not mean rolling out a red carpet for new and emerging nicotine and tobacco products.

“We cannot protect public health by carving out weak rules and loopholes for vapes, heated tobacco products, and nicotine pouches.”

Akinbode added that while the amendment bill contains minor positive updates, such as Clause 5, which extends smoke-free zones within 30 metres of schools and health facilities, and Clause 3, which adds the Nigeria Police Force and Youth Development Ministry to the National Tobacco Control Committee, these provisions cannot excuse the far more reckless changes introduced throughout the text.

He explained that Clause 16 alters section 45 of the Principal Act by defining heated tobacco products as noncombustible products and explicitly excluding non-combustible items from the legal definition of a tobacco product.

Akinbode stressed that Clause 7 amends Section 12 by introducing Subsection (6), Section 12(1) of the NTC Act 2015 currently prohibits tobacco advertising, promotion and sponsorship.

In his submission, In-Country Coordinator, Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids, Michael Olaniyan, argued that public health is under attack and called on the health ministry to wake up.

He lamented that the National Assembly discarded public recommendations on the proposed Bill and created a new 31-page Tobacco Control Bill, contradicting the original two documents.

Olaniyan stressed the Bill reduces health warning sizes and removes penalties for non-compliance, granting the minister broad discretion over product regulations.

According to him, “The bill now permits online sales of tobacco products, despite previous prohibitions, raising concerns about verification and enforcement.”

Olaniyan explained that there is a loophole in the bill that allows for product sampling in enclosed areas, which effectively allows perpetual use of tobacco products under the guise of sampling.

He said the Bill also introduces a maximum size for health warnings on tobacco products, which could be reduced to zero, contradicting the principle of increasing health warnings.

Olaniyan stressed that the standard practice is to set a minimum size for health warnings, which could be increased in response to health challenges, but the bill downplays this.

He decried that the Bill deletes provisions for offences and penalties related to sales, weakening the law and making non-compliance more likely.

Olaniyan revealed that the minister was given unprecedented power to decide which products do not need to comply with the law, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest and undermining public health efforts.

The alliance demanded: “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu must withhold assent should this compromised draft reach his desk.

“The National Assembly must immediately recall the consolidated Bill and subject it to a transparent, public health led review.

“Publish all committee reports, voting records, and stakeholder submissions, which led to the development of this anti-health bill.

“The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare must publicly clarify its position and demand the recall of the Bill if it was not properly consulted.”

The coalition noted that nothing in the proposed Bill aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda of the president.

World.title: Edo ADC House Candidate Decries Name Substitution
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

The Egharevba Bright Osakpamwan Campaign Organisation has demanded an explanation on how the name of Deacon Festus Osaigbovo Osagie found its way into the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) portal as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate for the House of Representatives election.

The organisation said the party’s internal processes have been compromised as Bright was the candidate of the party.

This was just as the organisation consequently called on INEC, former Edo State Governor, Chief John Odigie-Oyegun; Senator Ehigie Uzamere, and Prof. Osariemen Osunbor, alongside the ADC national leadership, to make public the records and resolutions relating to the primary election and the subsequent submission of the party’s candidate to INEC.

The campaign organisation said the development was disturbing, insisting that Bright participated in and won the ADC primary election conducted to select the party’s candidate for the constituency.

In a statement signed by its spokesman, Onyia Harrison, the organisation said it was particularly concerned that the name and credentials of another candidate could appear on the electoral commission’s portal despite what it described as the outcome of the party’s established internal processes.

It also called on the ADC national leadership and INEC to explain the circumstances surrounding the disputed upload and make public the records relating to the primary election and the subsequent submission of the party’s candidate to the commission.

The organisation said: “Bright emergence was based on the votes of delegates, including purchasing the nomination form, paying the prescribed fees, submitting the necessary documents, and taking part in the primary election.”

The campaign group acknowledged that Osagie’s name and credentials were currently appearing on the INEC portal, but argued that the upload should not automatically override the outcome of the party primary, which it said Bright won.

It warned that it would not accept any attempt to overturn what it described as the mandate given to Bright by ADC delegates through what it called administrative manipulation, backroom arrangements or alteration of party records.

However, Festus Osagie said the party decides to choose whoever represents them, adding: “Is it Egharevba that will choose who represents ADC? Whatever he is doing is his own decision.”

World.title: CMFC Shows Bright Prospects Three Months after Transformation
World.content:
Three months after shareholders approved the change from Deap Capital Management & Trust Plc to Critical Minerals Financing Corp Plc (CMFC), the company has started showing very bright prospects going by its latest financial results for nine months ended June 30, 2026.

The company was restructured following the entry of Banklink Africa Private Equities Limited as a core investor, making CMFC as a specialised financing and investment Banking institution focused on developing Africa’s critical minerals, metals, and commodities sectors. Unaudited interim financial statements of the company for the nine month ended

June 30, 2026 submitted to the NGX on August5, showed that CMFC has started to earn income and closing period with a robust cash position.

Specifically, unlike the nine months ended June 2025 when the company recorded zero income, it ended nine months in 2026 with an income of N82.641 million. A further analysis of the earnings showed that 90 per cent was recorded between

March and June 2026. Also, the company closed the period with a robust cash position of over N6 billion, a situation market analysts said gives the company opportunity for business funding to earn more income in the coming months.

Besides, the company has paid off the AMCON negotiated debt of N430 million for which they were originally claiming N2.5 billion. Also, AMCON, which used to be the largest shareholder with 16 per cent of the paid-up capital, is no longer a shareholder in the company, freeing the company from issues related to its painful past years.

Banlink Africa Private Equities Limited is now the majority shareholder and has committed a total of N6 billion to accelerate the corporate transition of CMFC.

Investors in the Nigeria Exchange Limited ( NGX) have embraced these developments in CMFC with a lot of optimism. Since August 2025 when the company and Banklink Africa Private Equities Limited started their discussions about Banklink’s strategic investment in the company to August 7, 2026 more than 1.44 billion shares of the company have been traded out of the total issued and fully paid up share capital of 1,500,660,000. This shows a turnover of 97 per cent compared to 946 million shares of the company traded between May 2023 when the company restarted operation after 10 years of inactivity and July 31, 2025. The stock has also become very liquid since the new investors showed interest in the company with daily deals being in excess of 190 transactions compared to less than 40 deals in the period from May 2023 to July 31, 2025 before Banklink Africa Private Equities Limited invested in the company. At the same time the price has moved from N1.35 per shares in the first week of August 2025 to N11.43 on January 31, 2026 before it came down from February 2026 to the present level of N3.01 on August 5, 2026 when the nine months result for 2026 was released to the market.

The result has given a complete picture of the turnaround and transformation of the company from negative shareholders fund of N2.3 billion as at September 30 , 2025 to a positive shareholders funds of N4.3 billion as at June

30, 2026, a positive movement of 272 per cent. This improvement in the asset base of the company has led to the net asset per share improving from negative 155 kobo as at September 30, 2025 to positive 167 kobo as at June 2026, a favourable change of 208 per cent.

In the same period the company has successfully converted legacy debts of N1.8 billion out of N2.52 billion into 1,068, 980,259 Ordinary shares of 50k each , thereby increasing the paid-up capital to 2,569, 640,259 ordinary shares of 50k each after receiving the approval of the Securities and Exchange Commission ( SEC) to that effect.

The Chairman, CMFC Plc, Mr Lamon Rutten, who was appointed in March 2026, has said the transition reflected company’s sharpened focus on capital structuring, investment banking, transaction advisory, project development support, and financing solutions for stakeholders across the minerals and commodities sector.

According to him, the completion of the transition to CMFC marks the beginning of an exciting new phase for the company.

Rutten, a founding Chief Executive Officer of Saudi Mining Exchange and Mumbai Commodity Exchange (MCX), said: “We are strategically positioned to deliver world- class capital structuring, advisory, and financing solutions to mining and metals companies operating across gold, copper, cobalt, lithium, tungsten, tin, tantalum, and other critical mineral sectors.”

He explained that CMFC’s strategy is focused on addressing the significant financing and transaction-structuring gap within Africa’s mining industry by combining global financial expertise, sector-specific knowledge, and strategic partnerships.

Market analysts have said with the new board members and management of CMFC, shareholders are in for an exciting time going forward.

For instance, the chairman, Rutten, is a globally respected expert in commodity markets, structured commodity finance, and exchange development with over 30 years of international experience across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

Founding CEO of the Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), which he led to become the world's second-largest commodity exchange after CME, achieving a public listing valued at approximately US $1.5 billion. Previously Founding CEO of the Indonesia Commodity & Derivatives Exchange (ICDX) and a key architect of the Saudi Mining Exchange initiative.

Earlier Rutten led international commodity risk management and trade finance programmes at the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD). Has advised governments, multilateral institutions, and financial organisations on commodity market development.

On the other hand, the President & Co-Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Israel Ovirih, is a development economist and veteran structured-finance expert with over 30 years of experience in Nigerian and international capital markets. Founder and Chairman of Banklink Africa Private Equities Group with a formidable track record in capital syndication, project finance, and institutional advisory. He has arranged and advised on financing programmes exceeding US $1.5 billion across energy, marine, and oil & gas sectors. Previously held senior strategic roles at Guaranty Trust Bank, Oceanic Bank, and ETBank (now Sterling Bank), and currently sits on multiple corporate boards across Africa driving economic transformation initiatives.

World.title: Funke Akindele Announces New Feature Film, The Four
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

Award-winning filmmaker, actress and producer Funke Akindele has announced her next feature film, ‘The Four: No One Fights Alone’ set for a global cinema release in December.

Produced by Funke Akindele Network (FAAN TV) and distributed by FilmOne Entertainment, the announcement marks the next chapter for one of Africa’s most commercially successful filmmakers, whose films have consistently redefined the possibilities of Nigerian cinema.

Set between the picturesque Odu Community and the vibrant pulse of the city, the film follows Esosa and three fiercely loyal women whose journey to fight for the future of a young man they love tests their courage, faith, and loyalty in unimaginable ways. Through music, fashion, language, tradition and breathtaking cinematography, the film celebrates Nigeria’s rich cultural identity while weaving together authentic storytelling around hope, sacrifice and the enduring power of unity.

The film brings together one of Nollywood’s most accomplished ensemble casts, starring Akindele herself, Bisola Aiyeola, Chioma Akpotha, Richard Mofe-Damijo (RMD), Timini Egbuson, Lateef Adedimeji, Ali Nuhu, Uzor Arukwe, Ronke Oshodi Oke, Antar Laniyan and Wunmi Toriola. The film also features award-winning singer Waje, afrobeats star Shoday, alongside entertainment personalities, Samuel Banks, Kolapo Omotosho and Ayomide Iwasokun.

“Audiences have grown with us over the years, and they expect stories that entertain while reflecting who we are,” said Akindele.

“With The Four, we are exploring the relationships that shape us, challenge us and stay with us. I think audiences will find a “part of themselves in this story.”

Over the years, Akindele has become one of the defining forces in African cinema, directing and producing a string of record-breaking theatrical releases including ‘Omo Ghetto: The Saga,’ ‘Battle on Buka Street,’ ‘A Tribe Called Judah,’ ‘Everybody Loves Jenifa’ and ‘Behind The Scenes.’

Her films have repeatedly rewritten Nigerian box-office history, cementing her position as the country’s highest-grossing filmmaker and one of the continent’s most influential creative voices.

‘The Four’ opens in cinemas on December 11 and is exclusively distributed by FilmOne Entertainment

World.title: Donald Duke Calls for Nigeria’s Financial System Overhaul, Faults High Interest Rates, Rising Debt
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator

The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in the forthcoming 2027 general election, Donald Duke, has called for a comprehensive overhaul of Nigeria’s financial architecture, blaming high interest rates, rising public debt, and misplaced government spending for the difficulties confronting businesses and the wider economy.

Duke, a former governor of Cross River State, said Nigeria urgently needed bold economic reforms focused on affordable credit, disciplined public expenditure, energy security, and institutional efficiency to stimulate productivity, restore investor confidence, and put the economy on a sustainable growth path.

Speaking during an interview, the PRP presidential candidate said prevailing lending rates had made meaningful economic expansion increasingly difficult for businesses, arguing that no economy could achieve sustainable growth when the cost of borrowing remained prohibitively high.

He said if elected president in 2027, his administration would prioritise the design of a financial system that supports productivity, which he said was currently lacking.

According to Duke, “With interest rates in the upper 30s, you are undermining the economy. You cannot grow an economy with borrowing costs at that level.

“Affordable loans promote growth, while inflation in our case is largely driven by the high cost of government and poor economic management.”

The former governor also criticised what he described as misplaced government spending priorities, calling for a fundamental shift in public expenditure towards sectors capable of driving productivity, improving citizens’ welfare, and creating jobs.

He further said that greater investments should be directed towards electricity, healthcare, education, and the judiciary rather than projects with limited economic returns.

Duke maintained that “strengthening these critical sectors would have a multiplier effect on the economy by improving human capital, supporting businesses, attracting investments and creating an enabling environment for sustainable development.”

He also called for sweeping reforms in Nigeria’s revenue generation system, energy policy, and administration of justice, arguing that the country had the resources required to achieve rapid economic transformation if they were properly managed.

“We are blessed with virtually every form of energy. Make energy available and affordable because that is the greatest stimulus for productivity.

“Combine that with prudent public spending, an efficient tax system and a judiciary that inspires confidence, and Nigeria can unlock its enormous economic potential,” he said.

On governance, Duke defended his leadership record in Cross River State, saying his tenure reflected a commitment to building institutions capable of outlasting individual administrations.

He said he would replicate the same philosophy at the federal level if elected, stressing that his administration would prioritise competence and integrity over political patronage.

According to him, political considerations should not determine who occupies critical government positions once elections are over.

“Politics ends after the election. Governance begins with assembling the best hands to move the country forward.

“Appointments should be based on competence and integrity, not political loyalty. Every public official must be committed to leaving the country better than they met it,” the former governor said.

Duke’s comments came amid continuing concerns over the cost of credit, public debt and the ability of businesses to access affordable financing, particularly as policymakers seek to balance inflation management with the need to stimulate economic activity.

He argued that Nigeria’s economic challenges could not be resolved through monetary policy alone, insisting that fiscal discipline, reliable energy supply, institutional reforms and access to affordable financing must work together to create the conditions required for businesses and households to thrive.

The PRP candidate further stressed the importance of restoring confidence in public institutions, saying investors would be more willing to commit capital to the country where the tax system was efficient, electricity was reliable, and the judiciary could provide timely and credible resolution of disputes.

Duke said his proposed reforms would ultimately be aimed at moving Nigeria from an economy constrained by high costs and weak productivity to one driven by investment, enterprise and sustainable economic expansion.

World.title: Journalists Urged to Harness AI to Transform Reporting
World.content:
The future of journalism is being reshaped by Artificial Intelligence (AI), offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance reporting, streamline workflows, and deliver more engaging content to readers worldwide.

The Chief Executive of Chesca Global Solutions Limited, Ms. Franca Ibuzo, stated this in a press statement, noting that “in automated news gathering, AI can scan vast amounts of data, social media feeds, and public records in real time, and help journalists identify breaking stories faster.”

According to her, during fact‑ checking and verification, with misinformation on the rise, AI tools assist in verifying sources, cross‑checking facts, and ensuring accuracy before publication.

She noted that “content personalisation and AI algorithms now tailor news delivery to readers’ interests, improving engagement and ensuring diverse perspectives reach the right audiences.”

Ibuzo added: “Multimedia enhancement, from generating graphics to transcribing interviews, AI reduces repetitive tasks, allowing journalists to focus on news writing.”

“Transcribing and translation are powered by AI, which enables newsrooms to break language barriers, making stories accessible to international audiences instantly.”

She, however, exphasised that “AI is not replacing journalists but rather it is empowering them.

“By leveraging AI responsibly, we can uphold the integrity of journalism while embracing innovation that makes reporting more efficient and impactful.”

“As media organisations adopt AI, ethical considerations remain paramount. Transparency, accountability, and human oversight are essential to ensure that technology strengthens trust rather than undermines it,” she said.

She urged “media organisations management to reiterate their commitment to advancing journalism through innovation by equipping reporters and editors with cutting‑edge tools to deliver credible, timely, and engaging news.”

World.title: No Backdoor Meeting Can Halt Rainbow Coalition, CRP Tells Nunieh, Others
World.content:
Concerned Rivers People (CRP) has said alleged meetings involving former Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Mrs Joy Nunieh, Gabriel Pidomson and Dumo Lulu-Briggs will not affect the Rainbow Coalition.

The group, in a statement signed by its Publicity Secretary, Sunny Nwagbo, on Sunday, alleged that Nunieh held a meeting with Pidomson and Lulu-Briggs at her residence to discuss issues relating to the coalition.

CRP stated the Rainbow Coalition had come to stay and insists no political manoeuvring would stop the coalition or, in its words, “the will of the people.”

CRP maintained that the Rainbow Coalition would remain focused on its political objectives despite the alleged meetings.

“Let it be known, the Rainbow Coalition has come to stay. These meetings and backdoor politics will not stop the will of the people,”

It added, “Also let us quickly send a reminder to Nunieh that she must be in a hurry to have forgotten so soon how she was saved from the pangs of (enemies) while in office.

CRP urged Nunieh to reflect on her previous political experiences, saying it was concerned that she may have forgotten.

World.title: AAAN Flags Of 21st Edition of LAIF Awards
World.content:
Raheem Akingbolu

The Association of Advertising Agencies of Nigeria (AAAN), the umbrella body for advertising professionals in Nigeria, has announced the kick-off of the 21st edition of the Lagos Advertising and Ideas Festival (LAIF). This announcement was made by the newly re-elected President of AAAN, Lanre Adisa, at a press conference in Lagos.

Also, a new leadership was unveiled for the Lagos Advertising and Ideas Festival Management Board. The newly appointed board members include: Funke Adekola, President; Jumoke Akinyele, Vice President; Victor Oyaroro; Tobi Williams; Rotimi Ade-Onajobi; Toheeb Balogun; Anne Obaseki; Dr. Meksley Nwagboh; Segun Akinyemiju; Sandra Amachree; Israel Obatunde; Olabisi Olusanya; and Jonathan Oyovwevotu.

Speaking at the press conference, Adisa described this year’s LAIF theme, “From Glitch to Great,” as not just a slogan but a powerful reminder that the path to greatness is rarely perfect.

“Every great idea faces obstacles. Every creative breakthrough is preceded by moments of doubt, disruption, experimentation, and even glitches. What distinguishes great creators is not the absence of challenges but the courage and resilience to learn, adapt, and keep creating. In many ways, it is the natural progression from grit through the inevitable glitches to greatness. That is the story of LAIF, and indeed, the story of creativity itself,” he said.

He noted that the AAAN remains committed to elevating LAIF from West Africa’s leading celebration of creativity to a globally respected benchmark for creative excellence, comparable to international award bodies such as Loeries, African Cristal, and Pitchers.

“That journey from glitch to great, from local acclaim to global relevance, will demand more from all of us: more originality, more craft, more innovation, and more courage to create ideas that can stand shoulder to shoulder with the very best in the world,” he said.

In her remarks, the newly elected President of LAIF Management Board, Funke Adekola, stated that the new board is committed to building on the previous board’s key learnings and structural momentum and to creating a festival that truly reflects where the industry has moved, as well as a governance structure that mirrors the modern creative economy.

Adekola stated that the new leadership will drive LAIF not only to establish itself as the champion of creative advertising but also as the ultimate benchmark for total business and cultural impact. She explained that the team is determined to position LAIF as the launchpad for the next operating system for African creativity, not just celebrating excellence but catalysing the future.

“As we step into a brand-new cycle today, we are not here merely to announce an award show. We are here to announce an evolution. This board stands on the shoulders of two decades of remarkable progress, and we are stepping into this season with a commitment to honour our past while fearlessly defining our future,” she said.

World.title: Deon Fourie drafted into Springbok squad
World.content:
Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has called up utility forward Deon Fourie to the national squad for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series. Image: SA Rugby website

Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has called up veteran utility forward Deon Fourie to the national squad for the forthcoming Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series following his return from a lengthy spell on the sidelines due to injury.

The 39-year-old Fourie, who doubles up as a loose forward and hooker, will join up with the squad in Johannesburg on Tuesday morning.

READ | Who is the oldest living Springbok?

His last Test for the Springboks was the 2023 Rugby World Cup final against New Zealand at the Stade de France in Paris, and he made a welcome return to top-class rugby in the Stormers’ clash in their RGR opener against the All Blacks on Friday night.



Invaluable experience

The Rugby World Cup-winner will add invaluable experience to Erasmus’ quality list of forwards for the historic series, which kicks off at Ellis Park in Johannesburg on Saturday, 22 August.

The match will mark the first of four Tests between the teams in the inaugural series, which will also see the teams meet at the Cape Town Stadium in Cape Town (29 August), the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg (5 September), and the M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore (12 September).

The Springboks travelled back to South Africa in two groups from Argentina on Sunday and Monday, with the last group scheduled to arrive in Johannesburg on Tuesday.

World.title: NSRI rescues woman after falling on Robberg Nature Reserve hiking trail
World.content:
A 20-year-old woman was rescued from the Robberg Nature Reserve near Plettenberg Bay after she was injured in a fall while running. Image: Facebook @SeaRescuePlettenbergBay

A 20-year-old woman was rescued from the Robberg Nature Reserve near Plettenberg Bay after she was injured in a fall while running on a hiking trail.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) Plettenberg Bay was activated at around 15:30 on Saturday, following reports of an injured woman near Fountain Shack.

An NSRI crew member who was already on Robberg reached the woman, who was visiting the area from Durban and had been running with local friends over the long weekend.



Her injuries were stabilised at the scene while rescuers considered the safest way to evacuate her.

READ | Routine NSRI training exercise turns into real-life rescue operation

Challenging sea conditions

Initially, NSRI and carrying her along the hiking trail to the car park. However, rescuers estimated that this would take considerable time.



At the same time, the heavy sea conditions made a rescue-craft extraction challenging.

NSRI crews investigated possible landing points at East Beach, Island Beach and Agterstrand before deciding that a boat evacuation was the safest option.

Additional rescuers responded to the NSRI Plettenberg Bay base, where the Spirit of Pilatus and Rescue Plett rescue craft were launched.



Despite 2 to 3 metre swells and 15-knot south-westerly winds, the crews managed to safely beach the rescue craft at Robberg Nature Reserve.

Medical treatment

An NSRI team then carried a Stokes basket stretcher to the injured woman, secured her inside it and transported her to the waiting rescue craft.

She was brought safely back to the NSRI rescue base without further incident.



The woman’s friends then transported her to hospital, where she received medical treatment for her injuries.

NSRI said she was later released from hospital and required no further medical care.

The rescue highlights the challenges faced by emergency crews operating along the rugged Robberg coastline, particularly when heavy swells and strong winds make access by sea difficult.

World.title: When is the next public holiday in South Africa?
World.content:
While South Africans are currently enjoying a day off work thanks to Women's Day, eyes will no doubt have already turned to when the next public holiday in the country falls. Image: Wikimedia Commons

While South Africans are currently enjoying a Monday off work thanks to Women’s Day, eyes will no doubt have already turned to when the next public holiday in the country falls.

National Women’s Day fell on Sunday, 9 August, meaning Monday, 10 August is being observed as a public holiday – and a long weekend.

As a reminder, if a public holiday occurs on a weekday (Monday to Friday), employees receive the day off.



But when a holiday falls on a Saturday, workers who normally do not work that day do not receive an additional day off, meaning the holiday is effectively ‘lost’.

If it falls on a Sunday, the following Monday is observed as a public holiday.

Next public holiday

The next official public holiday isn’t too far off.



Heritage Day will be celebrated on Thursday, 24 September. Widely known as ‘Braai Day’, it should be celebrated with an ice-cold beer and braai tongs in hand, no?

If you move fast, taking Friday, 25 September off work will give you a four-day weekend.

Public holidays in 2026

The number of public holidays in South Africa in 2026 will be 14.



However, South Africans have lost – and will lose – two of those holidays due to the fact that they fall on Saturdays.

Looking at the 2026 public holiday calendar, those public holidays falling on a Saturday are – or were:

Human Rights Day – 21 March 2026

Day of Goodwill – 26 December 2026

Below is the full list of remaining public holidays in South Africa for 2026:



24 September (Thursday) – Heritage Day

– Heritage Day 4 November (Wednesday) – Local Government Elections

– Local Government Elections 16 December (Wednesday) – Day of Reconciliation

– Day of Reconciliation 25 December (Friday) – Christmas Day

– Christmas Day 26 December (Saturday) – Day of Goodwill

Which is your favourite public holiday of the year?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: Beauty through subtraction: Mazda3 Astina review
World.content:
The Mazda3 Astina originally landed many moons ago (back in 2019) promising to trouble the Audi A3, BMW 1 Series and VW Gold. Revisit it today and that ambition still holds true, even if the entire hatch segment is more or less gone. Interestingly, the svelte bodywork hasn’t aged a day and still turns heads wherever it goes …

The Japanese firm calls the Mazda3 Astina design language ‘beauty through subtraction.’ Translation: no fussy creases, just continuous, deliberate surfacing. Granted, some of a cynical disposition still gripe about the low-slung nose making it look like an anteater (not me!). Nevertheless, most people just fix a stare and don’t let it go till it’s out of sight. Impressive for an eight-year-old design.

MAZDA3 ASTINA

Red and black with silver accents. It’s kind of old school but it still works. Central, none-touchscreen is showing its age though.

Climb inside and the maturity holds up, too. MZD Connect infotainment is a none-touchscreen, and a 7-inch screen and heads-up display remain standard across the range. Cabin colours stick to black or red, with silver detailing kept deliberately minimal. It’s still one of the calmer cockpits in the segment, free of the button clutter rivals piled on and then removed entirely over the years.



Sound-deadening and structural work keep noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) impressively low. The standard BOSE sound system, with front speakers relocated behind the firewall, remains a genuine highlight. Few cars sound this good, no matter if its doof, doof or hard rock blaring out!

NO TURBOS, NO HYBRID

Newer-engineered cars will offer more rear leg- and head- and luggage space for the purchaser, it must be said. Image: Ray Leathern

The mechanical story hasn’t changed either. No diesel, no turbo, no hybrid, just Mazda’s naturally aspirated Skyactiv-G petrol in 2.0-litre form. The Mazda3 Astina you see here accounts for 121 kW and 213 Nm of torque. This top-of-the-pile hatchback remains automatic-only, a six-speed unit doing all the work. No manual option, sadly, at this price point. This bummed us out at the launch, and still does. The ride quality, as ever for Mazda, remains genuinely impressive. It is composed, quiet, connected and unbothered by changing, rough surfaces. As is the inch-accurate steering.

The naturally aspirated 2.0-litre was never really the highlight, despite how bulletproof the engineers say it is. Whether at altitude or sea level, it still feels short of the sort of punch you’d expect from a genuine flagship model. And it leans on the thrashy side of life when asked to work hard for an overtake. It’s been many years since it launched, and we’ve really become accustom to the smooth torque fill of smaller capacity turbos and hybrid assistance.

THE VERDICT

This good-looking, low-fuss Japanese hatchback should be absolutely bombproof when it comes to reliability. Image: Ray Leathern

In conclusion, the Mazda3 Astina still looks like nothing else on the road. Bravo to the designers. However, in the intervening eight years, its price has moved up a cent or two: R629 700. While that sounds like a lot, balanced against inflation, its pricing is admirably consistent, and we still like it, perhaps in a nostalgic kind of way.

Nevertheless, you can always look for a tidy secondhand version and save a few bob. Given the choice, we would have introduced an old-school manual gearbox paired with that old-school naturally aspirated 2.0-litre engine. A manual shifter would elevate the car’s otherwise flat power delivery that makes driving feel sometimes like a chore when you’ve only got two pedals to work with.

World.title: Snow leaves motorists stranded as three Eastern Cape mountain passes CLOSED
World.content:
Several motorists have been left stranded after heavy snowfall forced the closure of three mountain passes in the Eastern Cape. Image: Eastern Cape Department of Transport

Several motorists have been left stranded after heavy snowfall forced the closure of three mountain passes in the Eastern Cape.

The Barkly Pass on the R58 between Khowa and Barkly East, Penhoek Pass on the N6 between Komani and Jamestown, and Boesmanshoek Pass between Sterkstroom and Molteno have all been closed as wintry conditions continue across the province.

Emergency personnel have been deployed to assist motorists trapped by the snow.



READ | Snow turns KwaZulu-Natal into a winter wonderland

Urged motorists

Eastern Cape Department of Transport spokesperson Unathi Binqose urged motorists to take the closures seriously and avoid attempting to travel through the affected routes.

“We urge road users, motorists in particular, to take these road closures very seriously, as they have been put in place for their safety.”



Binqose confirmed that several vehicles had become stuck in the snow, leaving occupants stranded.

“There are several vehicles that are stuck in the snow with people stranded in them, and we are doing everything we can to rescue them.”

Authorities are continuing to monitor other mountain passes across the Eastern Cape as snowfall affects several high-lying areas.



READ | Snow chase: Sutherland, here I come …

Swartberg Pass also closed

The snowfall has also reached the Western Cape, where snow has fallen on Swartberg Pass near Oudtshoorn in the Little Karoo.

The pass has been closed, with traffic officials warning motorists to stay away because of dangerous icy conditions.



Despite the closure, some vehicles have reportedly managed to travel through the pass, with families making their way to the area to see the snowfall.

Officials have warned that the thick layer of ice makes the route particularly dangerous and that motorists should not ignore the closure.

Freezing temperatures

The latest disruptions come as a widespread winter system continues to bring snow, freezing temperatures and hazardous driving conditions to parts of South Africa.



Motorists are urged to check road conditions before travelling, avoid non-essential journeys in affected areas and, most importantly, never attempt to bypass a road closure.

World.title: Who is the oldest living Springbok?
World.content:
Frik du Preez has the honour of being the oldest living Springbok according to the history books. Here's how old he is. Image: Blue Bulls

Following the news of the passing of former Springbok hooker Jacobus Frederick Beatrix “Piston” van Wyk, we got thinking: ‘Who is the oldest living Springbok?’

The answer?

A true legend of South African rugby: Frik du Preez.



At 90 years and 255 days, Du Preez is currently the oldest living Springbok, a little over 16 months older than Avril Malan.

Rugby great

Frederick Christoffel Hendrik “Frik” du Preez was more than a rugby great.

The former Springbok lock and flank was a player whose skill, personality and influence transcended provincial rivalries, earning him an enduring place in South African sporting history.

Despite retiring from international rugby in 1971, Du Preez was named South Africa’s Rugby Player of the 20th Century, an extraordinary recognition of the impact he had made during his career.

His popularity stretched far beyond his Northern Transvaal roots. At a time when provincial rivalries dominated South African rugby, Du Preez was admired from Pretoria to Cape Town and by supporters around the world.

A player ahead of his time

Du Preez possessed an extraordinary range of skills, particularly considering his size.



He was a powerful presence in the lineout, had pace and impressive running ability, and was one of the most accomplished kickers of his generation.

His versatility was perhaps best illustrated by his ability to punt, drop-kick and place-kick with equal confidence.

One of his most famous moments came against the British Lions in 1968.

After peeling around the front of a lineout, Du Preez collected the ball near the touchline and accelerated towards the try line. He then produced a perfectly executed sidestep before diving over to complete a spectacular try from around 40 metres.

It was the type of moment that captured the imagination of rugby supporters and helped cement his legendary status.

More than just a rugby player

Du Preez’s influence extended beyond what he achieved on the field.

Former Springbok great and administrator Danie Craven regarded him as one of the personalities who helped shape South African rugby.

Craven described Du Preez as one of the great players and personalities who had provided direction to generations of South African rugby supporters.

That admiration was reflected decades later when Du Preez was honoured as the country’s Rugby Player of the Century.

Former Springbok coach André Markgraaff also highlighted Du Preez’s character, suggesting that the legendary player would have been an ideal fit for the professional era because he could have demonstrated to modern players the value of humility.

A decade in the green and gold

Du Preez made his Springbok debut against England in January 1961 and remained an international player for more than a decade.

His final appearance for South Africa came against Australia in August 1971.

During that period, he became one of the country’s most capped players, sharing the Springbok record of 38 Test appearances with another legendary Northern Transvaal figure, loose forward Jan Ellis.

His overall record was even more remarkable when his non-Test appearances are taken into account. Du Preez played 87 matches for South Africa and scored 87 points.

That longevity was particularly impressive given the far smaller international calendar of the era.

Unlike today’s professional game, southern hemisphere nations did not have an annual Rugby Championship-style competition and international teams played considerably fewer Tests.

A place among rugby’s immortals

Du Preez’s legacy is not confined to South Africa.

When the Rugby Hall of Fame was established in 1997, he was one of only two South Africans inducted in its inaugural class, alongside Craven.

The company he joined underlined his standing in world rugby.

That group included some of the game’s greatest names, among them Gareth Edwards, Colin Meads, Hugo Porta, JPR Williams, Mike Gibson and Willie John McBride.

For a player whose international career had ended more than two decades earlier, his inclusion was a powerful acknowledgement of his contribution to the sport.

A legacy that endures

Du Preez’s election as South Africa’s rugby player of the 20th century ultimately reflected more than statistics.

It recognised a player who combined strength, skill and versatility with an unmistakable personality.

He could dominate a lineout, sprint 40 metres to score a try and then produce a match-winning kick.

But perhaps most importantly, he became a figure admired across the traditional boundaries of South African rugby.

Decades after his retirement, Frik du Preez remains one of the enduring symbols of Springbok rugby – a player whose influence continues to be felt long after his final appearance in the green and gold.

Factfile: Frik du Preez

Full names: Frederick Christoffel Hendrik du Preez Date of birth: 28 November 1935 Place of birth: Rustenburg School: Parys Springbok #375 Physical: 1.88m, 96.2kg Current age: 90

World.title: Camps Bay for retirees? Suburb with luxury coastal homes for 75% less
World.content:
Camps Bay is the crown jewel of Cape Town’s coast.

Being the jewel comes at a cost: R20 million to be exact.

Retirees who want a luxury coastal home have an alternative.



One Cape Town suburb has the lifestyle, amenities, view, and safety but not the price tag.

Suburb where Retirees can get Luxury Coastal Homes

Kommetjie is the newest suburb for wealthy retirees looking for value and space on the Atlantic Ocean.

According to Property24.com, homes in the area start at R4.9 million. But buyers could get on the property ladder for less.



As recently as July 2026, homes in Kommetjie have sold for R3 million.

Contrast this with Camps Bay.

According to Property24, the most affordable home sold in the last 30 days was R16 million.



This could be why shrewd retirees are selling their homes further afield and settling in Kommetjie.

Prices in this luxury coastal suburb are reminiscent of Camps Bay circa 2009.

Property Size Camps Bay Price Kommetjie Price Average R20 million R5.7 million < 200 sqm R7.5 million – R15 million R5.9 million – R6.1 million 201 – 500 sqm R11 million – R25 million R5.3 million – R10.5 million 501 – 800 sqm R15 million – R30 million R6.7 million – R13.5 million 801 sqm < R19.9 million – R65 million R4.9 million – R24 million

Beyond reasonable luxury homes, Kommetjie has cost-effective rates.



Rates and taxes in Camps Bay start at R2 000 for a modest 200-square-metre home.

For more space, rates skyrocket to R12 000.

Kommetjie rates start at R1 200 and typically max out at R2 500.



What to Do in Kommetjie

The suburb has the potential to become the next Camps Bay, but without the crowds.

Originally a quaint fishing town, Kommetjie has left that moniker in the dust and now has gorgeous sprawling properties within walking distance of the beach.

The suburb is lively but peaceful. There aren’t any large chain restaurants on the oceanside.



But that doesn’t mean retirees will have to say goodbye to an active lifestyle.

Long Beach offers roughly 8 kilometres of uninterrupted, powdery beaches, perfect for a morning walk or evening stroll.

On the beachfront, you have options like Espresso Coffee and Good Riddance Coffee Co.



Within a short drive, retirees can shop at Long Beach Mall, where there’s a Woolworths, Pick ‘n Pay Hypermarket, Food Lover’s Market, and an arts and crafts market on the first and last Saturday of the month.

Retail therapy doesn’t start and end at the mall.

There’s also Imhoff Farm, which offers experiential retail and restaurants.



Much like Camps Bay, Kommetjie has the most pleasant sunsets. The sky turns a gorgeous deep pink at sunset, with sunrise offering a diffuse orange and deep blue skyline.

Destination Driving Distance Long Beach 2 minutes Long Beach Mall 11 minutes Clovelly Country Club 21 minutes Mediclinic Constantiaberg 30 minutes Camps Bay 50 minutes

Kommetjie’s Property Prices are Rising

If you’re thinking of picking up property in Kommetjie, now might be the last time you can do so affordably.

According to Property24, prices in the area have been steadily increasing for years.



In 2025, the average property price was R3.795 million.

So far this year, the average price among the 66 sales in the area is R5.7 million.

Retirees aren’t the only group finding value in Kommetjie. Buyers aged 36 to 49 make up 41.2% of sales.



The suburb is benefitting from ever-increasing demand for affordable coastal living within the city limits.

This demand means it could become Cape Town’s new vibrant coastal community.

World.title: Fernando Da Cruz refuses to blame Brandon Petersen for goalkeeping howler
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz has refused to pin the club’s MTN8 quarter-final exit on goalkeeper Brandon Petersen. Image: Facebook @KaizerChiefs

Kaizer Chiefs coach Fernando Da Cruz has refused to pin the club’s MTN8 quarter-final exit on goalkeeper Brandon Petersen after Amakhosi suffered a 1-0 defeat to Golden Arrows at FNB Stadium on Sunday.

The Soweto giants returned to the MTN8 after a two-year absence, but their campaign came to an abrupt end as Golden Arrows secured their place in the semi-finals.



Caught off his line

The decisive moment arrived in the 53rd minute when Khulekani Shezi caught Petersen off his line with a cross-cum-shot from the right.

Shezi picked up the ball out wide before noticing Petersen’s advanced position and sent the ball towards the Kaizer Chiefs goal.

The effort beat the 31-year-old Amakhosi goalkeeper at his near post to give Arrows the lead.

However, Da Cruz was adamant that the defeat could not be blamed on one individual.

“I don’t want to say we lost because of one player,” the new Kaizer Chiefs coach told SuperSport TV.

Da Cruz said he would review the goal before making a definitive assessment, while suggesting Shezi may have intended to deliver a cross rather than attempt a direct shot.



“I will look at the goal because I will watch the game, but I think the player missed his cross and we lost it.”

Kaizer Chiefs failed to take their chances

For Da Cruz, the bigger frustration was Kaizer Chiefs’ inability to convert their opportunities after falling behind.

Amakhosi pushed for an equaliser but could not find the finishing touch needed to force the match towards extra time.

“The score is unfortunately the only one goal changed in the half and after that we tried to come back, but we had a lack of efficiency there.”

The result ends Kaizer Chiefs’ hopes of lifting the MTN8 trophy this season, while Arrows progress to the two-legged semi-finals.

For Amakhosi, there is little time to dwell on the disappointment.

Kaizer Chiefs return to FNB Stadium on Wednesday, 12 August when they face Sekhukhune United in their first home Betway Premiership fixture of the 2026/27 campaign.

Kick-off is at 19:30.

Da Cruz will now look for an immediate response from his side as Kaizer Chiefs turn their attention from cup disappointment to their league campaign.

Was Brandon Petersen to blame for the goal against Golden Arrows?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: MEC Maile calls on communities to help protect Gauteng schools
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Education MEC Lebogang Maile has said protecting schools is a shared responsibility.

Maile briefed the media on plans to curb issues affecting Gauteng schools.

He said issues around bullying, gender-based violence and gangsterism have been of great concern.

The department has embarked on a campaign called - it takes a village to raise a child.

“Violence, gangsterism, bullying, substance abuse, gender-based violence, vandalism and criminal activity around schools were repeatedly raised. The program of action strengthened Safe Schools intervention and cooperation with SAPs, community policing forums, NGOs and communities.

“Work is also being driven on anti-bullying interventions and misconduct measures while school safety matters are being assigned to the responsible education support and curriculum functions.

“The purpose is to move from responding only after incidents occur to prevention, early intervention, clear escalation and coordinated action around high-risk schools. Communities themselves remain essential to the solution. Protecting a school cannot be left entirely to government.

“The communities must help identify criminal activity, protect public infrastructure, support learner discipline and refuse to normalize drug dealing, vandalism and violence around schools."

World.title: MP Fadiel Adams expected to face tough questions at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Member of Parliament and National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams is set to testify under subpoena before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Tuesday.

He is expected to face tough questioning about the unauthorised disclosure of classified state documents and his allegations of systemic corruption in South Africa’s criminal justice system.

In just a few hours, Member of Parliament Fadiel Adams will take the hot seat at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry. This is exactly what Adams has demanded on social media: a chance to clear his name.

Adams is facing serious charges of fraud and defeating the administration of justice.

He’s also at the centre of IDAC scandals, including allegations that authorities used questionable information from Adams to pursue investigations against senior police officers.

IDAC State Advocate Drushantha Ramsamy testified that Adams ought to have been charged for being in possession of Crime Intelligence information.

Evidence before the commission revealed that Adams’s original complaint did not legally fall within IDAC’s mandate or trigger a valid investigation.

World.title: Holidaymakers stuck in Eastern Cape snow
World.content:
RHODES – What was meant to be a short time away from home for an East London family has resulted in an extended stay at snow-capped mountains in the hamlet of Rhodes.

Ainsley Sumner and his family had planned a little getaway at Tiffindell, but roads have been closed because of the snow.

“We will be stranded here for another day or two. It is nice and cold.

“We will have to wait it out. We will stay overnight to assess again before hitting the road back to East London where we are from.

“There is no point in trying to drive now as it will get dangerous,” Sumner said.

World.title: Police recover firearms linked to Reiger Park shooting
World.content:
GERMISTON – Police have recovered firearms linked to the Reiger Park murders on Friday night.

Two Anti-Gang Unit officers and two civilians were killed.

The firearms were recovered in Duka Thole, near Germiston.

On Sunday, Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia said the state would deploy all necessary resources to solve the crime.

This is a developing story.

World.title: Power cuts put oxygen-dependent residents at risk
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - Ongoing power cuts are putting the lives of vulnerable Padkamp residents at risk.

Ester Gerber's husband relies on an oxygen machine that needs electricity, while another resident had to move in with her son because she also needs oxygen.

The Buffalo City Metro has cut off electricity for the people living in this government housing community because Public Works owes the municipality.

Gerber said her sick husband needs electricity.

“As you can see, he's very, very sick. We are depending on electricity for his oxygen. Our doctor did apply to vital air for to get oxygen without being able to use electricity. But since up to now, we haven't heard anything.

“This is a very big concern to me because he's not the only one. There's also another lady. And she had to move in the second week, she had move to her son because she's also on oxygen. So, and I just feel it's not fair.

“Public Works came about a year ago and they told us that they are going to put in meters, but we are going be connected to BCM,” she said.

World.title: Stronger consequences needed for criminals – former gangster
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former gang member Ayoob Toffie has said visible policing can help reduce crime, but it’s not enough.

He said communities become frustrated when suspects are released on bail and later return to commit more crimes.

Toffie said stronger sentences are needed to deter people from crime.

“The police visibility is always there. It makes it difficult for any criminal to move around and do his things. However, it doesn't mean that it is going to stop. I think it would minimize it, but at the very same time, the community are tired of situations where cases are not being prosecuted, guys going out on bail.

“It’s a wicked cycle that keeps on repeating itself. For me, I were sentenced to a double life plus 16 years and I spent 21 years in prison. At the time when I was sentenced, there was no legal directive for any lifer to ever go out. And that pushed me to a point of thinking very deeply if I really want to continue with the crime or not. And because of the deterrence, because of this sentence that was played before me without any legal directive, it forced me to understand that my life is over."

Toffie said gangs are operating across different communities, with their influence extending beyond individual neighbourhoods.

He said their main aim is to control communities through fear, leaving residents afraid to move around freely, especially at night.

Toffie said while visible policing is good, it is not enough to deter criminals from committing crime.

“You'll find that there are gangs, gangsters, a group of gangs that is in Reiger Park, that's got the same gang in Nigel. And you've got the same game or a different gang in Westbury that has got the same gang in El Dorado Park.

“And so, it goes from one to the other, but the entire modus operandi of them all is control. It is to control and to bring fear to our communities. And that is what cannot be allowed because nobody can live in a community where they're fearful, they can't go at night. Our elderly, they can't walk around after five o'clock, six o' clock. Nobody can walk at that time because the control is now in the hands of the gangsters," Toffie said.

World.title: ‘There are gang ecosystems’ - Cape Crime Crisis Coalition
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The country’s criminal justice system is failing to protect communities.

That's the view of Cape Crime Crisis Coalition’s Llewellyn Macmaster.

He argued that poverty, unemployment, drugs and extortion are fertile ground,

for organised crime and gangs to thrive.

“We must start with the failure of the state in protecting the whole criminal justice system at the moment is broken, I think, and that contributes heavily to the failure. The other factor that we always mention is that the socio-economic conditions.

“They are drivers of gangsterism and organized crime and the drug, illicit drug trade. In our discussions, I mean, even the first submission that we made to Professor Cachalia when he met with us soon after his appointment was that you've got to look at gangs differently.

Macmaster believes gang violence does not need a one-size-fits-all approach.

“It's no longer just the street gangs of yesteryear. These are gang ecosystems. They have established alternative governance and economies in our communities. And with a high unemployment and poverty that's ravaging our communities, these organized criminals find a way to assert themselves in communities.

“And of course, when you add the whole issue of extortion, I think an easy way for elements to sort of put pressure on communities, on shebeens or taverns or informal businesses. I think that is what drives this. People have the sense, I think, that they can get away with it because the police are not successful. Yes, there are successes and every time acknowledge that, but clearly it is not enough,” he said.

World.title: Snow and very cold weather in some parts of SA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service is warning of disruptive snow and severe weather across several provinces as a cold front hits.

Snow is already reported in high-lying parts of the Western Cape.

The Weather Service warns the snowfall is likely to spread to parts of the Eastern Cape where it could close roads and temporarily cut off some communities.

Damaging winds and waves are also expected along the KwaZulu-Natal coast, while thunderstorms could affect parts of Gauteng and neighbouring provinces.

A cold front and cut-off low are bringing very cold conditions.

Residents and motorists are urged to take precautions as the weather system moves inland.

Heavy snowfall has trapped multiple vehicles and forced the closure of three Eastern Cape mountain passes: Barkly, Penhoek, and Boesmanshoek.

Weather forecaster Tokelo Chiloane said amaging winds and waves are also expected along the KZN coast with the snow already falling in the province, while thunderstorms could affect parts of Gauteng and neighbouring provinces.
