World.title: Crackdown on students, PM Modi's apology, Ram temple theft: Congress sets 3 non-negotiables for Parliament
World.content:
Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi has set three non-negotiable demands.

What govt said on Rahul's demand

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday restated his three demands, which he termed as"non-negotaibles", to break the Parliament deadlock.In his "unnegotiable list of demands", the Congress leader reiterated that the Union home minister Amit Shah must tell Parliament who ordered firing against students during NEET paper leak protest. He said, apart from Shah's statement, PM Modi should apologise for what happened and he called for an accountablity over the donation theft in Ayodhya Ram Mandir."The question was always that Amit Shah has to make it clear who authorised the shooting of our youngsters in Delhi. Pellet guns were fired, students were beaten with lathis with nails on them. He should come clean. Did he order it or did he not order it? If he ordered it, he is guilty of getting our children shot. And if he didn't know about it happening, he's incompetent. Either way, he should go. This was the discussion," Rahul Gandhi said in a presser.He further said: "Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi says, "The question was never that Mr Amit Shah is going to come and give a speech on some general topics in Parliament. Second, the Prime Minister apologises for what has happened. And third was the issue of the Ram temple theft.People very close to the Prime Minister have stolen from the Ram Mandir. These are the three issues."Rahul said opposition was not "interested in Amit Shah's fantasy conversations", saying: "We are interested in whether he authorised or didn't authorise the shooting of our children. First, he should make that abundantly clear. After that, the question of any discussion arises. That is the situation. And that is what the opposition is demanding. That is what we have been demanding for the last 15 days".Rahul Gandhi's remarks comes hours after Union Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said that home minister Amit Shah was prepared to respond in Parliament on the student protest crackdown. Rijiju, however, asked members not to disrupt the proceedings when the statement is made."The offer made by the government is very clear that it is ready to have a full and detailed discussion on students' movement and activities related to it," news agency ANI quoted Rijiju saying.Emphasising the need for an uninterrupted parliamentary process, Rijiju urged the opposition to hear the government's response before raising further issues."My only point made to the opposition is that while the discussion and a reply are being made, the opposition should not create disturbances to prevent the statement of the Home Minister," he added. "They must listen to the reply of the home minister and the government. Once discussion begins, we must have a threadbare discussion."

World.title: RSS coordination meeting of 32 outfits to be held in Andhra Pradesh from August 19-21
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The annual Akhil Bharatiya Samanvay Baithak, a coordination meeting of organisations inspired by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), will be held at Gudilova in

's Visakhapatnam district from August 19 to 21, the organisation said on Monday.

The three-day meeting will bring together senior office-bearers of 32 organisations associated with the Sangh, including their national presidents, general secretaries, organising secretaries and selected other functionaries, an RSS statement said.

RSS chief

, general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale, all Sahsarkaryawahs and national-level heads of various RSS departments will attend the meeting, it said.

Senior representatives of organisations including the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh, Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, Bharatiya Janata Party, Vishwa Hindu Parishad, Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, Saksham and Rashtra Sevika Samiti are expected to participate.

World.title: Right wing commentator TG Mohandas gets bail over controversial remarks on NEET student protest
World.content:
TG Mohandas' arrest was recorded on Monday morning after he was taken into custody.

ALSO READ |

What did he say

ALSO READ |

A court in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday granted bail to right-wing political commentator T G Mohandas, who was arrested over alleged remarks in a YouTube video concerning a student protest in New Delhi linked to the NEET paper leak.Mohandas was produced before the Thiruvananthapuram Additional Chief Judicial First Class Magistrate Court for remand proceedings. Judge Mithun Gopi G S granted him bail after hearing arguments from both sides.Police had taken Mohandas into custody from his residence in Mattancherry, Kochi, on Sunday evening. His arrest was formally recorded on Monday.The case has been registered under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Information Technology Act and the Kerala Police Act. The Thiruvananthapuram Cyber Police also informed the court that additional charges had been added for allegedly using words, sounds, gestures or objects intended to insult a woman's modesty, as well as for criminal intimidation involving severe threats.The prosecution asked the court to allow Mohandas to remain in custody for further investigation. It argued that he was an influential person who could potentially influence witnesses or interfere with evidence if released.His defence opposed the request, citing his age and health condition. His lawyer also argued that all the offences invoked against him were bailable.After considering the submissions, the court granted Mohandas bail. It directed him to appear before the investigating officer for three days as part of the ongoing probe and to appear before police whenever required.The court also ordered him not to repeat a similar offence while he remains on bail.The case stems from a complaint against videos posted on Mohandas' YouTube channel, 'Pathrika'. The complaint alleged that the videos were capable of disturbing public order and creating fear and unrest.In one of the videos, Mohandas allegedly said the Delhi students' protest "could lead to incidents of gang rape" and claimed that there would be no complaints because "those attending the protest like rape and there are girls who enjoy being raped".He further claimed that although some people would be killed or permanently injured, the situation would be brought under control within hours and the bodies shifted to hospitals.

World.title: After Rahul's 'fifth row' seat last year, government says LoP to sit after ministers on Independence Day
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Defence secretary RK Singh on Monday said leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15 and will be seated immediately after the Union Cabinet ministers."Leader of opposition has been invited, and his seating would be as per the Table of Precedence, which is exactly after Cabinet ministers," Singh told news agency ANI.The clarification comes after Congress criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over Rahul Gandhi's seating arrangement during the Independence Day celebrations last year, alleging that he was seated in the "fifth row" and calling the move a display of "pettiness" and a disregard for democratic norms.Officials from the ministry of defence, which organises the event, said the seating was arranged "according to the Table of Precedence".Congress had also accused the Centre of violating established protocol and undermining democratic decorum after Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge were seated in the third row during the Republic Day celebrations earlier this year.As per protocol, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha has a rank equivalent to that of a Cabinet minister.According to the Warrant of Precedence issued by the President's Secretariat, seating arrangements at state and ceremonial occasions are decided based on constitutional rank and office, and not political affiliation.The Table of Precedence is a protocol list that applies to state and ceremonial occasions, including national events such as Republic Day celebrations, and has no application to the day-to-day functioning of the government.Under Article 7 of the Table of Precedence, the Leaders of opposition in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are placed alongside Union Cabinet ministers, after the Speaker of Lok Sabha, the Chief Justice of India and former prime ministers.

World.title: Watch: Jharkhand protesters echo Bihar, dance as police turn water cannons on them
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Echoing scenes from Bihar where student protesters recently danced under police water cannons, Jharkhand job aspirants on Monday broke followed suit as police turned water cannons on them during their 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march in Ranchi.

Thousands of protesters breached multiple barricades while marching towards the Jharkhand assembly over alleged recruitment exam irregularities, prompting police to use water cannons, tear gas shells and lathi charges.

Tensions escalated when the protesters reached the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple, on the road leading to the assembly.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Police used water cannons to disperse the gathering, followed by lathi charges when protesters attempted to move forward.

Several rounds of tear gas shells were also fired when the crowd came within around 200 metres of the assembly.

The protest comes as the agitation led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch entered its 17th day. The march began around 10.30am from outside the old assembly building and coincided with chief minister Hemant Soren's 51st birthday.

The scenes in Ranchi came weeks after student protesters in Bihar similarly danced under police water cannons during a march towards the chief minister's residence over alleged examination paper leaks, unemployment and recruitment irregularities.

In Patna, protesters had broken into dance as water jets were used to stop them from advancing, while others sat on the road and raised slogans.

World.title: 'US has similar laws': Indian envoy Vinay Kwatra clarifies FCRA Bill, shares 'myth vs reality' check
World.content:
Kwatra issued a âMyth vs. Reality checkâ on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill.

âFCRA does not target any religionâ

âForeign money inflows have been risingâ

âUS has FARA, FATCAâ

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Monday defended the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), saying the changes are aimed at improving transparency, governance and oversight of foreign funds.In a series of posts on X on Monday, Kwatra issued a âMyth vs. Reality checkâ on the proposed FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, amid concerns raised by sections of civil society and a US lawmaker over the legislation.Kwatra said regulating foreign financial flows in public and political spaces was a sovereign measure driven by national security concerns and was common in several democracies.âTruth: Regulation of foreign financial flows in public and political spaces is a sovereign step driven by national security concerns. It is an accepted feature of modern governance in many democracies around the world,â he said.Responding to the claim that India was framing a new law to cut off foreign aid to civil society, Kwatra said the proposed legislation did not prohibit Indians from receiving foreign donations or seek to shut down law-abiding organisations.âThe fact is that the law does not forbid Indians from receiving foreign donations or shut down law abiding civil society.Tens of thousands of associations are registered under FCRA and routinely receive foreign funds for health, education, disaster relief, research and humanitarian work,â he said.Kwatra said the FCRA was first enacted in India in 1976 and replaced by a new framework in 2010. It was subsequently strengthened through amendments in 2016, 2018 and 2020.âThe 2026 Bill and Rules are the next step in the same direction: more transparency, better governance, clearer rules,â he said.Kwatra also rejected allegations that the FCRA amendments "specifically target a particular religion or community."âTruth: Nothing could be farther from it. The Act applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion, community or ideology,â he said.He added that faith-based welfare activities, including religious education, maintenance of places of worship and charitable work by organisations of all faiths, would continue to be eligible for foreign funding.Kwatra also rejected claims that the FCRA had adversely affected NGOs and charitable organisations or that the proposed amendments would further restrict their operations.âTruth: In reality, foreign money inflows into India have been rising, not falling. Foreign contributions to registered organisations grew from roughly $1.2 billion in 2010â11 to $2.67 billion in 2024â25,â he said.He said India has more than 3 million NGOs, while only 14,450 have FCRA registration, arguing that the overwhelming majority of civil society organisations fall outside the ambit of the Act.âFCRA does not stop anyone from accepting foreign charity, research grants or humanitarian aid. It asks three things â register, receive the money through laid down process, report what you did with it,â Kwatra said.Addressing concerns that the proposed law would allow the government to seize assets of NGOs, religious charities, places of worship, hospitals and schools dependent on foreign donations, Kwatra said the provision regarding assets was not new.âWhen a registration is cancelled or surrendered, foreign contributions and the assets created from them already vest in a State Government authority. This has been in force since 2010. It is not new,â he said.According to Kwatra, the 2026 Bill proposes to create a designated authority to safeguard such assets and also provides a mechanism for their return if an organisation restores its FCRA registration.âWhat the 2026 Bill adds is a designated authority to safeguard those assets â and a way back. If the organisation restores its registration, all assets and unused funds are returned in full,â he said.He also said the proposed legislation contains specific provisions for places of worship.âPlaces of worship carry their own protection. Where a cancelled association has created property connected to a place of worship, that property goes to another FCRA-registered association of the same faith to ensure continuity of worship,â Kwatra said.Kwatra also dismissed the argument that India was an outlier in regulating foreign funding, pointing to similar laws in other countries.âTruth: The US has had FARA since 1938 and FATCA since 2010. Australia legislated in 2018, Canada in 2024. The UK's scheme came into force in July 2025. The EU is legislating now,â he posted on X.His comments came days after a US lawmaker raised concerns over the proposed FCRA amendments, claiming that the legislation could allow the Indian government to take control of churches and charities.The FCRA Bill, 2026 proposes to empower the government to create a âDesignated Authorityâ to take over the management of foreign contributions and assets created using such contributions when an organisation's FCRA registration is cancelled, surrendered or ceases because it is not renewed.The Bill also states that where such assets constitute a place of worship, the Designated Authority must ensure that its religious character is maintained.

World.title: 'Diplomatic premises are inviolable': India condemns embassy defacement in Slovenia
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Monday condemned the defacement of the Indian Embassy premises in Slovenia's Ljubljana, by "anti-India elements", and urged Slovenian authorities to take action against those responsible.

In a statement, the MEA said, "We condemn the defacement of the premises of our Embassy in Ljubljana, Slovenia by anti-India elements."

Highlighting the protections accorded to diplomatic missions under international law, the ministry said, "Under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The MEA said it has taken up the matter with Slovenian authorities in both New Delhi and Ljubljana and called for those behind the incident to be held accountable.

"We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubjlana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable," it said.

The ministry also urged law enforcement agencies in other countries to remain alert as hateful propaganda and disinformation being circulated by such groups.

"We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," the MEA said.

World.title: Harish Rao urges govt. to fill reservoirs, MI tanks of Kaleshwaram project
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) senior leader and Deputy Floor Leader in the Assembly T. Harish Rao demanded that the government fill Annapurna, Ranganayakasagar, Mallannasagar, Kondapochammasagar and Nrusimhasagar reservoirs with water from Mid Manair and ensure water for irrigation to about 4 lakh acres under them.

In a letter addressed to Minister for Irrigation N. Uttam Kumar Reddy on Monday, he said the five reservoirs of the Kaleshwaram Project could be given water since the Mid Manair reservoir has about 22 tmc ft storage now against its full capacity of 27.5 tmc ft. It is being filled by pumping water from Yellampally through Nandi and Gayathri pump houses of the Kaleshwaram Project and it would get more water since Yellampally was getting good inflows with rains in the upstream areas.

After filling the five reservoirs with water from Mid Manair, the minor irrigation tanks and check-dams linked to them could be filled without any delay to irrigate 4 lakh acres ayacut assuring the farmers get a good crop. Similarly, Lower Manair Dam could also be filled with water from Mid Manair to give water for irrigation to the ayacut in SRSP Stage-2.

He brought to the minister’s notice that the 4 lakh acres ayacut was given water in the last Rabi season by filled the reservoirs and MI tanks, check-dams linked to them. He stated that filled the five reservoirs and MI tanks linked to them would protect the interests of the farming community of the ayacut.

(eom)

World.title: Jharkhand students protest LIVE: Protestors reach State Assembly premises; police use tear gas, water cannons
World.content:
Police used water cannons, lobbed tear gas shells, and lathi-charged job aspirants as they breached barricades and attempted to reach the State Assembly, protesting the recruitment exam irregularities. Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for nine days in protest against exam irregularities, also joined the march, despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Jharkhand Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

Also read: For Jharkhand’s Adivasi youth, competitive exams are about finding a voice in the system that governs them

The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups. However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue. The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protesters that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, said they want cancellation of JSSC-CGL and all exams connected to the TSR Data Processing Private Limited Agency, a blacklisted entity.

World.title: Top news of the day: Jharkhand protesters face lathis, tear gas as they march to Assembly; Lok Sabha passes Tribunals Reforms Bill without debate, and more
World.content:
Protestors reach State Assembly premises; police use tear gas, water cannons

Police used water cannons, lobbed tear gas shells, and lathi-charged job aspirants as they breached barricades and attempted to reach the State Assembly, protesting the recruitment exam irregularities. Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for nine days in protest against exam irregularities, also joined the march, despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Jharkhand Chief Minister Shibu Soren.

Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 passed in LS without discussion

The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 10, 2026) passed the 'Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026’, without discussion, amidst heavy sloganeering by the Opposition MPs. The Rajya Sabha returned the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 through a voice vote. Earlier, the upper house passed The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026’, through a voice vote.

Not turbulence: Air India A320 suffered rare flight-control event before 300-foot altitude drop

The Phuket–Delhi flight that experienced a “momentary loss in altitude” on August 4, injuring 17 people on board, was preceded by a cascade of failures involving the aircraft’s hydraulic and flight-control systems, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter, contradicting the airline’s initial attribution of the incident to turbulence. Nearly 2.5 hours after taking off from Phuket at 6.56 a.m., Air India flight AI 2379 operated on an Airbus A320neo was hit by a cascade of technical failures at 9.32 a.m. IST, involving the aircraft’s hydraulic and flight-control systems.

Russia’s share in India’s oil imports jumps to all-time high of 48%, even as U.S. readies 100% tariffs

At a time when the U.S. looks all set to enact legislation to impose a tariff of up to 100% on India for its Russian oil imports, an analysis of the latest data shows Russia’s share in India’s oil imports rose to an all-time-high of 48% in June 2026. At a time when the U.S. looks all set to enact legislation to impose a tariff of up to 100% on India for its Russian oil imports, an analysis of the latest data shows Russia’s share in India’s oil imports rose to an all-time-high of 48% in June 2026.

Amidst tension in India-Bangladesh relations, High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi calls on PM Tarique Rahman

Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Monday (August 10, 2026) called on Prime Minister of Bangladesh Tarique Rahman amid tensions in bilateral relations generated after exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina addressed a virtual press conference here on August 5, in which she criticised Mr. Rahman’s government. Diplomatic sources in New Delhi have interpreted the meeting as a positive development, as it came at a time when Dhaka is also hosting a high-level security-related delegation from India. Sources further informed that the meeting was cordial and that the Bangladeshi side consisted of Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and Foreign Affairs Adviser to the PM Humayun Kobir. High Commissioner Trivedi was accompanied by Deputy Chief of Mission Pawan Badhe.

Supreme Court allows Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for eye treatment

The Supreme Court on Monday (August 10, 2026) permitted Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for three weeks for eye treatment while noting that every individual has a right to travel abroad and choose the medical assistance he wants to receive. A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was hearing a petition filed by Mr. Banerjee against a Calcutta High Court order refusing a restriction imposed on him to travel abroad. The travel restriction was imposed on him in a case concerning an alleged provocative remark made during the 2026 State Assembly election campaign while staying his arrest.

Tamil Nadu Assembly adopts resolution for ‘Tamil Thai Vazhthu’ to be sung first at events

The Tamil Nadu Assembly on Monday (August 10, 2026) unanimously adopted a resolution for Tamil Thai Vazhthu to be mandatorily sung first before the commencement of programmes in all educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings, and other public institutions in the State. The government resolution, moved by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, emphasised that Tamil Thai Vazhthu was an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture.

Supreme Court agrees to Tamil Nadu government’s plea for early hearing of Cauvery water dispute

The Tamil Nadu Government, headed by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay on Monday (August 10, 2026) sought an early hearing of its application over the Cauvery water allocation dispute with neighbouring Karnataka. Appearing before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, senior advocate C.S. Vaidyanathan, for Tamil Nadu, highlighted the deficit in allocation of the river water has left farmers in a perilous situation.

SC proposes special courts to exclusively hear CBI, NIA cases on Manipur ethnic violence

The Supreme Court on Monday (August 10, 2026) proposed Special Courts to exclusively hear Manipur ethnic violence cases investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the National Investigation Agency (NIA). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made a request to the Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court to constitute Special Courts, separately to hear CBI and NIA cases linked to the 2023 Manipur violence on a day-to-day basis.

Iran ties Strait of Hormuz reopening to U.S. concessions on several demands

Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman to define new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz, but reiterated that the U.S. must meet other conditions, including compensation and an end to sanctions and military threats, before the strategic waterway is reopened. A U.S. official told Reuters on August 7, 2026, that Iran and Oman were close to a deal that ⁠could pave the way for restoring safe passage through the strait, a major conduit for oil and gas shipping before Iran blocked Hormuz in response to U.S. and Israeli attacks on Tehran that began in late February.

World.title: Water level in Papanasam dam stands at 83.60 feet
World.content: The water level in Papanasam dam on Monday stood at 83.60 feet (the maximum level is 143 ft.) with an inflow of 1,282.33 cusecs and a discharge of 475 cusecs. The level in Manimuthar dam was 67.17 ft. (118 ft.) with an inflow of 53.68 cusecs and a discharge of 225 cusecs.

World.title: Cabinet to discuss drought situation, crop loss on August 13: Priyank Kharge
World.content:
As crops wither across rain-deficient parts of the State, the drought-like situation and mounting crop losses will come up for discussion at the State Cabinet meeting on Thursday, Minister for Home, IT-BT and e-Governance and Kalaburagi district in-charge Minister Priyank Kharge said here on Monday.

Mr. Kharge stated that the State had recorded a rainfall deficit of approximately 75%, with the situation attributed to the impact of the “Super El Niño” phenomenon. He was speaking after inspecting rain-hit agricultural fields in the Aurad (B) village of Kalaburagi taluk.

The Minister visited the fields of Vimalabai Ambaraya and Shakuntala Suryakant, where crops had withered.

Ms. Vimalabai appealed to Mr. Kharge for compensation, saying she had spent about ₹50,000 on DAP fertiliser and seeds to sow black gram, only to lose the crop to the prolonged dry spell. She had sown red gram on another four acres, but feared that the crop too would fail if the drought situation continued.

Mr. Kharge said the Chief Minister had directed Ministers to visit drought-affected areas in their respective districts and submit reports. “Accordingly, I have come here for a field visit,” he added.

He later visited Kere Bhosga village and inspected the field of Shabbir Ahmed, where red gram had been sown twice following the failure of the first crop.

State seeks relaxation of NDRF norms

Mr. Kharge said Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had already written to the Centre highlighting the drought situation in the State. The stringent provisions governing assistance under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) were making it difficult for the State to provide adequate compensation to farmers, he expressed.

“The State has been seeking a simplification of the NDRF norms to ensure that farmers receive fair compensation. The Centre should consider this demand,” Mr. Kharge reiterated.

Kalaburagi district received a record ₹650 crore in compensation last year, making it the second-highest recipient in the country, Mr. Kharge said. This year, nearly 4.5 lakh farmers in the district have so far enrolled under the crop insurance scheme.

Farmers had complained that adequate compensation did not reach nearly 20% of the gram panchayat areas last year, Mr. Kharge said. “I have issued strict instructions to the Revenue and Agriculture Department officials to ensure that this is not repeated this year,” he said.

On drinking water, Mr. Kharge said ₹1 crore had been allocated to each Assembly constituency in the district. “There is no shortage of funds for drinking water supply,” he said.

Another ₹5 crore had already been released for drinking water requirements in rural areas, he added.

Legislators Allamprabhu Patil, Basavaraj Mattimadu, Thippannappa Kamaknoor, Deputy Commissioner Ikram Shareef, IGP Shantanu Sinha, Kalaburagi City Police Commissioner S.D. Sharanappa, Superintendent of Police, Adduru Srinivasulu and Joint Director of Agriculture Samad Patel were present.

World.title: Bengaluru police seize drugs worth ₹55.80 crore, arrest 39 in citywide crackdown
World.content:
The city police have seized drugs worth ₹55.80 crore and arrested 39 drug peddlers, including eight foreign nationals, 21 people from other states, and 10 locals, as part of a special crackdown against narcotics.

The operation was carried out across several police station limits in the city. The police said the accused were procuring banned drugs at low prices from foreign, inter-state, and unidentified suppliers and selling them at higher prices to the public, including college students.

According to Bengaluru City Commissioner of Police Seemant Kumar Singh, the seized narcotics included 21.641 kg of MDMA, 738 g of cocaine, 4.493 kg of hydroponic weed, 184.625 kg of weed, 1.065 kg of opium, 25 g of mephedrone, along with 22 mobile phones and five two-wheelers. Police also seized ₹17 lakh in cash from the accused.

The 39 accused were produced before courts on different dates and remanded in judicial custody, the Police Commissioner said, adding that the police are continuing efforts to trace the unidentified persons who allegedly supplied drugs to the accused.

Prominent cases

The Girinagar police arrested a French national, Demba Jouma Francis, and seized 4.378 kg of MDMA, valued at around ₹10.36 crore, the police said. According to the police, the accused had established contact with African drug suppliers in Delhi, procured drugs at a low price, and transported them to Bengaluru. He was allegedly staying in a rented house at Shivakote in Yelahanka and selling the drugs. Similarly, the Amruthahalli police seized 14.436 kg of MDMA, valued at approximately ₹28.88 crore, and have taken up further investigation.

In a similar operation, the Anti-Narcotics Wing of the Central Crime Branch (CCB) arrested four persons, including foreign nationals, in connection with three cases and seized drugs worth approximately ₹8.88 crore. The seizure included 738 g of cocaine, 336 g of MDMA, and 82.305 kg of ganja, alongside two two-wheelers and three mobile phones. In another operation, Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) police seized 4.278 kg of hydro ganja, valued at around ₹3 crore, in three cases.

The Yeshwanthpur police seized 650 g of MDMA and 41.446 kg of ganja, valued at approximately ₹1.71 crore, in two cases. Police also seized a two-wheeler and three mobile phones. The Yelahanka police seized 794 g of MDMA, worth around ₹1.59 crore, along with two mobile phones.

World.title: GalaxEye acquires Bengaluru-based spacecraft engineering company StarOps
World.content:
Space tech startup GalaxEye has acquired StarOps, a Bengaluru-based spacecraft engineering company.

GalaxEye, which is building next-generation Earth Observation capabilities through its proprietary OptoSAR, said the acquisition marks a significant milestone in its journey to becoming a fully integrated space technology company.

It said that the integration brings StarOps’ proprietary technologies, qualified satellite platforms and deep systems engineering expertise, along with an experienced engineering team, several of whom previously worked at TeamIndus on the Lunar Lander and Rover.

“Their end-to-end experience from mission design through End-of-Life further strengthens GalaxEye’s capabilities across the satellite value chain,” it said.

Incorporated in 2022, StarOps was established to develop satellite platforms and indigenize critical spacecraft technologies in India.

GalaxEye said that the StarOps team brings proficiency across spacecraft systems engineering, mission operations, propulsion, avionics, flight computing, guidance and navigation, structures and mechanisms, electrical systems, programme management and ground operations.

“The team is further supported by a panel of veteran ISRO experts with extensive experience in designing, qualifying and delivering complex space programmes,” it said.

It noted that the integration adds a strong portfolio of indigenous spacecraft technologies and engineering know-how to GalaxEye. These include qualified satellite bus platforms across the 50 kg, 150 kg and 250 kg classes, proprietary subsystem technologies, qualification heritage, testing infrastructure and engineering tools.

Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO, GalaxEye, said, “By welcoming this exceptional team and their technologies into GalaxEye, we are significantly strengthening our capabilities across satellite engineering. Together, we are building a company capable of designing, engineering and operating advanced space systems from India for the world.”

“We’re now bringing that experience to GalaxEye, and I’m excited to see our work become part of its ambitious mission to develop and deploy a constellation of OptoSAR satellites. It’s a privilege to contribute to a mission that has the potential to push the boundaries of what Indian space technology can achieve,” Nirmal Suraj Gadde, co-founder and Missions Lead, StarOps said.

World.title: Group flags online terror threat issued against Pandits in Kashmir, seeks probe
World.content:
A Kashmir Pandit organisation on Sunday (August 9, 2026) expressed concerns over purported online threats issued by terrorists to Pandits living in the valley and demanded a probe. It said the threats have “forced many minority community employees” working in the in the Muslim-majority Jammu & Kashmir to “go on leave”.

A spokesperson of Panun Kashmir, one of the Jammu-based organisations of Kashmiri Pandits, said a purported threat communication dated August 7, 2026 and issued in the name of the United Liberation Council “has specifically named members of the Kashmiri Pandit community and disclosed their telephone numbers”.

“The communication represented a serious escalation because it went beyond generic threats and appeared to identify individuals as potential targets while claiming access to information about their families, locations and places of work,” said Agnishekhar, convenor of Panun Kashmir.

Mr. Agnishekhar demanded an investigation into the authenticity of the claims made in the letter. He also urged J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha “to immediately direct the police and security agencies to undertake a comprehensive threat assessment of all persons named in the communication and their immediate families”.

Official sources said scores of Kashmiri Pandits working in Kashmir under the Prime Minister’s package have left the valley in the face of the fresh threat. They said departments in “volatile and sensitive locations” in Kashmir have allowed Pandit employees to go on leave till August 20. However, there has been no official communication from the government.

The Pandit organisation also sought appropriate security measures for the individuals identified in the communication and a review of the security of Kashmiri Pandit employees working in sensitive government departments.

Referring to the letter, Mr. Agnishekhar said it needed to be established whether the perpetrators actually possessed such information or were “attempting psychological warfare”. “The authorities must investigate the source of the information, the digital trail behind the communication and whether any surveillance, profiling or reconnaissance of the targeted persons has taken place,” he added.

A sense of fear returned to Kashmir after terrorists killed one policeman and two non-local labourers in south Kashmir in the past 20 days in two separate targeted killings. According to police sources, a local Lashkar-e-Taiba militant could be involved in these targeted killings.

JeI premises searched

Meanwhile, the J&K police conducted coordinated searches at 26 locations across Sopore in north Kashmir in connection with the cases registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against the banned socio-religious organisation Jamaat-e-Islami (JeI).

“The searches were carried out at residential and other premises linked to the JeI leaders, members and activists across different areas of Sopore. During the searches, incriminating documents, literature and electronic devices were recovered and seized from various premises. The seized material is being examined as part of the ongoing investigation to ascertain further linkages and activities connected with the proscribed organisation,” said the police.

The police said the operation forms part of sustained efforts to dismantle networks and ecosystems associated with proscribed organisations and separatist activities and to take firm action against activities “prejudicial to the security, sovereignty and integrity” of the nation.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact ‘entirely for defensive purposes’, not aggression
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday affirmed that the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz recalled that he, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact in Makkah on Friday.

The prime minister stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

“Its purpose is definitely not that any aggression occurs. It is entirely for defensive purposes, for peace, tranquillity and progress in the region,” he affirmed.

The premier noted that while Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already entered the “Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement” in September 2025, Islamabad and Ankara also had “arrangements for decades” between them.

PM Shehbaz recalled that the Pakistani nation and the army had been honoured to “defend the world’s holiest places” of Makkah and Madina for years along with the Saudi forces.

“Last year, with Allah’s grace, this arrangement was officially recognised so that a proper agreement was signed. Friday’s agreement is another extension of it, with a trilateral agreement signed.”

More to follow

World.title: Sindh govt defers judicial commission decision on Mir Raza Ali murder case probe
World.content:
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Monday the provincial government had deferred the decision on the formation of a judicial commission to probe the Mir Raza Ali murder case.

Lanjar made the announcement on X, saying that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab had spoken to Ali’s family, who had expressed “confidence in the new police team” constituted to investigate the case and was of the view that it should conduct the probe.

“Therefore, the decision of establishing a judicial commission has been deferred for the time being,” the home minister said.

An IBA graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report after the exhumation and a second postmortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide.

On Sunday, PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission to probe the case, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Lanjar and Wahab had reached Ali’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar had said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case.

However, Jibran Nasir, the family’s lawyer, posted on X that they had not requested or consented to any judicial commission.

“Nor do we believe it’s required at this stage. A new investigation team has been formed, which the family will meet tomorrow. The Sindh government should not try to create hurdles/confusion in the name of ‘facilitation,’“ he said.

He had earlier also objected to the initially constituted police team probing the case and demanded that it be replaced.

Speaking to the media on Saturday after the results of the second autopsy came out, he had said that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team.

Subsequently, the Sindh inspector general of police’s office notified on Sunday the reconstitution of the investigating team probing the case. The order to this effect said the new investigation team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem.

The same day, Karachi police chief Azad Khan also suspended Sharea Faisal Sub-divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after Ali’s body was found.

The city police chief also ordered the case be transferred to Zaman Town Police Station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was initially registered.

Controversy over autopsy

The latest developments in the case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination.

Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel last week that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs.

The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another.

The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case.

Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation.

The statement, however, said that exhumation of the body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission.

On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed.

But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts.

The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday.

After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said.

She said the body bore “injuries in the right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in the mouth and throat”.

World.title: 3rd phase of AJK elections: Polling concludes in Poonch Division's Bagh, Haveli districts
World.content:
Polling in four constituencies of Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts concluded on Monday as part of the third phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections.

Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Citing law and order concerns, the Election Commission had decided to postpone polling in Bagh and Sudhnoti districts that was originally set for today.

On Monday, polling began at 8am and continued until 5pm in four Poonch constituencies. The PPP, which has accused the PML-N of rigging in the previous phases, continued to make similar allegations on Monday as well.

In response, PML-N leaders said the PPP had no evidence for its claims, and reiterated their confidence to form the government in AJK based on the seats it has already secured so far.

The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. On the other hand, the PPP has only won 10 constituencies so far.

The third phase of the AJK elections was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Government officials had anticipated clashes in some areas today, while the Election Commission had classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive.

“Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier

Malpractice, rigging allegations

Polling in previous phases of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging, scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — the main contenders in AJK but allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words.

The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging and electoral malpractices in the previous phases. It continued to allege rigging in Haveli and Bagh as well.

In a series of posts on X, the PPP shared complaints it said it had filed to the Election Commission.

In one of the complaints, the PPP alleged that roads leading to the Banni Marasira area had been blocked, where PML-N supporters were illegally stamping ballot papers at 12 polling stations in the LA-15 constituency.

“The commission is requested to consider the two acts together rather than separately, because the second is made possible by the first,” the party said, adding that officials, voters, polling agents and party workers were unable to reach the polling stations “to see what is being done inside”.

The party also claimed delays in polling at LA-15’s polling station no.87 in Thub. It also alleged that polling at stations no.143 and 144 in Hatala Pader did not commence on time due to the non-arrival of polling staff.

The PPP also alleged that its polling agent was “forcibly removed” from LA-15’s station no.158 in Makhdoom Kot. Similarly, PPP’s agents had also been removed from polling stations no.8-14 in Bani Maldhara and PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers at those stations, the party alleged.

At around 12:45, the party claimed on X that workers of Jamaat-i-Islami had gathered to “capture” 26 polling stations in the constituency — nos.31-38, nos.70-79 and nos.180-186. It said the police had initially arrived but then withdrew.

“The stations are, therefore, unguarded at this moment, with an organised body assembled against them.”

It urged the Election Commission to determine on whose orders police had withdrawn and direct the law enforcers to return to the station.

The PPP also posted a blurry video, which it said was of PML-N workers “attacking” the polling station set up at the Boys Middle School in LA-15 Central Bagh.

Regarding LA-16, the party claimed that its polling agents were not being allowed inside stations no.119 and 120 while PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers inside the stations in the agents’ absence.

The PPP further alleged delays in polling at stations no.61 and 141 of the constituency.

It made similar allegations regarding polling stations no.109 and 110 in LA-16 Bagh-III Sharqi. Moreover, the party accused “armed individuals associated with the PML-N” of opening fire at polling station no.179, Kot Chinalla in the constituency and disrupting the election process.

“The polling agents of the PPP have been removed from the station. It is further alleged that ballot papers are being stamped lawfully,” the PPP added.

In LA-17, the party alleged that its agents had been “forced out” from the polling station in Mullah Basti, Kahuta City by PML-N workers.

PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman expressed reservations after reports of rigging and malpractices emerged, saying that preventing polling agents from entering polling stations in LA-16 raised “serious questions” about the transparency of the election process.

In a statement, she demanded that an explanation be sought from the presiding officers of stations nos.119 and 120 on the matter.

The senator also called for the Election Commission to take notice of the reports of PPP’s polling agent being removed from station no.158 in LA-15.

Rehman further demanded alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortage of polling staff and material, calling on the authorities to ensure that free and transparent elections were held at all polling stations without any disruption.

PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari also accused the PML-N of continuing rigging in the third phase of the elections. He highlighted that his party was regularly informing the Election Commission about the alleged rigging via phone.

But, “the chief election commissioner and the election commission secretary’s reply to all of our complaints has been that nothing has happened and everything is good,” he claimed.

When Dawn approached the Election Commission regarding Bokhari’s claim, Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel said any complaint that he or the chief election commissioner received was being attended and responded to, and the Quick Response Force (QRF) was also moved over it.

‘AJK’s people have supported PML-N’

Responding to PPP’s allegations, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said the rival party had not provided any proof for its claims.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad flanked by Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, Sanaullah denied that a comparatively high turnout could be considered proof of rigging.

The PML-N leader explained that a strong family and tribe system in AJK prompted people to show up for their relatives.

“Our opposing candidate Chaudhry Yasin was complaining yesterday that in his opposing candidate’s union council (UC), 80pc votes were cast, whereas in his own UC, 96pc votes were cast,” Sanaullah claimed.

Sanaullah asserted that balloting had gone fairly smoothly in Bagh and Haveli today.

He, however, detailed a few reported incidents. In Haveli, people tried to snatch documents from the polling agents in one station, but the Quick Response Force (QRF) promptly responded and resolved the situation without incident, according to Sanaullah.

In Bagh, some people, whom Sanaullah claimed were PPP workers, tried to halt polling at three stations. QRF responded there as well and resumed polling, the minister added.

Meanwhile, Muqam urged PPP to review the number of people attending their rallies instead of accusing others of rigging, insisting that PPP lacked support from the people of AJK.

“AJK’s people have supported PML-N,” Muqam asserted.

Disputing PPP’s recent stance that it was against phased elections, Muqam said the party had mentioned no reservations when the election schedule was first announced.

Sanaullah also backed Muqam, saying that PPP had not raised concerns when the Election Commission had originally sought consent from all parties for phased elections.

He further claimed that upon PPP’s insistence, the electoral watchdog had scheduled voting on the 12 refugee seats in the second phase of the elections.

Sanaullah contended that PPP did not want election results from the refugee seats in the rest of Pakistan to impact its numbers in AJK polls since PPP had not even canvassed in those places.

Speaking about the recent unrest in the region, Sanaullah expressed hope that the protests would end once the third phase of elections concludes, as protesters had “only aimed to stop elections”.

The new AJK government, which he said PML-N would form with a two-thirds majority, will respond to the protesters’ “valid demands”, the PML-N leader added.

However, he also warned that those who “took up arms and instigated the people of AJK, while acting on the directions of the enemy… will have to face the law and answer for their crimes”.

In response to a reporter’s question about PPP’s claim that PML-N only had numbered days of rule in the Centre, Sanaullah expressed hope that after the AJK elections, PPP would “open-heartedly” congratulate PML-N.

Meanwhile, PML-N’s AJK chapter secretary general Tariq Farooq — who also emerged as the winner in LA-7 recently — said allegations of “rigging, violence, coercion, or fake voting” emerging from the constituency of Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore were a “serious question of constitutional governance”.

“This is no longer merely an electoral dispute. It becomes a serious question of constitutional governance, democratic values, and the sanctity of the people’s vote,” Farooq wrote on X.

“I find it difficult to believe that the prime minister of Azad Jammu & Kashmir could consider himself above the Constitution, the law, and basic ethical obligations merely to secure his own election,” he said, without providing further details.

The PML-N candidate asserted that “public mandate must be secured through a free, fair and transparent election, not through power, influence or state authority”.

Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test

In Monday’s polls, AJK PM Rathore, who is from the PPP, and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls.

Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine.

In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council.

Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals.

Aziz, whose father Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign.

Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans.

Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister.

The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties.

In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), ex-PM Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist.

Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.”

Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan.

Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition.

In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively.

The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC).

Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following.

Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe.

Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position.

Additional reporting by Tariq Naqash

World.title: Iran says Pak-Saudi-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US
World.content:
Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday that the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “a sign of a change in the perception” of regional countries towards the United States.

The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

“This development is a sign of a change in the perception of the countries of the region,” ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said while responding to a query during a weekly press briefing on Monday.

“Considering the developments of the last two to three years, the countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false security brokers,” Iran’s state media quoted him as saying, referring to the United States.

Baqaei further said that there was “no reason to worry that this treaty will be against Iran”, highlighting Iran’s deep religious, historical and civilisational ties with Pakistan, Turkiye and even Saudi Arabia.

“This development is an important sign that the countries of the region have concluded that they cannot rely on and trust the claim of security provided by the United States and some other actors outside the region, and they are attempting to try another method; by relying on their own capabilities and perspectives,” IRNA quoted Baqaei as saying.

“Any plan that is based on the geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly identifies the enemy and the threat, has a chance of helping to strengthen security and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy and its allies,” he added, referring to Israel.

In response to a question about Iran’s willingness to possibly join the joint pact, Baqaei said Iran has always “emphasised pursuing security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries” and “free from the influence and destructive intervention” of foreign actors.

“Those plans still exist and can certainly be updated in light of developments,” the spokesperson added.

“We are in close contact with neighbouring countries and regional countries, and we hope that all countries will learn from the developments of the last two or three years and adopt the best path to strengthen the region’s collective security,” he said, according to IRNA.

Asked about Pakistan’s invitations to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to visit Pakistan, Baqaei said, “This visit will take place whenever the time is right. Bilateral relations are mainly considered.”

He added: “The relationship between Iran and Pakistan is a very important one. In the last seven or eight months, it has become even more important than before, for various reasons.”

On Sunday, Deputy Prime Minister and FM Ishaq Dar said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact.

Dar said the pact was the “culmination of years of discussions and coordination”, adding that it was “purely defensive” in nature.

“It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.”

The deputy PM clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations.

Dar speaks with Kuwait FM, others on pact

Separately, DPM Dar received a phone call from Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, wherein the latter felicitated the former on the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday.

According to the FO, the two dignitaries spoke late on Sunday and also “exchanged views on the regional situation, including occupied East Jerusalem”.

They also discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and “matters of mutual interest, including the follow-up to FM Jarrah’s recent visit to Pakistan and further enhancing cooperation and investment in key sectors”.

“The two sides agreed to remain closely engaged,” the FO added.

The deputy premier also shared the contours of the pact with Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi and former Guinea-Bissau president General Umaro Sissoco Embaló.

In a joint call with them late last night, Dar shared the agreement’s “significance for strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace, stability and security”, FO said.

Dar and Tshisekedi also exchanged views on Pakistan-DRC relations and agreed on the importance of further strengthening bilateral cooperation, including through high-level exchanges.

DPM Dar had also spoken to Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand a day ago.

“The two exchanged views on the regional situation, including the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye,” the FO said.

It added that Dar shared the “essence of the agreement” and the “joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

World.title: In letter to PM, Achakzai urges 'immediate' appointment of new chief election commissioner
World.content:
In a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday urged the appointment of a new chief election commissioner of the Election Commission of Pakistan, as well as two members representing Sindh and Balochistan.

In the letter, dated August 10 and available with Dawn, Achakzai, who heads the Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) and is chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party, drew the prime minister’s attention to a “critical constitutional duty” and stated that the statutory tenure of the CEC and the members representing Sindh and Balochistan had ended on January 26, 2025.

To that effect, he urged the “immediate filling” of the offices, terming it “essential for maintaining the operational continuity, independence, and credibility of the commission”.

In his letter, Achakzai cited two provisions of the Constitution, including Article 213(2A), which he said “mandates that the prime minister shall, in consultation with the leader of the opposition in the NA, forward three names for the appointment of the CEC to a Parliamentary Committee for hearing and confirmation”.

Article 218(2)(b), meanwhile, required that the “appointment of the members of the ECP from each province shall follow the exact same procedural requirement of consultation between the prime minister and the leader of the opposition under Article 213”.

Achakzai also drew attention to the matter at a meeting of the TTAP on Monday and informed the participants about the letter, according to a post on TTAP’s X account.

“The meeting expressed astonishment and concern over the fact that the current CEC and members continue to serve even after the expiry of their constitutional terms, and that the prime minister has not yet initiated the constitutional process for appointing new members.”

The meeting termed the establishment of an “impartial and independent EC essential for fair, transparent, and free elections”.

“Therefore, the prime minister should immediately meet with the opposition leader in this regard and initiate this important constitutional process without delay,” it added.

The incumbent CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja, along with Sindh and Balochistan ECP members, have now been in office for over a year after the expiry of their constitutionally mandated five-year terms.

The terms of the three officials ended on Jan 26, 2025. Under Article 215(4) of the Constitution, appointments to these posts were required within 45 days after the positions became vacant , i.e., by March 12, 2025.

However, a proviso inserted into Article 215(1) through the 26th Constitutional Amendment allows the CEC and members to continue until their successors are appointed. The incumbent CEC and two ECP members are serving under this provision.

At the time, the delay was partly attributed to the absence of an officially notified leader of the opposition in the NA.

It should also be mentioned that on July 30, the ECP had refused to recognise Achakzai as chairman of the PkMAP over the party’s failure to hold intra-party elections.

World.title: Three football confederations rebuke Infantino, say sport ‘belongs to no individual’
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino came under renewed fire on Monday as a joint letter from three confederations — European football’s governing body UEFA, Confederations of North America, Central America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF) and Asia (AFC) — declared football “belongs to no individual”.

Infantino has been the butt of scathing criticism ever since launching, and then withdrawing within days, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups.

FIFA had hit back on Saturday at “a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine” football’s governing body and Infantino.

However, Monday’s letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC showed his critics are unbowed.

“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote.

“When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the confederations added.

The three confederations had been vociferous in their condemnation of Infantino’s plan and had not let up after it was shelved.

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will seek a fourth and final term at the FIFA presidential election in Rabat next March.

Candidates have to be declared by November 18.

UEFA’s threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead — in theory depriving the competition of teams including reigning men’s champions Spain and 2026 semi-finalists France and England — proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his plan.

Prior to this debacle, Infantino had looked likely to be unopposed, after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL are largely supportive.

The confederations do not vote as blocs and there have been some supportive voices for Infantino from CONCACAF, Mexico and two AFC members — Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house.

Although the proposal has been dead in the water for over a week now — UEFA had termed it “a shabby, opaque, backroom deal” — the confederations harangued him for a lack of judgment.

“FIFA’s recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process,” they said.

“It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment.”

Although Infantino had received the “full support” of senior FIFA directors last week in an emergency meeting he called in Morocco, the confederations said it was meaningless.

“This recent meeting, where a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee — not the full Committee — were summoned abroad, rather than leadership going to Zurich to address the heart of FIFA, its staff, only reinforces these concerns and represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment,” they said.

“It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.”

Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of a hugely successful World Cup — the largest ever involving 48 teams.

However, the confederations made clear in the letter that it was not just Infantino who had made this possible.

“The growth over the past decade has been real,” they said.

“But that progress was never the work of one individual.

“It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game.

“The expanded tournaments, the awarding of the 2030 and 2034 FIFA World Cups, the distribution of resources to associations. These were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together.”

The confederations signed off their letter by claiming that under Infantino’s leadership “there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness”.

They added: “That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve. Football’s strength has always been its unity.”

World.title: Security forces kill 5 terrorists in intelligence-based operation in Balochistan's Panjgur
World.content:
Security forces have killed five terrorists, including a key commander, in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Sarkini and Chedgi areas of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Radio Pakistan reported on Monday.

The operation was conducted as part of Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3 in Balochistan, the state broadcaster said.

“According to security sources, the security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation against Fitna al Hindustan terrorists in Sarkani and Chedgi areas of Panjgur, killing five terrorists, including a key Fitna al Hindustan commander, Wazir,” it said.

Fitna al-Hindustan is a term used by the Pakistani military for India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation in Pakistan.

“Four motorcycles, machine guns, heavy weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the slain terrorists,” Radio Pakistan reported.

The terrorists were allegedly involved in robbery, extortion, kidnapping and attacks targeting local traders and other residents in Panjgur, it added.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi lauded security forces on the successful operation, according to state-run APP. Paying tribute to the professionalism and operational capabilities of the security forces, Naqvi said the successful action had thwarted the nefarious designs of the terrorists and dealt a major blow to their activities in the region.

Naqvi said the successful operation demonstrated the security forces’ preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment to combating terrorism. He stressed that the elimination of terrorist elements was essential for restoring lasting peace and stability in Balochistan and across the country.

He said the government and the people remained committed to supporting the security forces in their efforts to eradicate terrorist networks and ensure peace and security throughout the country.

The operation comes a day after security forces killed 15 terrorists in multiple intelligence-based operations across Balochistan. The operations were conducted in Mastung, Bolan, Washuk, Awaran, Sibi, Khuzdar, Harnai and Nushki under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna-3, according to state media.

The latest operations by the security forces in Balochistan take place as the province continues to face security challenges.

According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month.

The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said.

Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province.

World.title: Delay in judicial appointments: IHC tells govt to explain consequences of keeping PM's advice pending
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday issued a ruling on a public interest petition challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s delay in approving judicial appointments, directing the government to explain the constitutional consequences of keeping the premier’s advice pending for an indefinite period.

Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir, who had reserved the order on the maintainability of the petition on August 6, issued notices to the president, the federation of Pakistan and the attorney general. He directed them to file separate concise reports explaining the timeline and status of the summary forwarded by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for judicial appointments.

The petition was filed by advocate Luqman Zafar through his counsel Zahid Asif Chaudhry amid a presidential delay in approving the judicial appointments recommended by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP).

The JCP, headed by Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, recommended the appointment of 19 additional judges and the confirmation of five judges to high courts during meetings on July 20 and 21. The summary was subsequently forwarded by PM Shehbaz to President Zardari for assent under Article 48 of the Constitution. However, the president has yet to assent to the summary.

Last week, the IHC had reserved its verdict on the maintainability of the plea.

During Monday’s hearing, the petitioner’s counsel contended that Article 48(1) of the Constitution employed the expression “shall,” which cast a constitutional obligation upon the president to act on the advice of the prime minister.

The proviso to Article 48(1) allows the advice to be returned for reconsideration “within 15 days,” after which the president must act within ten days on the advice tendered after reconsideration.

The counsel relied on precedent to argue that the president was bound to act on the advice of the prime minister and could not convert the constitutional process into a power of indefinite deferral or veto.
